items.x: Terbinafine inhibits squalene epoxidase, causing toxic squalene to build up; monitor for hepatotoxicity.
items.a: Squalene epoxidase
w: 14-alpha-demethylase
Beta-1,3-glucan synthase
Thymidylate synthase

items.q: A 35-year-old man with cryptococcal meningitis receives amphotericin B with a second agent. He later develops pancytopenia. The second agent is converted within fungi by which enzyme?
items.x: Flucytosine is converted to 5-fluorouracil by fungal cytosine deaminase, inhibiting DNA and RNA synthesis; bone marrow suppression occurs.
items.a: Cytosine deaminase
w: Thymidine kinase
Hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase
Squalene epoxidase

items.q: A 55-year-old man with leukemia and invasive aspergillosis starts voriconazole. Two days later he reports altered color perception and blurry vision. Which statement about this effect is most accurate?
items.x: Transient visual disturbances are common with voriconazole; photosensitivity and hepatotoxicity also occur.
items.a: It is a common and usually transient effect
w: It signals irreversible retinal damage
It reflects optic neuritis from the drug
It indicates fungal spread to the eye

items.q: A 66-year-old woman receiving unfractionated heparin after knee replacement has a platelet count that falls from 250,000 to 90,000 on day 7, with a new leg DVT. What is the most appropriate anticoagulant?
items.x: HIT is caused by antibodies to heparin-platelet factor 4; stop all heparins and use a direct thrombin inhibitor such as argatroban.
items.a: Argatroban
w: Enoxaparin
Warfarin alone
Protamine sulfate

items.q: A 55-year-old man develops bleeding after receiving too much unfractionated heparin during cardiac catheterization. Which antidote is most appropriate, and how does it act?
items.x: Protamine is positively charged and binds negatively charged heparin, neutralizing it.
items.a: Protamine, a basic protein binding heparin
w: Vitamin K, restoring clotting factor synthesis
Idarucizumab, an antibody binding heparin
Andexanet, a decoy factor Xa protein

items.q: A 70-year-old man on warfarin has an INR of 9.5 and active GI bleeding. Which treatment provides the fastest reversal?
items.x: Four-factor PCC replaces factors II, VII, IX and X immediately; IV vitamin K is also given for sustained reversal.
items.a: Four-factor prothrombin complex concentrate
w: Fresh frozen plasma given intravenously
Vitamin K given by slow intravenous infusion
Protamine sulfate given intravenously

items.q: A 76-year-old woman taking dabigatran for atrial fibrillation has a subdural hematoma needing emergency surgery. Which agent specifically reverses this drug?
items.x: Idarucizumab is a monoclonal antibody fragment that binds dabigatran, a direct thrombin inhibitor.
items.a: Idarucizumab
w: Protamine sulfate
Andexanet alfa
Phytonadione

items.q: A 58-year-old man has a stent thrombosis despite taking clopidogrel. Genetic testing shows he is a CYP2C19 poor metabolizer. Why did the drug fail?
items.x: Clopidogrel is a prodrug activated by CYP2C19 to irreversibly block the P2Y12 ADP receptor; ticagrelor does not need activation.
items.a: It is a prodrug needing CYP2C19 activation
w: It is inactivated faster by CYP2C19
CYP2C19 metabolism creates an antagonist
It requires CYP2C19 for intestinal uptake

items.q: A 62-year-old man takes low-dose aspirin daily to prevent heart attacks. Why does a single dose inhibit platelet function for the life of the platelet?
items.x: Platelets lack a nucleus and cannot make new COX-1, so irreversible acetylation lasts 7 to 10 days.
items.a: It irreversibly acetylates platelet COX-1
w: It irreversibly blocks platelet P2Y12 receptors
It reversibly inhibits thromboxane synthase
It irreversibly blocks glycoprotein IIb/IIIa

items.q: A 68-year-old woman with an acute ischemic stroke arrives 2 hours after symptom onset and receives alteplase. Which mechanism and major risk does this drug have?
items.x: Tissue plasminogen activators convert plasminogen to plasmin to lyse fibrin; intracranial bleeding is the major risk.
items.a: Converts plasminogen to plasmin; hemorrhage
w: Inhibits thrombin directly; thrombocytopenia
Blocks factor Xa; hyperkalemia
Blocks glycoprotein IIb/IIIa; hypotension

items.q: A drug is given by continuous IV infusion. It has first-order elimination and a half-life of 6 hours. How long will it take to reach approximately 94 percent of steady-state concentration?
items.x: Time to steady state depends only on half-life: about 50, 75, 88 and 94 percent are reached after 1, 2, 3 and 4 half-lives.
items.a: 24 hours
w: 12 hours
36 hours
48 hours

items.q: A drug has a volume of distribution of 40 L and bioavailability of 1. The target plasma concentration is 10 mg/L. What loading dose is needed?
items.x: Loading dose equals target concentration times volume of distribution divided by bioavailability: 10 times 40 = 400 mg.
items.a: 400 mg
w: 40 mg
4 mg

items.q: A drug has a clearance of 5 L/h and an oral bioavailability of 0.5. The target steady-state concentration is 2 mg/L, given every 12 hours. What maintenance dose is needed?
items.x: Maintenance dose equals Css times CL times dosing interval divided by F: 2 times 5 times 12 divided by 0.5 = 240 mg.
items.a: 240 mg
w: 120 mg
60 mg
480 mg

items.q: A drug has a volume of distribution of 70 L and a clearance of 7 L/h. What is its approximate elimination half-life?
items.x: Half-life equals 0.7 times Vd divided by CL: 0.7 times 70 divided by 7 = 7 hours.
items.a: 7 hours
w: 10 hours
0.7 hours
49 hours

items.q: A 500 mg IV dose of a drug produces an initial plasma concentration of 2 mg/L. Which statement best describes this drug?
items.x: Vd equals dose divided by concentration (250 L), far above total body water, so the drug is sequestered in tissues.
items.a: It distributes extensively into tissues
w: It is confined mostly to the plasma
It distributes mainly in extracellular fluid
It is highly bound to plasma proteins

items.q: In a phase 1 study, a drug has an ED50 of 10 mg and a TD50 of 200 mg. What is its therapeutic index?
items.x: Therapeutic index equals TD50 divided by ED50; a higher value means a safer drug.

items.q: In an isolated tissue experiment, adding a fixed concentration of an antagonist shifts the agonist dose-response curve to the right, but the maximal response is still reached at high agonist doses. What type of antagonist is this?
items.x: A competitive (surmountable) antagonist raises EC50 without lowering Emax; potency falls but efficacy does not.
items.a: Competitive antagonist
w: Noncompetitive antagonist
Partial agonist
Irreversible antagonist

items.q: Two opioids are compared. Drug A produces a maximal analgesic effect of 100 percent at 10 mg. Drug B produces a maximal effect of 60 percent at 1 mg. Which statement is correct?
items.x: Efficacy is the maximal effect (Emax); potency relates to the dose needed (EC50). Drug A is more efficacious, and Drug B is more potent.
items.a: Drug A has greater efficacy
w: Drug B has greater efficacy
Drug A has greater potency
The two drugs have equal efficacy

items.q: A 34-year-old man with HSV encephalitis receives high-dose IV acyclovir as a rapid infusion. On day 3 his creatinine rises from 0.9 to 2.4 mg/dL and urine microscopy shows needle-shaped crystals. What is the mechanism of his kidney injury?
items.x: Acyclovir is poorly soluble in urine and can crystallize in tubules, causing obstructive nephropathy; IV hydration and slower infusion prevent it.
items.a: Drug precipitation within the renal tubules
w: Immune-mediated acute interstitial nephritis
Direct toxicity to glomerular podocytes
Afferent arteriolar constriction from loss of prostaglandins

items.q: A 38-year-old man with AIDS has HSV lesions that progress despite acyclovir, and the isolate lacks thymidine kinase activity. He is switched to a drug that does not need viral phosphorylation. Which laboratory abnormalities should be monitored most closely?
items.x: Foscarnet is a pyrophosphate analog that binds viral DNA polymerase directly; it chelates divalent cations (risk of seizures) and is nephrotoxic.
items.a: Hypocalcemia and hypomagnesemia
w: Hyperkalemia and hyperphosphatemia
Hypernatremia and hypochloremia
Hypercalcemia and metabolic alkalosis

items.q: A 52-year-old kidney transplant recipient develops CMV colitis and is treated with IV ganciclovir. Two weeks later his absolute neutrophil count is 600/uL. Which statement best explains the drug's activation and main toxicity?
items.x: Ganciclovir is monophosphorylated by the CMV UL97 kinase and then inhibits viral DNA polymerase; myelosuppression is its dose-limiting toxicity.
items.a: Activated by viral UL97 kinase; suppresses bone marrow
w: Pyrophosphate analog; chelates calcium and magnesium
Activated by host thymidine kinase; causes nephrolithiasis
Blocks viral uncoating; directly destroys neutrophils

items.q: A 70-year-old woman develops fever, myalgia and cough during a winter outbreak, and a rapid test is positive for influenza A. She starts an oral drug within 48 hours of symptom onset. Which viral step does it inhibit?
items.x: Oseltamivir inhibits neuraminidase, so progeny virions cannot cleave sialic acid and be released; baloxavir inhibits the cap-dependent endonuclease.
items.a: Release of new virions from infected cells
w: Fusion of the viral envelope with the endosome
Uncoating of the virus through the M2 channel
Cap-snatching by the polymerase acidic endonuclease

items.q: A 29-year-old woman with HIV takes a regimen that includes zidovudine. Routine labs show hemoglobin of 8.9 g/dL with an MCV of 112 fL. Which mechanism underlies the antiviral effect of this drug?
items.x: NRTIs such as zidovudine are phosphorylated by host kinases and lack a 3' hydroxyl, terminating DNA chains; zidovudine causes macrocytic anemia and marrow suppression.
items.a: Chain termination of viral DNA after phosphorylation
w: Allosteric inhibition of reverse transcriptase without activation
Blockade of strand transfer by the viral integrase
Inhibition of the protease that cleaves the gag-pol protein

items.q: A 26-year-old man starting HIV therapy has vivid dreams, insomnia and dizziness in the first weeks. The responsible drug binds reverse transcriptase at a pocket distant from the active site. How does it differ from nucleoside analogs?
items.x: NNRTIs such as efavirenz bind an allosteric site and need no phosphorylation; CNS effects are characteristic.
items.a: It does not require intracellular phosphorylation
w: It requires activation by a viral thymidine kinase
It competes with natural nucleotides at the catalytic site
It acts only after viral DNA has integrated into the host genome

items.q: A 33-year-old woman with well-controlled HIV takes dolutegravir. Her viral load rises after she begins taking an aluminum-magnesium antacid at the same time as her morning pills. What explains the treatment failure?
items.x: Integrase inhibitors bind metal ions in the integrase active site and also chelate Mg, Al, Ca and Fe in the gut; doses must be separated.
items.a: Chelation by polyvalent cations lowering absorption
w: Induction of hepatic CYP3A4 increasing drug clearance
Higher gastric pH preventing tablet dissolution
Competition for renal tubular secretion of the drug

items.q: A 36-year-old man's HIV regimen includes darunavir with a low dose of ritonavir. The ritonavir dose is too low to have meaningful antiviral activity on its own. What is its purpose?
items.x: Low-dose ritonavir strongly inhibits CYP3A4, boosting levels of other protease inhibitors; this causes many drug interactions.
items.a: Inhibition of CYP3A4 to raise darunavir levels
w: Induction of P-glycoprotein to improve CNS penetration
Inhibition of renal secretion to prolong darunavir action
Blockade of a second binding site on HIV protease

items.q: Before starting a new HIV regimen, a 30-year-old man is tested for HLA-B*57:01 and the result is positive. Which drug must be avoided because of the risk of a severe hypersensitivity reaction?
items.x: Abacavir hypersensitivity (fever, rash, GI and respiratory symptoms) is strongly linked to HLA-B*57:01, and rechallenge can be fatal.
items.a: Abacavir
w: Lamivudine
Tenofovir
Raltegravir

items.q: A 45-year-old treatment-experienced man with HIV has a tropism assay showing only CCR5-using virus. He starts a drug that blocks viral entry by binding a host cell protein. What is the drug's target?
items.x: Maraviroc binds host CCR5 and prevents its interaction with gp120; enfuvirtide binds gp41 and blocks membrane fusion.
items.a: Host CCR5 chemokine coreceptor
w: Viral gp41 transmembrane protein
Host CD4 receptor on helper T cells
Viral gp120 envelope glycoprotein

items.q: A 50-year-old man with chronic hepatitis C genotype 1 is cured after 12 weeks of an oral combination that contains sofosbuvir. Which viral protein does sofosbuvir inhibit?
items.x: Sofosbuvir is a nucleotide analog inhibitor of NS5B; drugs ending in -previr inhibit NS3/4A and those ending in -asvir inhibit NS5A.
items.a: NS5B RNA-dependent RNA polymerase
w: NS3/4A serine protease complex
NS5A replication complex protein
E2 envelope glycoprotein receptor

items.q: A 24-year-old soldier returning from Southeast Asia is treated for Plasmodium vivax malaria. Before a second drug is added to prevent relapse, his G6PD activity is measured. What does that second drug target, and what is the risk?
items.x: Primaquine eradicates dormant liver hypnozoites of P. vivax and P. ovale but causes oxidative hemolysis in G6PD deficiency.
items.a: Liver hypnozoites; hemolysis
w: Blood schizonts; retinopathy
Gametocytes; QT prolongation
Liver hypnozoites; agranulocytosis

items.q: A 35-year-old woman with systemic lupus erythematosus has taken hydroxychloroquine for 6 years. Which screening test should she have regularly because of this drug?
items.x: Hydroxychloroquine can cause irreversible bull's-eye maculopathy, so annual retinal screening is recommended after 5 years of use.
items.a: Retinal examination
w: Pulmonary function tests
Audiometry
Bone density scan

items.q: A 6-year-old girl has perianal itching at night, and a tape test shows Enterobius eggs. She receives a single oral dose that is repeated in 2 weeks. What is the mechanism of this drug?
items.x: Mebendazole binds parasite beta-tubulin and blocks microtubule formation, impairing glucose uptake; pyrantel is a depolarizing nicotinic agonist.
items.a: Inhibits parasite microtubule polymerization
w: Opens glutamate-gated chloride channels
Increases tegument calcium permeability
Depolarizing nicotinic receptor agonism

items.q: A 40-year-old man from Sierra Leone has itchy skin nodules and microfilariae in skin snips, consistent with onchocerciasis. Which drug and mechanism are most appropriate?
items.x: Ivermectin activates invertebrate glutamate-gated chloride channels, causing hyperpolarization and paralysis of microfilariae.
items.a: Ivermectin; opens glutamate-gated chloride channels
w: Praziquantel; raises tegument calcium permeability
Mebendazole; blocks beta-tubulin polymerization
Pyrantel; causes spastic paralysis via nicotinic agonism

items.q: A 30-year-old woman returns from Nigeria with fever and uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria and receives artemether-lumefantrine. How does the artemisinin component kill the parasite?
items.x: Heme iron cleaves the endoperoxide bridge of artemisinins, producing free radicals that damage parasite proteins.
items.a: Endoperoxide-derived free radicals
w: Inhibition of dihydrofolate reductase
Blockade of mitochondrial cytochrome b
Prevention of heme polymerization to hemozoin

items.q: A 9-year-old boy has tinea capitis and starts oral griseofulvin, which his mother is told to give with a fatty meal. Which mechanism and drug interaction are characteristic of this drug?
items.x: Griseofulvin deposits in keratin and disrupts the mitotic spindle; it induces CYP450, lowering warfarin and oral contraceptive levels, and is teratogenic.
items.a: Disrupts microtubules; induces CYP450
w: Inhibits ergosterol synthesis; inhibits CYP3A4
Binds ergosterol; causes potassium wasting
Inhibits squalene epoxidase; induces CYP2D6

items.q: A 28-year-old woman from rural Mexico has new-onset seizures, and MRI shows multiple cystic brain lesions containing scolices. In addition to corticosteroids, which drug is given?
items.x: Neurocysticercosis is treated with albendazole (sometimes with praziquantel), with steroids to limit inflammation as cysts die.
items.a: Albendazole
w: Ivermectin
Pyrantel pamoate
Nitazoxanide

items.q: A 19-year-old student with pharyngitis, posterior cervical lymphadenopathy and splenomegaly is given ampicillin. Three days later she develops a diffuse maculopapular rash. What is the most likely explanation?
items.x: Aminopenicillins given during infectious mononucleosis commonly cause a nonallergic morbilliform rash that does not predict true penicillin allergy.
items.a: Nonallergic rash associated with EBV infection
w: IgE-mediated type I penicillin hypersensitivity
Toxin-mediated scarlet fever from group A streptococci
Serum sickness from immune complex deposition

items.q: A 45-year-old woman with epilepsy controlled on valproic acid is treated with meropenem for a resistant gram-negative infection. Two days later she has a generalized seizure. What is the most likely cause?
items.x: Carbapenems block hydrolysis of valproate glucuronide, so valproate levels drop sharply within days; the combination should be avoided.
items.a: Carbapenem-induced fall in valproate levels
w: Direct carbapenem agonism at GABA-A receptors
Valproate inhibition of meropenem clearance
Hyponatremia from carbapenem-induced SIADH

items.q: A 78-year-old woman with chronic kidney disease receives full-dose cefepime for Pseudomonas pneumonia. Three days later she is confused with myoclonus, and EEG shows nonconvulsive status epilepticus. What best explains this toxicity?
items.x: Cefepime accumulates when renal dosing is not adjusted and antagonizes GABA-A receptors, causing encephalopathy and seizures.
items.a: Drug accumulation with central GABA-A antagonism
w: Thiamine depletion from altered gut flora
Hypoprothrombinemia from its N-methylthiotetrazole side chain
Disulfiram-like reaction to its side chain group

items.q: A 60-year-old man has pneumonia caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae that is resistant to levofloxacin. Which mechanism most likely produced this resistance?
items.x: Fluoroquinolone resistance arises mainly from chromosomal mutations in gyrA and parC, plus efflux pumps.
items.a: Mutations in DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV
w: Methylation of the 23S ribosomal RNA
Production of an extended-spectrum beta-lactamase
Altered penicillin-binding protein 2a

items.q: A 55-year-old man in the ICU has pneumonia caused by carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter and is treated with colistin. Which toxicity profile is most characteristic of this drug class?
items.x: Polymyxins act as cationic detergents on bacterial membranes and cause dose-related nephrotoxicity and neurotoxicity, including neuromuscular blockade.
items.a: Nephrotoxicity and neurotoxicity
w: Ototoxicity and red man syndrome
Hepatotoxicity and optic neuritis
Tendinopathy and QT prolongation

items.q: A 70-year-old woman has a second recurrence of Clostridioides difficile colitis. She is treated with a narrow-spectrum macrocyclic antibiotic that is minimally absorbed and spares normal colonic flora. What is its target?
items.x: Fidaxomicin inhibits bacterial RNA polymerase and has lower recurrence rates than vancomycin.
items.a: Bacterial RNA polymerase sigma subunit
w: Peptidyl transferase of the 50S ribosome
Cell wall D-Ala-D-Ala peptide terminus
Bacterial DNA gyrase A subunit

items.q: A 30-year-old man with neurosyphilis declines IV therapy and is treated with IM procaine penicillin G plus oral probenecid. How does probenecid improve therapy?
items.x: Probenecid blocks organic anion transporters in the proximal tubule, raising and prolonging penicillin levels.
items.a: Inhibits renal tubular secretion of penicillin
w: Inhibits bacterial beta-lactamase enzymes
Increases penicillin entry across the blood-brain barrier
Slows hepatic glucuronidation of penicillin

items.q: A 12-year-old boy with osteosarcoma receives high-dose methotrexate. Twenty-four hours later he is given a reduced folate that rescues normal cells without needing the enzyme that methotrexate blocks. Which enzyme does methotrexate inhibit?
items.x: Methotrexate inhibits DHFR; leucovorin (folinic acid) bypasses the block and rescues normal cells.
items.a: Dihydrofolate reductase
w: Thymidylate synthase
Ribonucleotide reductase
IMP dehydrogenase

items.q: A 60-year-old man with colon cancer receives fluorouracil with leucovorin. Here leucovorin is given to increase cytotoxicity rather than to rescue normal cells. What is the target of fluorouracil?
items.x: 5-FdUMP forms a covalent complex with thymidylate synthase and methylene-THF; leucovorin stabilizes this complex.
items.a: Thymidylate synthase
w: Dihydrofolate reductase
Topoisomerase I
Ribonucleotide reductase

items.q: A 42-year-old woman with lupus nephritis receives IV cyclophosphamide and is given mesna with each dose. Which toxicity is mesna preventing?
items.x: The metabolite acrolein injures bladder urothelium; mesna is a thiol that binds and inactivates acrolein in the urine.
items.a: Hemorrhagic cystitis from acrolein
w: Cardiomyopathy from free radicals
Pulmonary fibrosis from oxidative injury
Acute tubular necrosis from cast formation

items.q: A 58-year-old man receiving cisplatin for bladder cancer develops high-frequency hearing loss, a rising creatinine and hypomagnesemia. How does cisplatin kill tumor cells?
items.x: Cisplatin forms intrastrand and interstrand DNA crosslinks; it causes nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity and neuropathy, reduced by hydration and amifostine.
items.a: Crosslinks DNA by forming platinum adducts
w: Stabilizes microtubules and blocks mitotic exit
Inhibits topoisomerase II and causes DNA breaks
Intercalates in DNA and generates oxygen free radicals

items.q: A 50-year-old woman develops dyspnea, edema and an ejection fraction of 30 percent a year after breast cancer chemotherapy. Her cumulative dose of one agent exceeded recommended limits. Which drug could have been given with it to reduce this toxicity?
items.x: Doxorubicin causes cumulative dose-dependent dilated cardiomyopathy through free radicals; the iron chelator dexrazoxane is protective.
items.a: Dexrazoxane
w: Amifostine
Mesna
Leucovorin

items.q: A 28-year-old man treated for testicular cancer with a three-drug regimen develops progressive dyspnea and bibasilar crackles, with a restrictive pattern on pulmonary function testing. Which drug most likely caused this?
items.x: Bleomycin causes pulmonary fibrosis because the lung lacks bleomycin hydrolase; it acts by generating free radicals that break DNA.
items.a: Bleomycin
w: Etoposide
Cisplatin
Ifosfamide

items.q: A 6-year-old boy with acute lymphoblastic leukemia develops constipation, tingling in his hands and foot drop during induction chemotherapy. Which mechanism explains the responsible drug's activity?
items.x: Vincristine binds tubulin and blocks microtubule assembly, arresting cells in M phase; peripheral and autonomic neuropathy are dose-limiting.
items.a: Prevents tubulin polymerization into microtubules
w: Stabilizes microtubules and prevents disassembly
Depletes asparagine needed by leukemic cells
Inhibits topoisomerase II during the S and G2 phases

items.q: A 25-year-old man with testicular cancer receives a podophyllotoxin derivative. Years later he develops acute myeloid leukemia with an 11q23 rearrangement. What is this drug's mechanism?
items.x: Etoposide stabilizes the topoisomerase II-DNA complex, causing double-strand breaks; secondary leukemias with MLL rearrangement can follow.
items.a: Inhibition of topoisomerase II
w: Inhibition of topoisomerase I
Alkylation of guanine at N7
Inhibition of DNA polymerase alpha

items.q: A 48-year-old man with fatigue, splenomegaly and a WBC of 120,000/uL has a t(9;22) translocation. He starts an oral drug and achieves remission. What does the drug inhibit?
items.x: Imatinib blocks the ATP-binding site of the constitutively active BCR-ABL kinase in chronic myeloid leukemia.
items.a: BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase
w: JAK2 tyrosine kinase
EGFR tyrosine kinase
Bruton tyrosine kinase

items.q: A 47-year-old woman with HER2-positive breast cancer receives trastuzumab, and echocardiograms are scheduled every 3 months. Which statement best describes its cardiotoxicity compared with that of anthracyclines?
items.x: Trastuzumab cardiac dysfunction is usually reversible after stopping the drug and is not related to cumulative dose, unlike anthracycline cardiomyopathy.
items.a: Usually reversible and not dose-dependent
w: Irreversible and cumulative dose-dependent
Mainly a restrictive cardiomyopathy
Fully prevented by dexrazoxane pretreatment

items.q: A 52-year-old postmenopausal woman has taken tamoxifen for 3 years for estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer and now has vaginal bleeding. Which property of the drug explains this finding?
items.x: Tamoxifen is a SERM that blocks estrogen in breast tissue but acts as an agonist in the endometrium (hyperplasia, cancer) and raises VTE risk.
items.a: Partial estrogen agonism in the endometrium
w: Complete estrogen antagonism in the uterus
Inhibition of peripheral aromatase activity
Suppression of pituitary gonadotropin release

items.q: A 9-year-old boy on maintenance mercaptopurine for ALL is started on allopurinol for hyperuricemia without a dose change, and he develops severe pancytopenia. What explains this?
items.x: Xanthine oxidase inactivates mercaptopurine and azathioprine; with allopurinol or febuxostat their doses must be reduced by about 75 percent.
items.a: Xanthine oxidase inhibition raises drug levels
w: Allopurinol induces thiopurine methyltransferase
Allopurinol directly suppresses the bone marrow
Competition for renal secretion of the drug

items.q: A 62-year-old man treated for metastatic melanoma develops fatigue, weight gain and a TSH of 24 mU/L after 3 months of an intravenous antibody. Which target of this drug best explains the adverse effect?
items.x: PD-1 inhibitors release T-cell checkpoints and can cause immune-related thyroiditis, colitis, hepatitis and pneumonitis.
items.a: Programmed cell death protein 1
w: Vascular endothelial growth factor A
BRAF V600E serine-threonine kinase
Epidermal growth factor receptor

items.q: A 45-year-old kidney transplant recipient has gingival hyperplasia, hirsutism and hypertension, and his creatinine has risen slowly. By which mechanism does his immunosuppressant work?
items.x: Cyclosporine binds cyclophilin, and the complex inhibits calcineurin, preventing NFAT activation and IL-2 transcription.
items.a: Inhibits calcineurin and lowers IL-2 transcription
w: Inhibits mTOR and blocks IL-2 signal transduction
Inhibits inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase
Blocks the alpha chain of the IL-2 receptor on T cells

items.q: A 38-year-old liver transplant recipient taking tacrolimus develops new-onset diabetes and a fine tremor. To which intracellular protein does tacrolimus bind before inhibiting its target?
items.x: Tacrolimus binds FKBP12, and the complex inhibits calcineurin; it is more diabetogenic and neurotoxic than cyclosporine.
items.a: FK-binding protein 12
w: Cyclophilin A
Calmodulin
Glucocorticoid receptor

items.q: A 30-year-old woman with lupus nephritis is maintained on mycophenolate mofetil. Which enzyme does it inhibit, and why are lymphocytes most affected?
items.x: Mycophenolate inhibits IMP dehydrogenase in de novo guanine synthesis, which lymphocytes rely on because they lack a purine salvage pathway.
items.a: IMP dehydrogenase; lymphocytes lack a salvage pathway
w: Dihydrofolate reductase; lymphocytes divide fastest
Calcineurin; lymphocytes depend on IL-2 transcription
Xanthine oxidase; lymphocytes accumulate toxic purine bases

items.q: A 34-year-old man with Crohn disease is about to start azathioprine. Which test should be done first to estimate his risk of severe myelosuppression?
items.x: Low TPMT activity shunts azathioprine toward toxic thioguanine nucleotides and severe marrow suppression.
items.a: Thiopurine methyltransferase activity
w: Dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase activity
Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase level
HLA-B*58:01 genotyping

items.q: A 40-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis is about to start infliximab. Which test must be completed before the first dose?
items.x: TNF-alpha maintains granulomas, so TNF inhibitors can reactivate latent tuberculosis; screening is required first.
items.a: Interferon-gamma release assay for tuberculosis
w: Serum IgA level for anaphylaxis risk
Thiopurine methyltransferase genotype
Antinuclear antibody titer to predict drug-induced lupus

items.q: A 25-year-old woman with severe allergic asthma and a high serum IgE has exacerbations despite high-dose inhaled steroids and a LABA. She starts a monthly injection. What does the drug bind?
items.x: Omalizumab binds the Fc portion of free IgE, preventing it from binding FcER1 on mast cells and basophils.
items.a: Free IgE at its Fc region
w: Interleukin-5 cytokine
IL-4 receptor alpha subunit
Thymic stromal lymphopoietin

items.q: A 66-year-old man with type 2 diabetes and an eGFR of 25 mL/min has his metformin stopped. Which adverse effect is being avoided, and what is the drug's main action?
items.x: Metformin reduces hepatic glucose output (in part via AMPK); accumulation in renal failure can cause lactic acidosis, and it rarely causes hypoglycemia alone.
items.a: Lactic acidosis; decreased hepatic gluconeogenesis
w: Hypoglycemia; increased pancreatic insulin release
Lactic acidosis; increased insulin secretion
Pancreatitis; slower gastric emptying

items.q: A 78-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes and reduced kidney function is found confused with a glucose of 38 mg/dL. Her drug closes ATP-sensitive potassium channels on beta cells and has active metabolites cleared by the kidney. Which drug is she taking?
items.x: Sulfonylureas depolarize beta cells to release insulin; long-acting glyburide is especially likely to cause prolonged hypoglycemia in older adults with CKD.
items.a: Glyburide
w: Glipizide
Repaglinide
Nateglinide

items.q: A 64-year-old man with type 2 diabetes develops weight gain, ankle edema and worsening dyspnea after a new drug is added. The drug acts on a nuclear receptor that is highly expressed in adipose tissue. What is its mechanism?
items.x: Thiazolidinediones activate PPAR-gamma to improve insulin sensitivity but cause fluid retention and can worsen heart failure.
items.a: PPAR-gamma agonist
w: PPAR-alpha agonist
SGLT2 inhibitor
DPP-4 inhibitor

items.q: A 52-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes presents with nausea, a glucose of 190 mg/dL and an anion gap metabolic acidosis with positive serum ketones. Where does her diabetes drug act?
items.x: SGLT2 inhibitors cause glucosuria and can produce euglycemic DKA; they also increase the risk of genital mycotic infections.
items.a: Proximal tubule sodium-glucose cotransporter
w: Intestinal alpha-glucosidase in the brush border

items.q: A 65-year-old woman on a stable levothyroxine dose now has a TSH of 9.8 mU/L. Three months ago she began taking calcium carbonate and ferrous sulfate with her levothyroxine every morning. Which is the most appropriate step?
items.x: Calcium, iron, and PPIs reduce levothyroxine absorption; take levothyroxine on an empty stomach separated from these products.
items.a: Separate levothyroxine from calcium and iron by at least 4 hours
w: Increase the levothyroxine dose and keep the timing the same
Add liothyronine to the same morning regimen of medications
Take levothyroxine with breakfast and the two supplements

items.q: A 35-year-old woman with known Addison disease has vomiting and diarrhea. BP is 72/40 mm Hg, sodium 126 mEq/L, potassium 5.9 mEq/L, and glucose 58 mg/dL. Which is the most appropriate immediate therapy?
items.x: Adrenal crisis needs immediate high-dose IV hydrocortisone (which also provides mineralocorticoid activity) plus fluids and dextrose; never delay steroids for testing.
items.a: Hydrocortisone 100 mg IV plus normal saline with dextrose
w: Dexamethasone 1 mg orally with a morning cortisol level
Fludrocortisone 0.1 mg orally plus normal saline alone
Prednisone 5 mg orally plus normal saline with dextrose

items.q: A 40-year-old man is newly diagnosed with primary adrenal insufficiency. He has salt craving, hyperkalemia, and orthostatic hypotension. Which maintenance regimen is most appropriate?
items.x: Primary adrenal insufficiency lacks both cortisol and aldosterone, so glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid replacement are needed.
items.a: Hydrocortisone plus fludrocortisone
w: Hydrocortisone alone
Dexamethasone alone
Prednisone plus spironolactone

items.q: A 16-year-old girl has asthma symptoms twice a month with no nighttime awakenings and normal spirometry between episodes. Which reliever regimen is preferred by current GINA recommendations?
items.x: GINA Track 1 prefers as-needed low-dose ICS-formoterol for mild asthma because it reduces severe exacerbations compared with SABA-only therapy.
items.a: As-needed low-dose budesonide-formoterol
w: As-needed albuterol alone for symptom relief
Daily montelukast plus as-needed albuterol
Daily salmeterol alone with as-needed albuterol

items.q: A 28-year-old woman with asthma uses low-dose budesonide-formoterol as maintenance and reliever therapy. She still has symptoms most days and woke at night twice last week. Inhaler technique and adherence are good. Which is the most appropriate step?
items.x: Step up within the ICS-formoterol track to medium-dose maintenance-and-reliever therapy after confirming technique and adherence.
items.a: Increase to medium-dose budesonide-formoterol maintenance and reliever
w: Add salmeterol as a separate inhaler and keep the current dose
Add daily montelukast and stop the budesonide-formoterol inhaler
Add tiotropium now and keep the low-dose budesonide-formoterol

items.q: A 25-year-old woman with a severe asthma exacerbation has received three back-to-back albuterol-ipratropium nebulizers and IV methylprednisolone. She still speaks in words only, and peak flow is 30 percent of predicted. Which is the most appropriate next medication?
items.x: IV magnesium sulfate is recommended for severe exacerbations not responding to initial bronchodilators and steroids.
items.a: Intravenous magnesium sulfate
w: Intravenous aminophylline
Inhaled salmeterol
Oral montelukast

items.q: A 34-year-old man has severe allergic asthma with 3 prednisone bursts in the past year despite high-dose ICS-LABA and good technique. Total IgE is 420 IU/mL with sensitization to dust mite. Which add-on therapy is most appropriate?
items.x: Anti-IgE therapy is indicated for severe allergic asthma with elevated IgE uncontrolled on step 4 to 5 therapy.
items.a: Subcutaneous omalizumab
w: Daily oral theophylline
Daily oral montelukast
Daily oral prednisone

items.q: Montelukast is added for a boy with asthma and allergic rhinitis. Which receptor action produces its effect?
items.x: Montelukast is a competitive antagonist at the CysLT1 receptor, blocking the bronchoconstriction, mucus secretion and eosinophil recruitment driven by LTD4. Zileuton is the 5-lipoxygenase inhibitor and roflumilast the PDE4 inhibitor, so each acts at a different point.
items.a: Blockade of the cysteinyl leukotriene type 1 receptor
w: Inhibition of 5-lipoxygenase in the leukotriene pathway
Blockade of thromboxane A2 receptors on bronchial muscle
Inhibition of phosphodiesterase 4 inside airway cells

items.q: A 66-year-old man with COPD (FEV1 55 percent predicted) has an mMRC dyspnea score of 2 and no exacerbations in the past year. Blood eosinophils are 120/microL. Which is the most appropriate maintenance therapy?
items.x: GOLD recommends LABA plus LAMA for symptomatic patients (group B); ICS monotherapy is not recommended in COPD.
items.a: LAMA plus LABA such as tiotropium-olodaterol
w: ICS plus LABA such as fluticasone-salmeterol
ICS alone such as fluticasone twice daily
SABA alone such as albuterol when needed

items.q: A 70-year-old woman with COPD on LAMA plus LABA has had 2 exacerbations requiring prednisone in the past year. Blood eosinophils are 380/microL. Which is the most appropriate change?
items.x: GOLD recommends escalating to LABA, LAMA, and ICS for exacerbations when eosinophils are 100/microL or higher, with the strongest benefit at 300/microL or higher.
items.a: Add an inhaled corticosteroid to make triple therapy
w: Replace the LAMA with an inhaled corticosteroid alone
Add oral theophylline to the current two inhalers
Add daily oral prednisone to the current inhalers

items.q: A 68-year-old man with COPD has 3 days of worsening dyspnea, increased sputum volume, and green sputum. SpO2 is 91 percent and he is not in respiratory distress. In addition to bronchodilators and an antibiotic, which is the most appropriate therapy?
items.x: A short course of prednisone 40 mg daily for 5 days is as effective as longer courses for COPD exacerbations and has less toxicity.
items.a: Prednisone 40 mg daily for 5 days
w: Prednisone 60 mg daily tapered over 6 weeks
Prednisone 10 mg daily for 5 days
Inhaled fluticasone twice daily for 5 days

items.q: A 32-year-old man has 3 days of fever, productive cough, and right lower lobe consolidation. He has no comorbidities and has not taken antibiotics recently. Pulse is 96/min and SpO2 96 percent. Which is the most appropriate outpatient antibiotic?
items.x: ATS/IDSA recommends high-dose amoxicillin (or doxycycline or a macrolide where resistance is low) for healthy outpatients with CAP.
items.a: Amoxicillin 1 g three times daily
w: Ciprofloxacin 500 mg twice daily
Cephalexin 500 mg four times daily
Clindamycin 300 mg four times daily

items.q: A 64-year-old woman with COPD and type 2 diabetes has CAP. She is stable for outpatient treatment and has no recent antibiotic use. Which is the most appropriate regimen?
items.x: Outpatients with comorbidities receive a beta-lactam plus a macrolide or doxycycline, or monotherapy with a respiratory fluoroquinolone.
items.a: Amoxicillin-clavulanate plus azithromycin
w: Azithromycin alone
Amoxicillin-clavulanate alone
Cephalexin plus azithromycin

items.q: A 70-year-old man is admitted to a medical ward with CAP. He is not in the ICU, has no MRSA or Pseudomonas risk factors, and has no drug allergies. Which is the most appropriate empiric therapy?
items.x: Non-severe inpatient CAP is treated with a beta-lactam plus a macrolide, or a respiratory fluoroquinolone alone.
items.a: Ceftriaxone plus azithromycin
w: Vancomycin plus piperacillin-tazobactam
Ceftriaxone alone
Azithromycin alone

items.q: A 58-year-old man with prior MRSA pneumonia is admitted to the ICU with severe CAP requiring norepinephrine. Which is the most appropriate empiric regimen?
items.x: Severe CAP with prior respiratory MRSA isolation warrants empiric MRSA coverage with vancomycin or linezolid added to standard therapy.
items.a: Ceftriaxone, azithromycin, and vancomycin
w: Ceftriaxone and azithromycin only
Levofloxacin and azithromycin only
Ceftriaxone, azithromycin, and daptomycin

items.q: A 55-year-old woman with a history of anaphylaxis to penicillin is admitted to a medical ward with CAP. Which is the most appropriate empiric therapy?
items.x: A respiratory fluoroquinolone covers typical and atypical pathogens and avoids beta-lactams in severe penicillin allergy.
items.a: Levofloxacin monotherapy
w: Ceftriaxone plus azithromycin
Ampicillin-sulbactam plus azithromycin
Azithromycin monotherapy

items.q: A 26-year-old nonpregnant woman has 2 days of dysuria and frequency without fever or flank pain. Urinalysis shows pyuria and nitrites. Which is the most appropriate treatment?
items.x: IDSA first-line options for uncomplicated cystitis are nitrofurantoin for 5 days (Macrobid label: 7 days), TMP-SMX for 3 days (if resistance is low), or a single dose of fosfomycin.
items.a: Nitrofurantoin for 5 days
w: Ciprofloxacin for 7 days
Amoxicillin for 3 days
Nitrofurantoin for 1 day

items.q: A 30-year-old woman has a fever of 38.6 C (101.5 F), flank pain, and costovertebral tenderness. She is tolerating oral intake and is not pregnant. Local fluoroquinolone resistance is below 10 percent. Which is the most appropriate outpatient treatment?
items.x: Nitrofurantoin and fosfomycin do not achieve adequate renal tissue levels; oral fluoroquinolones for 7 days are first-line for pyelonephritis.
items.a: Ciprofloxacin for 7 days
w: Nitrofurantoin for 5 days
Fosfomycin as a single dose
Amoxicillin for 3 days

items.q: A 24-year-old woman at 26 weeks gestation has fever, rigors, and right flank pain. Urinalysis shows pyuria and bacteriuria. Which is the most appropriate management?
items.x: Pyelonephritis in pregnancy is treated as an inpatient with IV beta-lactam therapy; fluoroquinolones and tetracyclines are avoided.
items.a: Admit and give IV ceftriaxone
w: Outpatient oral nitrofurantoin
Outpatient oral cephalexin
Admit and give IV levofloxacin

items.q: A 25-year-old woman at 12 weeks gestation has a urine culture with more than 100,000 CFU/mL of E. coli. She has no symptoms. The organism is susceptible to all tested agents. Which is the most appropriate management?
items.x: Asymptomatic bacteriuria in pregnancy is treated to prevent pyelonephritis; beta-lactams are preferred in the first trimester.
items.a: Cephalexin for 5 to 7 days
w: No treatment because she is asymptomatic
Ciprofloxacin for 3 days
Doxycycline for 7 days

items.q: A 22-year-old college student has fever, headache, neck stiffness, and a petechial rash. CSF shows neutrophilic pleocytosis and low glucose. Which is the most appropriate empiric regimen?
items.x: Empiric adult bacterial meningitis coverage is vancomycin plus a third-generation cephalosporin, with dexamethasone given before or with the first dose.
items.a: Vancomycin plus ceftriaxone plus dexamethasone
w: Vancomycin plus ampicillin plus dexamethasone
Ceftriaxone plus ampicillin plus dexamethasone
Vancomycin plus gentamicin plus dexamethasone

items.q: A 68-year-old man has fever, confusion, and nuchal rigidity. CSF shows 1,800 WBC/mm3 with neutrophils and low glucose. Which is the most appropriate empiric antibiotic regimen?
items.x: Adults older than 50 need ampicillin added for Listeria monocytogenes coverage, along with dexamethasone.
items.a: Vancomycin, ceftriaxone, and ampicillin
w: Vancomycin and ceftriaxone only
Ceftriaxone and ampicillin only
Vancomycin and ampicillin only

items.q: A 35-year-old man with suspected pneumococcal meningitis is about to receive vancomycin and ceftriaxone. When should dexamethasone be given?
items.x: Dexamethasone reduces mortality and hearing loss in pneumococcal meningitis when given before or with the first antibiotic dose.
items.a: Shortly before or with the first antibiotic dose
w: Only after CSF culture confirms pneumococcus
24 hours after antibiotics have started
Only if the patient develops seizures

items.q: A 45-year-old man has a 2-day history of a spreading, warm, erythematous area on the lower leg without purulence or abscess. He is afebrile with normal vital signs. Which is the most appropriate antibiotic?
items.x: Nonpurulent cellulitis is usually streptococcal; oral beta-lactams such as cephalexin are first-line. TMP-SMX alone covers streptococci poorly.
items.a: Cephalexin
w: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole alone
Ciprofloxacin
Intravenous vancomycin

items.q: A 28-year-old man has a 4-cm fluctuant abscess on the thigh with surrounding erythema and a temperature of 38.3 C (100.9 F). Incision and drainage is performed. Which antibiotic is most appropriate?
items.x: Purulent infections with systemic signs warrant drainage plus MRSA coverage such as TMP-SMX or doxycycline.
items.a: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole
w: Penicillin V potassium
Amoxicillin-clavulanate
Cefuroxime axetil

items.q: A 52-year-old man with diabetes has rapidly spreading thigh erythema, severe pain out of proportion to exam, crepitus, and BP 84/50 mm Hg. Along with emergency surgical debridement, which regimen is most appropriate?
items.x: Necrotizing soft tissue infection requires broad coverage including MRSA and gram-negatives, plus clindamycin to suppress toxin production.
items.a: Vancomycin, piperacillin-tazobactam, and clindamycin
w: Vancomycin, piperacillin-tazobactam, and gentamicin
Cefazolin, metronidazole, and oral doxycycline
Vancomycin and ceftriaxone without clindamycin

items.q: A 50-year-old woman receiving IV vancomycin over 20 minutes develops flushing and an erythematous rash on the face, neck, and upper trunk. BP is 118/76 mm Hg and there is no wheezing or angioedema. Which is the most appropriate management?
items.x: Vancomycin infusion reaction is non-IgE histamine release from rapid infusion; infuse over at least 60 minutes and premedicate with an antihistamine.
items.a: Slow the infusion rate and give an antihistamine
w: Stop vancomycin permanently and record an allergy
Give intramuscular epinephrine immediately
Switch to cefazolin plus clindamycin indefinitely

items.q: A 63-year-old man has MRSA pneumonia confirmed by sputum culture. Which antibiotic should not be used for this infection?
items.x: Daptomycin is inactivated by pulmonary surfactant and is not used for pneumonia, although it is effective for MRSA bacteremia and endocarditis.
items.a: Daptomycin
w: Vancomycin
Linezolid
Ceftaroline

items.q: A 23-year-old man has urethral discharge and dysuria. NAAT is positive for Neisseria gonorrhoeae and negative for Chlamydia. Which is the most appropriate treatment?
items.x: CDC recommends a single 500-mg IM ceftriaxone dose for uncomplicated gonorrhea (1 g if 150 kg or more); add doxycycline only if chlamydia is not excluded.
items.a: Ceftriaxone 500 mg IM once
w: Azithromycin 1 g orally once
Ciprofloxacin 500 mg orally once
Cefixime 400 mg orally plus azithromycin

items.q: A 20-year-old nonpregnant woman has a positive NAAT for Chlamydia trachomatis on routine screening. Which is the most appropriate treatment?
items.x: CDC now prefers doxycycline for 7 days over single-dose azithromycin for chlamydia in nonpregnant patients.
items.a: Doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 7 days
w: Doxycycline 200 mg as a single oral dose
Ceftriaxone 500 mg IM as a single dose
Metronidazole 500 mg twice daily for 7 days

items.q: A 29-year-old woman has 6 weeks of depressed mood, anhedonia, early morning awakening, poor concentration, and excessive guilt. She has no suicidal ideation, no history of mania, and no medical illness. PHQ-9 score is 17 and she prefers medication. Which is the most appropriate initial pharmacotherapy?
items.x: An SSRI such as sertraline is first-line for moderate major depression because of efficacy, tolerability, and safety in overdose. TCAs are more toxic in overdose, and benzodiazepines do not treat depression.
items.a: Sertraline 50 mg daily
w: Amitriptyline 75 mg at bedtime
Phenelzine 15 mg twice daily
Buspirone 10 mg twice daily

items.q: A 44-year-old man with bipolar I disorder has been stable on lithium for 5 years. He now has coarse tremor, ataxia, vomiting, and confusion. Lithium level is 2.4 mEq/L (previously 0.8). Two weeks ago a new antihypertensive was started. Which medication most likely precipitated this?
items.x: Thiazides increase proximal tubular sodium and lithium reabsorption and can raise lithium levels 25 percent or more. ACE inhibitors, ARBs, and NSAIDs also raise levels; calcium channel blockers and alpha blockers do not meaningfully affect levels.
items.a: Hydrochlorothiazide
w: Amlodipine
Doxazosin
Metoprolol succinate extended-release

items.q: A man has been on clozapine for 5 weeks. Which laboratory result requires the drug to be interrupted under its REMS program?
items.x: Clozapine is interrupted when the ANC falls below 1,000 per microliter, and the ANC rather than the total WBC is the monitored value, weekly for the first 6 months. The eosinophil and platelet values shown here are not treatment-limiting.
items.a: Absolute neutrophil count of 900 per microliter
w: White blood cell count of 6,200 per microliter
Absolute eosinophil count of 720 cells per microliter
Platelet count of 141,000 per microliter

items.q: A man on IV haloperidol has fever, rigidity and a CK of 18,000 U/L. Which additional finding would instead point to serotonin syndrome?
items.x: Clonus and hyperreflexia are characteristic of serotonin syndrome and are absent in neuroleptic malignant syndrome, where rigidity is lead-pipe and reflexes are normal or reduced. Fever, diaphoresis and autonomic instability occur in both, so they do not separate them.
items.a: Inducible ankle clonus with brisk reflexes
w: Lead-pipe rigidity of the arms and legs
Diaphoresis with a labile blood pressure reading
A temperature above 40 C with confusion

items.q: A 40-year-old woman taking sertraline was started on tramadol for back pain. She now has agitation, a temperature of 39.0 C (102.2 F), diaphoresis, diarrhea, mydriasis, hyperreflexia, and inducible clonus most prominent in the legs. Both drugs are stopped and IV benzodiazepines are given, but symptoms persist. Which medication is indicated next?
items.x: Serotonin syndrome features clonus and hyperreflexia. After stopping serotonergic drugs and giving benzodiazepines, cyproheptadine, a 5-HT2A antagonist, is used. Bromocriptine worsens serotonin toxicity, and dantrolene is for NMS or malignant hyperthermia.
items.a: Cyproheptadine
w: Dantrolene
Bromocriptine
Physostigmine

items.q: A 34-year-old woman with schizophrenia well controlled on olanzapine 20 mg daily has gained 14 kg in 9 months. Fasting glucose is 118 mg/dL and triglycerides are 290 mg/dL. Which antipsychotic is the best alternative to minimize metabolic risk?
items.x: Aripiprazole, ziprasidone, and lurasidone have the lowest metabolic liability. Clozapine and olanzapine carry the highest risk, and quetiapine and low-potency typicals also cause substantial weight gain.
items.a: Aripiprazole
w: Risperidone
Quetiapine
Clozapine

items.q: A 22-year-old woman with bulimia nervosa (self-induced vomiting until 1 year ago) wants help quitting her 1-pack-per-day smoking habit. Which smoking cessation medication is contraindicated?
items.x: Bupropion lowers the seizure threshold and is contraindicated in seizure disorders and in bulimia or anorexia nervosa, in which electrolyte disturbances further increase seizure risk.
items.a: Bupropion sustained-release
w: Varenicline
Nicotine patch plus nicotine gum
Nicotine lozenge as needed

items.q: A 56-year-old man with decompensated alcoholic cirrhosis (ascites, INR 2.0, albumin 2.4 g/dL) is admitted. Thirty hours after his last drink he has tremor, diaphoresis, pulse 118/min, BP 162/96 mm Hg, and visual hallucinations. CIWA-Ar score is 22. Which is the most appropriate medication?
items.x: Benzodiazepines are first-line for alcohol withdrawal. In severe liver disease, agents metabolized only by glucuronidation without active metabolites (lorazepam, oxazepam) are preferred over long-acting chlordiazepoxide or diazepam.
items.a: Lorazepam
w: Chlordiazepoxide
Diazepam
Haloperidol

items.q: A 48-year-old man with alcohol use disorder has completed detoxification and wants medication to help maintain abstinence. He has decompensated cirrhosis with bilirubin 3.1 mg/dL and an elevated INR. Creatinine is 0.8 mg/dL. Which is the most appropriate medication?
items.x: Acamprosate is renally cleared without hepatic metabolism, making it suitable in advanced liver disease. Naltrexone is avoided in acute hepatitis or liver failure, and disulfiram is hepatotoxic.
items.a: Acamprosate
w: Naltrexone
Disulfiram
Chlordiazepoxide

items.q: A 4-year-old boy has had hyperactivity, impulsivity, and inattention at home and in preschool for 9 months, causing significant impairment. Hearing, vision, and development are otherwise normal. Which is the most appropriate first-line treatment?
items.x: For preschool children ages 4 to 5, the AAP recommends evidence-based parent training in behavior management first; methylphenidate may be considered if behavioral therapy is insufficient.
items.a: Parent training in behavior management
w: Methylphenidate at a low starting dose
Cognitive behavioral therapy for the child
Elimination diet without artificial dyes

items.q: A 17-year-old girl has morning myoclonic jerks and had one generalized tonic-clonic seizure after a sleepless night. EEG shows 4- to 6-Hz generalized polyspike-and-wave discharges. Which is the most appropriate initial medication?
items.x: Juvenile myoclonic epilepsy responds to broad-spectrum agents. Valproate is effective but is avoided in people who may become pregnant because of neural tube defects and lower offspring IQ. Carbamazepine and phenytoin can worsen myoclonic seizures.
items.a: Levetiracetam
w: Valproic acid
Carbamazepine
Phenytoin

items.q: A 61-year-old woman has taken haloperidol for 8 years for stable schizophrenia. She has developed involuntary lip smacking, tongue protrusion, and choreiform finger movements. Which medication is most appropriate to treat this movement disorder?
items.x: Tardive dyskinesia is treated with a VMAT2 inhibitor such as valbenazine or deutetrabenazine. Anticholinergics such as benztropine do not help and may worsen TD.
items.a: Valbenazine
w: Benztropine
Amantadine
Propranolol

items.q: A 32-year-old veteran has PTSD with intrusive memories, nightmares, hypervigilance, and avoidance. He is starting trauma-focused psychotherapy and asks about medication. Which medication should be avoided for PTSD?
items.x: Guidelines recommend against benzodiazepines in PTSD because they may worsen outcomes and impede extinction learning. Sertraline, paroxetine, and venlafaxine are recommended pharmacotherapies.
items.a: Alprazolam
w: Sertraline
Paroxetine
Venlafaxine extended-release

items.q: An 84-year-old man becomes acutely confused 2 days after hip fracture surgery. His attention fluctuates and is worse at night. He picks at the sheets but is not a danger to himself or staff. Infection and metabolic causes are being addressed. Which is the most appropriate initial management?
items.x: Delirium is managed by treating underlying causes and using multicomponent nonpharmacologic measures. Antipsychotics are reserved for severe distress or danger, and benzodiazepines and anticholinergics worsen delirium.
items.a: Reorientation, sleep promotion, mobilization, and family presence
w: Lorazepam at night, physical restraints, and a quiet dark room
Low-dose quetiapine, bed rest, and limited daytime visitors
Diphenhydramine at bedtime, bed alarm, and a urinary catheter

items.q: An older woman taking nightly diphenhydramine has urinary retention, constipation and worsening memory. Which receptor action explains these?
items.x: First-generation antihistamines are nonselective and block muscarinic receptors, producing retention, constipation, dry mouth and cognitive impairment, which is why they sit on the Beers list. H1 blockade in the brain explains the sedation but not the anticholinergic findings.
items.a: Antagonism at muscarinic acetylcholine receptors
w: Antagonism at central histamine H1 receptors
Antagonism at peripheral alpha-1 adrenergic receptors
Inverse agonism at central 5-HT2A receptors

items.q: An 82-year-old man with Alzheimer disease on donepezil has urge urinary incontinence. Oxybutynin was started 3 weeks ago and his confusion has worsened. Which is the best alternative for his bladder symptoms?
items.x: Antimuscarinics worsen cognition and oppose cholinesterase inhibitors. A beta-3 agonist such as mirabegron treats overactive bladder without anticholinergic effects.
items.a: Mirabegron
w: Tolterodine
Hyoscyamine
Imipramine

items.q: A 34-year-old man is having a generalized tonic-clonic seizure that began 12 minutes ago. He has received IV lorazepam 4 mg twice without cessation. Glucose is 104 mg/dL and the airway is supported. Which is the most appropriate next medication?
items.x: After benzodiazepines fail, a second-line IV agent is given: levetiracetam, fosphenytoin, or valproate, which had similar efficacy in ESETT. Further benzodiazepine doses add respiratory risk without benefit.
items.a: Intravenous levetiracetam 60 mg/kg
w: A third dose of IV lorazepam 4 mg
Intravenous propofol bolus and infusion
Oral phenytoin 1 g by nasogastric tube

items.q: A 7-year-old girl has many brief staring spells daily, lasting about 10 seconds with eyelid fluttering and no postictal confusion. Hyperventilation provokes an episode. EEG shows 3-Hz generalized spike-and-wave discharges. Which is the most appropriate initial medication?
items.x: Ethosuximide is first-line for childhood absence epilepsy, with better tolerability than valproate. Carbamazepine, phenytoin, and gabapentin can worsen absence seizures.
items.a: Ethosuximide
w: Carbamazepine
Lamotrigine
Phenytoin

items.q: A 32-year-old man of Han Chinese ancestry has brief electric-shock pains in the right cheek triggered by chewing and brushing his teeth. Exam and MRI are normal. Carbamazepine is planned. Which test should be performed before starting it?
items.x: HLA-B*1502, common in people of Asian ancestry, strongly predicts carbamazepine-induced SJS and TEN. HLA-B*5701 predicts abacavir hypersensitivity and TPMT guides thiopurine dosing.
items.a: HLA-B*1502 genotyping
w: HLA-B*5701 genotyping
Thiopurine methyltransferase activity
Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase level

items.q: A 54-year-old woman with migraine without aura had an MI with a coronary stent placed 1 year ago. She asks for an acute treatment for her migraine attacks. Which medication should be avoided?
items.x: Triptans cause vasoconstriction and are contraindicated in coronary artery disease, stroke, and uncontrolled hypertension. Gepants such as ubrogepant do not vasoconstrict and are an option.
items.a: Sumatriptan
w: Lasmiditan
Ubrogepant
Metoclopramide

items.q: A 28-year-old woman has migraine with 7 headache days per month despite trigger avoidance. She has moderate persistent asthma and a BMI of 33 kg/m2. She uses a levonorgestrel IUD. Which is the most appropriate preventive medication?
items.x: Topiramate is an effective migraine preventive that tends to cause weight loss. Propranolol is avoided in asthma, amitriptyline and valproate cause weight gain, and valproate is teratogenic. Topiramate also needs reliable contraception.
items.a: Topiramate
w: Propranolol
Amitriptyline
Valproic acid

items.q: A 30-year-old woman with generalized myasthenia gravis on pyridostigmine has dysuria and frequency without fever. Urinalysis shows pyuria. Which antibiotic should be avoided?
items.x: Fluoroquinolones carry a boxed warning for exacerbating myasthenia gravis. Aminoglycosides, macrolides, and magnesium also impair neuromuscular transmission.
items.a: Ciprofloxacin
w: Nitrofurantoin
Cephalexin
Fosfomycin

items.q: A 63-year-old woman has a minor ischemic stroke (NIHSS 2) and is not a thrombolysis candidate. ECG and telemetry show sinus rhythm. Which antithrombotic regimen is most appropriate?
items.x: Short-term DAPT started within 24 hours reduces recurrent stroke after minor stroke or high-risk TIA (CHANCE, POINT). Prolonged DAPT increases bleeding without added benefit, and anticoagulation is not indicated without AF.
items.a: Aspirin plus clopidogrel for 21 days, then single antiplatelet
w: Aspirin plus clopidogrel continued for 12 months, then stop
Aspirin alone for 21 days, then aspirin plus clopidogrel
Apixaban twice daily for 21 days, then single antiplatelet

items.q: A 79-year-old woman with Alzheimer disease started donepezil 6 weeks ago. She has now had two episodes of syncope. Pulse is 44/min and ECG shows sinus bradycardia. Which is the most likely mechanism?
items.x: Cholinesterase inhibitors increase acetylcholine at cardiac muscarinic receptors, causing bradycardia, heart block, and syncope. They should be used cautiously with conduction disease.
items.a: Increased vagal tone from cholinesterase inhibition
w: Orthostatic hypotension from alpha-1 adrenergic blockade
QT prolongation with torsades de pointes
Hyperkalemia caused by drug-induced hypoaldosteronism

items.q: A 74-year-old man with Parkinson disease has distressing visual hallucinations. Anticholinergics and amantadine have been stopped and levodopa reduced as far as tolerated. Which antipsychotic is most appropriate?
items.x: Parkinson disease psychosis is treated with quetiapine, clozapine, or pimavanserin, which have minimal D2 blockade in the nigrostriatal pathway. Haloperidol, risperidone, and olanzapine worsen motor symptoms.
items.a: Quetiapine
w: Haloperidol
Risperidone
Olanzapine

items.q: A 55-year-old woman has an urge to move her legs in the evening, relieved by walking, that disrupts sleep. Exam is normal. Serum ferritin is 32 ng/mL and transferrin saturation is 18 percent. Which is the most appropriate initial treatment?
items.x: Iron is recommended in restless legs syndrome when ferritin is 75 ng/mL or lower or TSAT is below 20 percent. Dopamine agonists and levodopa cause augmentation, and antihistamines worsen symptoms.
items.a: Iron supplementation
w: Pramipexole nightly
Carbidopa-levodopa at bedtime
Diphenhydramine at bedtime

items.q: A 46-year-old man with heavy alcohol use is brought in confused. He has horizontal nystagmus, bilateral lateral rectus weakness, and a wide-based gait. Fingerstick glucose is 82 mg/dL. Which is the most appropriate next step?
items.x: Wernicke encephalopathy requires high-dose IV thiamine immediately, given before or with glucose. Oral thiamine is poorly absorbed in alcohol use disorder and inadequate for acute treatment.
items.a: Intravenous thiamine
w: Intravenous 50 percent dextrose followed by oral thiamine
Oral thiamine once daily
Intravenous lorazepam

items.q: A 3-year-old boy has 2 days of ear pain and fever of 39.2 C (102.6 F). The right tympanic membrane is bulging and erythematous. He has not received antibiotics in the past month and has no drug allergies. Which is the most appropriate treatment?
items.x: High-dose amoxicillin is first-line for acute otitis media in the absence of recent amoxicillin use, concurrent conjunctivitis, or penicillin allergy. Severe symptoms such as fever of 39 C (102.2 F) or higher warrant immediate antibiotics.

Azithromycin 10 mg/kg on day 1, then 5 mg/kg daily
Cefdinir 14 mg/kg/day

items.q: A 10-year-old girl has fever, sore throat, tonsillar exudates, and tender anterior cervical nodes. Rapid strep test is positive. She had anaphylaxis to amoxicillin at age 5. Which is the most appropriate treatment?
items.x: With immediate-type penicillin allergy, IDSA recommends clindamycin, azithromycin, or clarithromycin. First-generation cephalosporins are acceptable only for non-anaphylactic allergy.
items.a: Azithromycin for 5 days
w: Cephalexin for 10 days
Doxycycline for 10 days
Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for 5 days

items.q: A 4-month-old girl has 3 days of rhinorrhea, cough, and wheeze. Respiratory rate is 52/min, SpO2 is 93 percent on room air, and she is feeding adequately. Which is the most appropriate management?
items.x: AAP guidelines recommend supportive care for bronchiolitis. Albuterol, epinephrine, glucocorticoids, and antibiotics are not routinely recommended; oxygen is given if SpO2 stays below 90 percent.
items.a: Nasal suctioning, hydration, and observation
w: Scheduled nebulized albuterol every 4 hours
Oral prednisolone daily for the next 5 days
Nebulized racemic epinephrine and discharge

items.q: A 3-year-old boy has had fever for 6 days with bilateral nonexudative conjunctivitis, cracked red lips, a polymorphous rash, cervical lymphadenopathy, and swollen hands. Which is the most appropriate treatment?
items.x: Kawasaki disease is treated with IVIG 2 g/kg plus aspirin within 10 days of fever onset to reduce coronary artery aneurysms. Ibuprofen antagonizes aspirin's antiplatelet effect.
items.a: Intravenous immune globulin plus aspirin
w: Intravenous immune globulin without aspirin
Aspirin alone with an echocardiogram later
Oral prednisolone plus scheduled ibuprofen

items.q: A 12-day-old girl has a temperature of 38.4 C (101.1 F) and is feeding less than usual. CSF shows pleocytosis and Gram stain is pending. Which is the most appropriate empiric antibiotic regimen?
items.x: Febrile neonates need coverage for GBS, E. coli, and Listeria. Ampicillin plus ceftazidime or cefepime is used when meningitis is suspected. Ceftriaxone is avoided in neonates because it displaces bilirubin and precipitates with calcium.
items.a: Ampicillin plus ceftazidime
w: Ampicillin plus ceftriaxone
Ceftriaxone plus vancomycin
Ceftazidime plus vancomycin

items.q: A 3-year-old boy living in an older home has a venous blood lead level of 52 mcg/dL on repeat testing. He is asymptomatic with a normal neurologic exam. Which is the most appropriate management besides removing the lead source?
items.x: Oral succimer is used for lead levels of 45 to 69 mcg/dL. Levels of 70 or higher or encephalopathy require hospitalization with dimercaprol plus CaNa2EDTA.
items.a: Oral succimer chelation
w: Intramuscular dimercaprol plus calcium disodium EDTA
Repeat lead level in 3 months without chelation
Intravenous deferoxamine infusion

items.q: A 2-year-old girl ingested her mother's prenatal iron tablets 4 hours ago. She has vomiting, hematemesis, and lethargy. Serum bicarbonate is 12 mEq/L and serum iron is 620 mcg/dL. Which is the most appropriate treatment?
items.x: Severe iron poisoning with acidosis, shock, or a level above 500 mcg/dL is treated with IV deferoxamine. Activated charcoal does not bind iron.
items.a: Intravenous deferoxamine
w: Oral activated charcoal
Oral succimer chelation
Intramuscular dimercaprol

items.q: A 31-year-old woman at 36 weeks gestation has BP 166/110 mm Hg, a severe headache, and platelets of 88,000/mm3. Antihypertensive therapy has been given and delivery is planned. Which medication should be given to prevent seizures?
items.x: Magnesium sulfate is the drug of choice to prevent and treat eclamptic seizures and is superior to phenytoin and diazepam.
items.a: Magnesium sulfate

Phenytoin
Lorazepam

items.q: A 27-year-old woman receiving magnesium sulfate for preeclampsia with severe features becomes drowsy. Patellar reflexes are absent and respiratory rate is 8/min. Which is the most appropriate treatment after stopping the infusion?
items.x: Magnesium toxicity causes loss of deep tendon reflexes, then respiratory depression and cardiac arrest. Calcium gluconate antagonizes magnesium at the neuromuscular junction.
items.a: Intravenous calcium gluconate
w: Intravenous naloxone
Intravenous furosemide
Intravenous sodium bicarbonate

items.q: A 30-year-old woman with moderate persistent asthma has uterine atony and heavy bleeding after vaginal delivery despite uterine massage and oxytocin infusion. BP is 118/72 mm Hg. Which uterotonic is contraindicated?
items.x: Carboprost (15-methyl PGF2-alpha) causes bronchoconstriction and is contraindicated in asthma. Methylergonovine is acceptable in normotensive patients.
items.a: Carboprost tromethamine
w: Methylergonovine
Misoprostol

items.q: A 33-year-old woman with preeclampsia delivered vaginally and has uterine atony with 1,000 mL of blood loss despite oxytocin. BP is 158/102 mm Hg. She has no asthma. Which uterotonic should be avoided?
items.x: Methylergonovine, an ergot alkaloid, causes vasoconstriction and is contraindicated in hypertension and preeclampsia.
items.a: Methylergonovine
w: Carboprost tromethamine
Misoprostol
Additional oxytocin

items.q: A 25-year-old woman at 9 weeks gestation has daily nausea with occasional vomiting. She is tolerating fluids, has no ketonuria, and dietary changes and ginger did not help. Which is the most appropriate first-line pharmacotherapy?
items.x: ACOG recommends vitamin B6 alone or with doxylamine as first-line pharmacotherapy for nausea and vomiting of pregnancy. Ondansetron and other antiemetics are later options, and steroids are for refractory hyperemesis.
items.a: Pyridoxine with or without doxylamine
w: Ondansetron with or without famotidine
Metoclopramide with or without ondansetron
Methylprednisolone with a 2-week taper

items.q: A 26-year-old woman with a BMI of 36 kg/m2 had unprotected intercourse 4 days ago. She wants to avoid pregnancy and would like long-term contraception. Which is the most effective option?
items.x: The copper IUD is the most effective emergency contraception up to 5 days after intercourse, is unaffected by body weight, and provides ongoing contraception. Oral levonorgestrel loses efficacy after 72 hours and with obesity.
items.a: Copper intrauterine device
w: Levonorgestrel orally once
Ulipristal acetate orally once
Two doses of combined oral contraceptive pills 12 hours apart

items.q: A 29-year-old woman with polycystic ovary syndrome and BMI 31 kg/m2 has oligomenorrhea and has been trying to conceive for 14 months. Her partner's semen analysis is normal and tubes are patent. Which is the most appropriate first-line ovulation induction agent?
items.x: Letrozole produces higher live birth rates than clomiphene in PCOS and is first-line per ACOG and ASRM. Metformin alone is less effective, and oral contraceptives prevent pregnancy.
items.a: Letrozole
w: Clomiphene citrate
Metformin alone
Combined oral contraceptive pills

items.q: A 51-year-old woman has frequent severe hot flashes and night sweats that disrupt sleep. Her last period was 14 months ago and she has an intact uterus. She has no history of breast cancer, VTE, or cardiovascular disease. Which is the most effective treatment?
items.x: Hormone therapy is the most effective treatment for vasomotor symptoms. With an intact uterus, a progestogen must be added to estrogen to prevent endometrial hyperplasia and cancer.
items.a: Estrogen plus a progestogen
w: Transdermal estradiol alone
Low-dose vaginal estradiol
Low-dose oral paroxetine

items.q: A 30-year-old woman at 30 weeks gestation has gestational diabetes. Despite 2 weeks of medical nutrition therapy, fasting glucose values are 104 to 112 mg/dL, while postprandial values are at goal. Which is the preferred pharmacotherapy?
items.x: Insulin is preferred for gestational diabetes because it does not cross the placenta. Glyburide and metformin cross the placenta, and DPP-4 inhibitors are not used in pregnancy. Bedtime NPH targets fasting hyperglycemia.
items.a: Bedtime NPH insulin
w: Mealtime insulin lispro
Twice-daily metformin
Once-daily glyburide

items.q: A 23-year-old nonpregnant woman has a frothy yellow-green vaginal discharge and vulvar itching. Wet mount shows motile flagellated organisms and vaginal pH is 6.0. Which is the most appropriate treatment?
items.x: CDC recommends the 7-day metronidazole regimen for trichomoniasis in women because it is more effective than single-dose therapy. Sex partners should also be treated.
items.a: Metronidazole 500 mg twice daily for 7 days
w: Metronidazole 2 g orally as a single dose
Fluconazole 150 mg orally once
Clindamycin 2 percent vaginal cream for 7 days

items.q: A 28-year-old woman at 18 weeks gestation has vulvar itching and thick white discharge. KOH prep shows pseudohyphae. Which is the most appropriate treatment?
items.x: Topical azoles for 7 days are recommended for vulvovaginal candidiasis in pregnancy. Oral fluconazole has been linked to miscarriage and birth defects.
items.a: Topical clotrimazole for 7 days
w: Oral fluconazole once
Oral fluconazole weekly for 6 months
Vaginal boric acid capsules for 14 days

items.q: A 25-year-old woman received benzathine penicillin G for secondary syphilis 4 hours ago. She now has fever of 38.7 C (101.7 F), myalgias, headache, and a more prominent rash. BP is 118/74 mm Hg. Which is the most appropriate management?
items.x: The Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction is an acute febrile response to treponemal lysis within 24 hours of treatment. It is self-limited, is not an allergy, and is treated supportively.
items.a: Antipyretics and reassurance for a self-limited reaction
w: Intramuscular epinephrine and admission for anaphylaxis
Doxycycline in place of penicillin for a drug allergy
A second penicillin dose now for treatment failure

items.q: A 30-year-old man is newly diagnosed with HIV. CD4 count is 420 cells/mm3 and viral load is 60,000 copies/mL. HLA-B*5701 is negative, hepatitis B serologies are negative, and creatinine is normal. Which is the most appropriate approach?
items.x: Guidelines recommend starting ART at diagnosis regardless of CD4 count, ideally the same day. Initial regimens are based on an integrase inhibitor such as dolutegravir or bictegravir with two NRTIs.
items.a: Start dolutegravir plus tenofovir-emtricitabine now
w: Defer all ART until the CD4 count falls below 350
Start tenofovir-emtricitabine alone as dual therapy
Start dolutegravir monotherapy and add others later

items.q: A 26-year-old nurse sustained a deep needlestick injury 3 hours ago from a patient with known HIV and a detectable viral load. Her baseline HIV test is pending. Which is the most appropriate management?
items.x: Post-exposure prophylaxis should begin as soon as possible, ideally within hours and no later than 72 hours, with a 3-drug regimen such as bictegravir-emtricitabine-tenofovir alafenamide for 28 days.
items.a: Start a 3-drug PEP regimen now for 28 days
w: Wait for the source viral load before deciding on PEP
Tenofovir-emtricitabine alone for 7 days
Start PEP only if her baseline HIV test is positive

items.q: A 39-year-old man with untreated HIV (CD4 60 cells/mm3) has progressive dyspnea, dry cough, and bilateral interstitial infiltrates. PaO2 is 62 mm Hg on room air. Induced sputum confirms Pneumocystis. TMP-SMX is started. Which medication should be added?
items.x: Adjunctive glucocorticoids reduce mortality in moderate to severe Pneumocystis pneumonia with PaO2 below 70 mm Hg or an A-a gradient of 35 or more, and should start within 72 hours.
items.a: Prednisone for 21 days
w: Leucovorin for 21 days
Fluconazole for 21 days
Azithromycin once weekly

items.q: A 34-year-old man with HIV (CD4 30 cells/mm3) has 2 weeks of headache and fever. CSF opening pressure is 32 cm H2O and cryptococcal antigen is positive. Which is the most appropriate induction therapy?
items.x: Induction for cryptococcal meningitis is liposomal amphotericin B plus flucytosine, with serial LPs for elevated pressure. ART is delayed 4 to 6 weeks to reduce fatal immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome.
items.a: Liposomal amphotericin B plus flucytosine
w: High-dose fluconazole monotherapy by mouth
Liposomal amphotericin B plus caspofungin
Liposomal amphotericin B plus voriconazole

items.q: A 35-year-old woman from Vietnam has a positive interferon-gamma release assay during employment screening. She has no symptoms and chest x-ray is normal. HIV is negative and she takes no other medications. Which is the most appropriate treatment?
items.x: Rifamycin-based short regimens (4 months of rifampin, 3 months of weekly isoniazid-rifapentine, or 3 months of daily isoniazid-rifampin) are preferred for latent TB because of better completion and less hepatotoxicity.
items.a: Rifampin daily for 4 months
w: Rifampin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol for 2 months
No treatment unless symptoms develop
Isoniazid daily for 3 months

items.q: A 27-year-old woman taking a combined oral contraceptive is starting rifampin for latent TB. Which is the most appropriate contraceptive advice?
items.x: Rifampin strongly induces CYP3A4 and reduces levels of oral hormonal contraceptives and implants. A copper IUD, levonorgestrel IUD, or DMPA injection is recommended.
items.a: Use a copper IUD or other nonhormonal method during therapy
w: No change, since the interaction is clinically minor
Switch to the etonogestrel implant during therapy
Switch to a progestin-only pill during therapy

items.q: A 29-year-old woman at 14 weeks gestation must travel for work to rural Ghana, where chloroquine-resistant P. falciparum is widespread. Which malaria chemoprophylaxis is most appropriate?
items.x: Mefloquine is the recommended chemoprophylaxis in pregnancy for chloroquine-resistant areas. Doxycycline is contraindicated, primaquine risks hemolysis in a G6PD-deficient fetus, and chloroquine resistance is widespread in Africa.
items.a: Mefloquine weekly
w: Doxycycline daily
Atovaquone-proguanil daily
Chloroquine weekly

items.q: A 26-year-old man traveling in Thailand develops fever of 38.8 C (101.8 F), abdominal cramps, and bloody diarrhea. Which is the most appropriate antibiotic?
items.x: Azithromycin is preferred for dysentery and for travelers' diarrhea in Southeast Asia because of high fluoroquinolone resistance in Campylobacter. Rifaximin is not used for invasive disease.
items.a: Azithromycin
w: Ciprofloxacin
Rifaximin
Loperamide alone

items.q: A 45-year-old woman has 2 days of fever, headache, and confusion with an episode of olfactory hallucinations. MRI shows right temporal lobe hyperintensity and CSF has lymphocytic pleocytosis with red cells. Which is the most appropriate treatment while awaiting PCR?
items.x: Suspected HSV encephalitis requires empiric IV acyclovir immediately because delay increases mortality and neurologic sequelae. Oral agents do not achieve adequate CNS levels.

Intravenous ganciclovir 5 mg/kg every 12 hours
Intravenous ceftriaxone 2 g every 12 hours alone

items.q: A 30-year-old man from Connecticut had an expanding red rash after a camping trip and now, 3 weeks after the trip, has a left facial droop involving the forehead. Lyme serology is positive. He has no headache or meningismus. Which is the most appropriate treatment?
items.x: Lyme facial palsy without meningitis can be treated with oral doxycycline for 14 days. IV ceftriaxone is reserved for meningitis, high-grade AV block, or inability to take oral therapy.
items.a: Oral doxycycline for 14 days

Oral prednisone alone
Oral amoxicillin for 5 days

items.q: A 66-year-old woman has 8 watery stools daily after a course of clindamycin. WBC is 11,000/mm3 and creatinine is 0.9 mg/dL. Stool testing confirms C. difficile infection. This is her first episode. Which is the most appropriate treatment?
items.x: IDSA prefers fidaxomicin for an initial episode because of lower recurrence, with oral vancomycin as an acceptable alternative. Metronidazole is only an option for nonsevere disease when the others are unavailable.
items.a: Oral fidaxomicin for 10 days
w: Oral metronidazole for 14 days
Intravenous metronidazole alone
Oral rifaximin for 7 days

items.q: A 58-year-old man with lung cancer will receive cisplatin-based chemotherapy. Which antiemetic regimen is most appropriate before the first cycle?
items.x: Highly emetogenic chemotherapy such as cisplatin warrants four-drug prophylaxis per ASCO and NCCN: an NK1 antagonist, a 5-HT3 antagonist, dexamethasone, and olanzapine.
items.a: NK1 antagonist, 5-HT3 antagonist, dexamethasone, and olanzapine
