items.q: The nurse is planning care for a medical-surgical unit. Which task is appropriate to delegate to an unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP)?

items.a: Walking a stable client in the hall 2 days after surgery
w: Teaching a client how to draw up and inject insulin
Doing the admission assessment for a newly arrived client
Evaluating a client's response to an IV pain medicine

items.q: The charge nurse is making assignments. Which client is most appropriate to assign to a licensed practical nurse (LPN)?
items.x: LPNs care for stable clients with predictable outcomes. New chest pain, the start of a transfusion and initial teaching need RN assessment.
items.a: A client with stable chronic heart failure who needs scheduled oral medicines
w: A newly admitted client who reports chest pain radiating to the jaw
A client in the first 15 minutes of a packed red blood cell transfusion
A client who needs first-time teaching about a new anticoagulant

items.q: A client who signed a surgical consent form says, "I don't really understand what the surgeon is going to do." What should the nurse do?
items.x: Consent is informed only when the client understands. Explaining the procedure and its risks is the provider's duty, so the nurse notifies the surgeon.
items.a: Notify the surgeon that the client needs more information before surgery
w: Explain the details of the procedure and its risks to the client
Reassure the client that the surgeon is skilled and experienced
Proceed with surgical preparation because the form is already signed

items.q: The nurse signs a surgical consent form as a witness. What does the nurse's signature confirm?
items.x: As a witness, the nurse verifies the identity of the signer and that the signature was given voluntarily. The provider is responsible for the explanation.
items.a: The client signed the form voluntarily and the signature is the client's
w: The nurse explained the risks and benefits of the procedure
The client understands every alternative to the planned surgery
The surgeon has the privileges needed to perform the procedure

items.q: An alert, competent adult client refuses a prescribed blood transfusion for religious reasons. What is the nurse's best action?
items.x: A competent adult has the right to refuse treatment. The nurse respects autonomy, informs the provider and documents the refusal.
items.a: Notify the provider and document the client's informed refusal
w: Give the transfusion because the client's hemoglobin is low
Ask the client's family to talk the client into the transfusion
Contact the hospital lawyer to obtain a court order right away

items.q: A caller says she is a client's daughter and asks how the client is doing. What should the nurse do first?
items.x: Under privacy rules, the nurse shares health information only with people the client has authorized, often verified by a code or the client's permission.
items.a: Check whether the client has authorized release of information to this caller
w: Give a brief update because family members are entitled to information
Tell the caller the client is stable but give no other details
Transfer the call to the client's room without asking the client

items.q: The nurse reviews documentation after a client fall. Which statement by a new nurse needs correction?

"I will note that I notified the provider and the time I called."
"I will record the assessment I performed after the fall."

items.q: The nurse questions a prescription that seems unsafe. The provider insists that the nurse carry it out. What is the nurse's next action?
items.x: When a safety concern is not resolved with the provider, the nurse follows the chain of command and does not carry out an order believed to be unsafe.
items.a: Notify the charge nurse or nursing supervisor using the chain of command

Ask another nurse on the unit to give the medicine instead
Write a note in the chart that the provider was rude and unsafe

items.q: During a mass-casualty event, the nurse uses START triage. Which client should be tagged immediate (red)?
items.x: In START, a respiratory rate above 30 is immediate. Walking wounded are minor, a client with a pulse who follows commands is delayed, and no breathing after repositioning is expectant.
items.a: A client who is breathing 34 times a minute after the airway is opened

A client with a deformed thigh, a radial pulse and who follows commands
A client who does not breathe after the airway is repositioned

items.q: The nurse calls the provider about a client whose oxygen saturation has dropped, using SBAR. Which statement is the recommendation?

"The client was admitted 2 days ago with pneumonia and has COPD."
"I think the client's pneumonia may be getting worse."

items.q: The nurse tells a client, "I will be back in 10 minutes to help you walk," and returns as promised. Which ethical principle does this show?

w: Veracity
Justice
Beneficence

items.q: A client tells the nurse, "I don't want this surgery, but my children keep pushing me." The client is alert and competent. What is the nurse's priority action?
items.x: As the client's advocate, the nurse makes sure the surgeon knows the client may not be giving voluntary consent.

Reassure the client that the surgery will help a great deal
Ask the children to sign the surgical consent form instead

items.q: A client says, "I'm leaving now. I've had enough of this hospital." The client is alert and oriented. What should the nurse do first?

Remove the IV and let the client leave without notifying anyone

items.q: An unlicensed assistive personnel reports that a client's blood pressure is 88/50 mm Hg after walking in the hall. What should the nurse do first?

"By about 6 months of age."
"By about 24 months of age."

items.q: The nurse assesses a 4-month-old at a well-child visit. Which finding should the nurse report to the provider?
items.x: The anterior fontanel normally closes by 12 to 18 months. Early closure can signal craniosynostosis.
items.a: The anterior fontanel is closed
w: The posterior fontanel is closed
The infant holds the head steady when sitting supported
The infant laughs out loud

items.q: A parent of a 1-year-old asks when to turn the car seat to face forward. What should the nurse say?
items.x: Current guidance is to keep children rear-facing as long as possible, until they reach the seat's rear-facing limit.
items.a: "Keep it rear-facing until your child outgrows the seat's rear-facing limits."
w: "You can turn it forward now, since your child has turned 1 year old."
"Turn it forward as soon as your child weighs about 20 pounds."
"Turn it forward once your child's feet can touch the back seat."

items.q: The nurse is teaching new parents about safe sleep. Which instruction is correct?
items.x: Back sleeping on a firm, flat, bare surface reduces the risk of sudden infant death and suffocation.
items.a: Place the baby on the back on a firm, flat mattress with no bumpers
w: Place the baby on the side with a rolled blanket for support
Place the baby on the stomach if the baby spits up often
Let the baby sleep in the parents' bed on a soft pillow

items.q: A postpartum client is not immune to rubella and receives the MMR vaccine before discharge. Which teaching is most important?
items.x: MMR is a live vaccine, so pregnancy should be avoided for 4 weeks. Breastfeeding can continue.
items.a: Avoid becoming pregnant for at least 4 weeks
w: Stop breastfeeding for 2 weeks after the vaccine
Stay away from other children for 2 weeks
Expect a rubella rash within 24 hours

items.q: Several children are due for the varicella vaccine. Which child has a contraindication to receiving it today?
items.x: Varicella vaccine is a live vaccine and is contraindicated with severe immunosuppression. A mild cold, a pregnant household member and local redness are not contraindications.
items.a: A child receiving chemotherapy for leukemia
w: A child with a runny nose and no fever
A child whose mother is pregnant
A child who had redness at a previous injection site

items.q: The nurse is measuring fundal height for a client at 20 weeks of gestation. Where should the nurse expect to find the fundus?
items.x: At 20 weeks the fundus is usually at the umbilicus. After that, fundal height in centimeters roughly matches the weeks of gestation.
items.a: At about the level of the umbilicus
w: Just above the symphysis pubis
Halfway between the pubis and the umbilicus
Just below the xiphoid process

items.q: A client planning a pregnancy asks why folic acid is recommended. What should the nurse say?
items.x: Folic acid taken before conception and in early pregnancy reduces neural tube defects such as spina bifida.
items.a: "It lowers the risk of neural tube defects in the baby."
w: "It prevents iron-deficiency anemia during pregnancy."
"It lowers the risk of high blood pressure in pregnancy."
"It helps the baby's bones develop properly."

items.q: A pregnant client asks when she will be screened for gestational diabetes. Unless she has risk factors, what should the nurse say?
items.x: Routine screening for gestational diabetes is done at 24 to 28 weeks. Clients with risk factors may be screened earlier.
items.a: "Between 24 and 28 weeks of pregnancy."
w: "At your first prenatal visit only."
"Between 12 and 16 weeks of pregnancy."
"After 36 weeks of pregnancy."

items.q: A pregnant client asks when she will be tested for group B streptococcus. What should the nurse say?
items.x: Vaginal-rectal GBS culture is done at 36 to 37 weeks so results are current at delivery.
items.a: "At about 36 to 37 weeks of pregnancy."
w: "At your first prenatal visit."
"At about 20 weeks of pregnancy."
"Only if you develop a fever in labor."

items.q: A pregnant client who is Rh negative and unsensitized is at 28 weeks of gestation. What should the nurse expect to give?
items.x: Rh(D) immune globulin is given at about 28 weeks and after birth of an Rh-positive infant to prevent sensitization.
items.a: Rh(D) immune globulin
w: Rubella vaccine
Hepatitis B immune globulin
Varicella vaccine

items.q: A client at 32 weeks of gestation calls the clinic. Which report needs prompt evaluation?
items.x: Severe headache with visual changes can signal preeclampsia with severe features. The others are common discomforts.
items.a: A severe headache with blurred vision
w: Swelling of the ankles at the end of the day
Heartburn after large meals
Leg cramps at night

items.q: A breastfeeding parent asks how to tell if the baby is getting enough milk. What should the nurse say?
items.x: Frequent wet diapers and steady weight gain show adequate intake. Breasts usually feel softer after feeding.
items.a: "Six or more wet diapers a day by the end of the first week is a good sign."
w: "Your baby should sleep at least 6 hours at a time at night."
"Your baby should feed for no more than 5 minutes per breast."
"Your breasts should feel full and firm after each feeding."

items.q: On the first day after birth, the nurse finds the client's fundus firm, 2 cm above the umbilicus and displaced to the right. What should the nurse do first?
items.x: A firm fundus that is high and displaced to one side usually means a full bladder, which can lead to uterine atony.
items.a: Help the client empty her bladder
w: Massage the fundus firmly
Notify the provider right away
Record it as an expected finding

items.q: An adult at average risk for colorectal cancer asks when to start screening. What should the nurse say?
items.x: Current guidelines recommend colorectal cancer screening for average-risk adults beginning at age 45.
items.a: "Screening is recommended starting at age 45."
w: "Screening is recommended starting at age 35."
"Screening starts at age 60 if you have no symptoms."
"Screening is needed only if you see blood in your stool."

items.q: A 23-year-old client asks how often she needs cervical cancer screening. What should the nurse say?
items.x: For ages 21 to 29, cervical cytology alone every 3 years is recommended.
items.a: "A Pap test every 3 years is recommended at your age."
w: "A Pap test every year is recommended at your age."
"An HPV test every 5 years is recommended at your age."
"You do not need screening until age 30."

items.q: The nurse is teaching a 17-year-old client about testicular self-examination. Which instruction is correct?
items.x: Monthly checks after a warm shower, when the scrotum is relaxed, help find painless lumps early.
items.a: "Check each testicle once a month after a warm shower."
w: "Check each testicle once a year at your checkup."
"Check while the scrotum is cold so lumps stand out."
"A firm, painless lump is normal and needs no follow-up."

items.q: A healthy 62-year-old client asks which vaccine is recommended to prevent shingles. What should the nurse tell the client?
items.x: The recombinant zoster vaccine is recommended as a 2-dose series for adults 50 and older.
items.a: The two-dose recombinant zoster vaccine series
w: One dose of the varicella vaccine
A measles, mumps and rubella booster
A single pneumococcal vaccine dose

items.q: The nurse is screening children for lead exposure. Which child is at highest risk?
items.x: Homes built before 1978 may contain lead paint, and peeling paint or dust is a major source of exposure.
items.a: A child living in a house built in 1950 with peeling paint
w: A child living in an apartment built in 2015
A child who drinks bottled water each day
A child who attends a new day care center

items.q: A parent calls because a 2-year-old swallowed several of a grandparent's pills. What should the nurse tell the parent to do first?
items.x: Poison Control gives specific guidance. Inducing vomiting is no longer recommended, and waiting can delay treatment.
items.a: Call Poison Control right away
w: Give the child syrup of ipecac
Give the child a large glass of milk
Wait and watch for symptoms

items.q: The nurse is assessing a healthy 80-year-old client. Which finding is an expected change of aging?
items.x: Presbycusis, high-frequency hearing loss, is common with aging. Acute confusion, incontinence and memory loss are not normal aging.
items.a: Reduced ability to hear high-pitched sounds
w: New confusion that began this week
Loss of bladder control with coughing
Forgetting the names of close family

items.q: A client who smokes says, "I plan to quit next month." Which nursing action fits this client's stage of change?
items.x: Planning to quit within the next month is the preparation stage, when setting a date and plan is most helpful.
items.a: Help the client set a quit date and make a plan
w: Give information about the health risks of smoking
Praise the client for staying smoke-free
Ask the client to think about pros and cons later

items.q: The nurse wants to confirm that a client understands new discharge instructions. Which method is best?
items.x: The teach-back method shows whether the client truly understood and lets the nurse correct gaps.
items.a: Ask the client to explain the instructions in their own words
w: Ask, "Do you have any questions about this?"
Ask the client to sign the discharge form
Give the client a printed handout to read at home

items.q: The nurse is teaching a parent about starting solid foods. Which parent statement needs more teaching?
items.x: Honey can cause infant botulism and should not be given before 12 months of age.
items.a: "I will add honey to the baby's cereal at 6 months."
w: "I will start one new single-ingredient food at a time."
"I will wait a few days before adding another new food."
"I will keep breastfeeding while starting solid foods."

items.q: A pregnant client asks about eating fish. Which statement shows she understands the teaching?
items.x: High-mercury fish should be avoided, but low-mercury fish 2 to 3 times a week is encouraged. Raw fish carries infection risk.
items.a: "I will avoid swordfish, shark and king mackerel."
w: "I will avoid all fish until after the baby is born."
"I will eat tuna steaks every day for the protein."
"I will eat raw sushi if it comes from a good restaurant."

items.q: A parent asks when a newborn screening blood test for conditions such as PKU should be collected. What should the nurse say?
items.x: The screen is collected after 24 hours of age so that metabolic changes, such as rising phenylalanine, can be detected.
items.a: "After the baby is at least 24 hours old."
w: "Right after birth from the umbilical cord."
"At the 2-month well-baby visit."
"Only if the baby is not feeding well."

items.q: A parent asks how to tell if a toddler is ready for toilet training. Which signs show readiness? Select all that apply.
items.x: Readiness depends on physical and cognitive signs, not age alone or the parent's schedule. Most children are ready between 18 and 24 months or later.
opts: Stays dry for about 2 hours at a time
Can tell the parent when the diaper is wet
Can pull pants up and down
Has just turned 12 months old
The parent wants training done before a new baby
ok: Stays dry for about 2 hours at a time
Can tell the parent when the diaper is wet
Can pull pants up and down

items.q: The nurse is assessing a 1-day-old newborn. Which findings are expected? Select all that apply.
items.x: Acrocyanosis, milia and congenital dermal melanocytosis are normal. Jaundice in the first 24 hours is pathologic, and a rate of 80 is tachypnea.
opts: Bluish hands and feet
Small white bumps on the nose
Blue-gray patches on the lower back
Yellow skin at 12 hours of age
A resting respiratory rate of 80
ok: Bluish hands and feet
Small white bumps on the nose
Blue-gray patches on the lower back

items.q: The nurse is teaching a pregnant client which signs to report right away. Which signs should be included? Select all that apply.
items.x: Bleeding, sudden facial swelling and decreased fetal movement can signal serious problems. The others are common discomforts.
opts: Vaginal bleeding
Sudden swelling of the face and hands
Fewer fetal movements than usual
Ankle swelling at the end of the day
Heartburn after large meals
A stuffy nose
ok: Vaginal bleeding
Sudden swelling of the face and hands
Fewer fetal movements than usual

items.q: The nurse is assessing an older adult. Which findings are expected changes of aging? Select all that apply.
items.x: Skin, vision and reaction-time changes are normal with aging. Sudden memory loss and incontinence need evaluation.
opts: Decreased skin elasticity
Difficulty seeing things up close
Slower reaction time
Sudden loss of memory
Urinary incontinence
ok: Decreased skin elasticity
Difficulty seeing things up close
Slower reaction time

items.q: The nurse is teaching parents how to lower the risk of sudden infant death. Which instructions are correct? Select all that apply.
items.x: Back sleeping, pacifier use and room-sharing without bed-sharing reduce risk. Bumpers, prone sleep and soft bedding increase it.
opts: Place the baby on the back for every sleep
Offer a pacifier at nap time and bedtime
Share a room but not a bed with the baby
Use soft crib bumpers to protect the head
Let the baby sleep on the stomach after feeding
Cover the baby with a thick blanket
ok: Place the baby on the back for every sleep
Offer a pacifier at nap time and bedtime
Share a room but not a bed with the baby

items.q: The nurse is teaching a new parent about breastfeeding. Which instructions are correct? Select all that apply.
items.x: Frequent, on-demand feeding and proper latch release support breastfeeding. Water supplements and time limits interfere with intake and supply.
opts: Feed the baby 8 to 12 times every 24 hours
Break the suction with a finger before removing the baby
Offer both breasts at each feeding
Give water between feedings to prevent dehydration
Limit each feeding to 5 minutes per breast
ok: Feed the baby 8 to 12 times every 24 hours
Break the suction with a finger before removing the baby
Offer both breasts at each feeding

items.q: A postmenopausal client asks how to lower the risk of osteoporosis. Which actions should the nurse recommend? Select all that apply.
items.x: Weight-bearing exercise, calcium, vitamin D and not smoking protect bone. High caffeine intake can increase calcium loss, and swimming is not weight-bearing.
opts: Walk or do other weight-bearing exercise
Get enough calcium and vitamin D
Quit smoking
Drink several cups of coffee each day
Choose swimming as the main exercise for bone strength
ok: Walk or do other weight-bearing exercise
Get enough calcium and vitamin D
Quit smoking

items.q: The nurse is screening a 2-year-old for lead exposure. Which findings increase the child's risk? Select all that apply.
items.x: Old paint, take-home lead dust from a parent's job and pica raise risk. Bottled water and new buildings do not.
opts: The family lives in a house built before 1978
A parent works at a battery recycling plant
The child often eats nonfood items like dirt
The family drinks bottled water
The child goes to a day care in a new building
ok: The family lives in a house built before 1978
A parent works at a battery recycling plant
The child often eats nonfood items like dirt

items.q: Put these infant motor milestones in the order they usually appear.
items.x: Motor development moves from head to toe: head control, rolling, sitting, pulling to stand, then walking.
opts: Holds the head steady
Rolls from front to back
Sits without support
Pulls to stand
Walks alone
ok: Holds the head steady
Rolls from front to back
Sits without support
Pulls to stand
Walks alone

items.q: A client is working to quit smoking. Put the stages of change in order.
items.x: The transtheoretical model moves from not considering change, to considering it, planning, acting and then sustaining it.
opts: Precontemplation
Contemplation
Preparation
Action
Maintenance
ok: Precontemplation
Contemplation
Preparation
Action
Maintenance

items.q: Put Erikson's childhood and adolescent stages in order.
items.x: Erikson's stages run from infancy through adolescence in this order.
opts: Trust versus mistrust
Autonomy versus shame and doubt
Initiative versus guilt
Industry versus inferiority
Identity versus role confusion
ok: Trust versus mistrust
Autonomy versus shame and doubt
Initiative versus guilt
Industry versus inferiority
Identity versus role confusion

items.q: The nurse uses the teach-back method. Put the steps in order.
items.x: Teach-back is a loop: teach, check understanding, clarify, then check again.
opts: Explain the information in plain language
Ask the client to explain it back in their own words
Clarify any part the client did not understand
Ask the client to explain it again
ok: Explain the information in plain language
Ask the client to explain it back in their own words
Clarify any part the client did not understand
Ask the client to explain it again

items.q: A client with cancer says, "I'm just a burden to my family now." Which response by the nurse is most therapeutic?
items.x: An open-ended invitation explores the client's feelings. Reassurance, advice and why-questions block communication.
items.a: "Tell me more about feeling like a burden."
w: "Your family loves you and is happy to help."
"You should not think about yourself that way."
"Why do you think your family feels that way?"

items.q: A client with depression says, "I won't be around to bother anyone much longer." What should the nurse say?
items.x: Asking directly about suicidal thoughts is essential and does not increase risk. It opens a full suicide risk assessment.
items.a: "Are you thinking about killing yourself?"
w: "Don't talk like that. You have so much to live for."
"Are you planning to move away from your family?"
"I'm sure you will feel better once the medicine works."

items.q: A client with major depression has been withdrawn for weeks. Today the client seems calm and is giving away personal items. What is the nurse's priority?
items.x: A sudden calm and giving away belongings can mean the client has decided on a suicide plan.
items.a: Assess the client for a suicide plan
w: Note the improvement in the client's mood
Encourage the client to join group activities
Ask the provider about a discharge date

items.q: A client with schizophrenia says the voices are talking again. Which question is the priority?
items.x: Command hallucinations can direct harm to self or others, so safety is assessed first.
items.a: "Are the voices telling you to hurt yourself or anyone else?"
w: "How long have you been hearing these voices?"
"Do you recognize whose voices they are?"
"Did you take your medicine this morning?"

items.q: A client believes the hospital food is poisoned and refuses meals. Which action is best?
items.x: Sealed foods meet nutrition needs without arguing with the delusion. Arguing and threats increase mistrust.
items.a: Offer foods in sealed packages the client can open
w: Explain that the hospital food is safe to eat
Taste the food in front of the client
Tell the client meals will be given by tube if refused

items.q: A client in an acute manic episode will not sit down to eat. Which action is best?
items.x: Portable, high-calorie foods meet the high energy needs of a client who cannot sit still.
items.a: Offer high-calorie finger foods the client can eat while moving
w: Require the client to sit at the table until the meal is done
Serve meals in the busy dining room with other clients
Wait until the client is calm before offering any food

items.q: A client who drinks heavily every day had the last drink 8 hours ago. Which finding is an early sign of alcohol withdrawal?
items.x: Tremor, anxiety and tachycardia appear within hours. Hallucinations with disorientation occur later, and pinpoint pupils suggest opioids.
items.a: Hand tremor and anxiety
w: Visual hallucinations and disorientation
Pinpoint pupils and drowsiness
Slow pulse and low blood pressure

items.q: A client is criticized by his boss at work and then yells at his wife when he gets home. Which defense mechanism is the client using?
items.x: Displacement moves feelings from the true source to a safer target.
items.a: Displacement
w: Projection
Sublimation
Rationalization

items.q: A client with terminal cancer says, "If I can just live to see my daughter's wedding, I'll be ready." Which stage of grief is the client showing?
items.x: Bargaining is an attempt to postpone loss, often by making a deal for more time.
items.a: Bargaining
w: Denial
Anger
Acceptance

items.q: A 4-month-old who cannot yet roll over is brought in with a spiral fracture of the femur. The parents say the baby rolled off the couch. What should the nurse do?
items.x: The injury does not match the child's development or the history. Nurses must report suspected abuse; they do not need proof.
items.a: Report suspected abuse to child protective services per law
w: Ask the parents to describe the fall again in more detail
Teach the parents how to prevent falls from furniture
Wait for the x-ray report before making any decision

items.q: A client in the emergency department has bruises on the upper arms. Her partner stays at her side and answers all questions. What should the nurse do?
items.x: Screening for intimate partner violence should take place privately so the client can speak safely.
items.a: Ask the partner to step out and interview the client alone
w: Ask the client about abuse while the partner is present
Ask the partner how the bruises happened
Give the client a hotline number in front of the partner

items.q: A client arrives in the emergency department after a sexual assault. What is the nurse's priority?
items.x: Safety and emotional support come first. Washing or changing clothes can destroy evidence, and blaming questions harm the client.
items.a: Stay with the client in a private room
w: Ask the client to change into a hospital gown and wash
Ask the client why she went to that place alone
Call the client's family to come to the hospital

items.q: A client is having a panic attack. Which action is best?
items.x: During panic, the client cannot process complex information. A calm presence and simple directions help.
items.a: Stay with the client and use short, simple statements
w: Teach the client a detailed relaxation technique now
Leave the client alone in a quiet room to calm down
Ask the client to explain what caused the attack

items.q: A client with bulimia nervosa is admitted for treatment. Which action helps prevent purging?
items.x: Supervision after meals prevents self-induced vomiting during the time it would most likely occur.
items.a: Supervise the client for at least 1 hour after meals
w: Let the client use the bathroom right after meals
Allow the client to eat alone in the room
Weigh the client after each meal

items.q: A client with anorexia nervosa is admitted. Which finding is the priority?
items.x: Bradycardia and orthostatic changes signal cardiovascular compromise. Lanugo, amenorrhea and food preoccupation are expected.
items.a: A resting heart rate of 42 and dizziness when standing
w: Fine, soft hair growing on the arms and back
No menstrual period for 4 months
Talking often about recipes and cooking

items.q: The nurse is assessing a client with schizophrenia. Which finding is a negative symptom?
items.x: Negative symptoms are losses of normal function, such as alogia and avolition. The others are positive symptoms.
items.a: Very little speech and no motivation to bathe
w: Hearing voices that no one else hears
Believing the television sends messages
Speech that jumps quickly between ideas

items.q: A client with Alzheimer disease keeps asking for her husband, who died 3 years ago. Which response is best?
items.x: Validation responds to the feeling without repeatedly causing new grief or lying to the client.
items.a: "You miss him. Tell me about your husband."
w: "Your husband died 3 years ago. Do you remember?"
"He will be here to visit you later today."
"Let's talk about something happier instead."

items.q: An older adult client becomes confused on the second day after surgery. Which finding suggests delirium rather than dementia?
items.x: Delirium begins suddenly and fluctuates, often with inattention. Dementia develops slowly.
items.a: Sudden onset of confusion that changes during the day
w: Slow memory loss over the past 2 years
Steady trouble finding words for months
Gradual change in personality over time

items.q: A client with obsessive-compulsive disorder washes the hands for long periods before each meal. Which approach is best at first?
items.x: Abruptly preventing a ritual raises anxiety. Time is allowed at first, and limits are set gradually with the client.
items.a: Allow time for the ritual and limit it gradually with the client
w: Prevent the client from washing the hands before any meal
Lock the bathroom door so the client is unable to wash
Explain to the client that the washing is not logical

items.q: A veteran with post-traumatic stress disorder is resting in bed. Which approach should the nurse use when entering the room?
items.x: Clients with PTSD may have an exaggerated startle response. Announcing yourself before touch prevents a sudden trigger.
items.a: Knock, speak the client's name and explain before touching
w: Touch the client's shoulder gently to wake him
Enter quietly so the client is not disturbed
Turn on all the lights at once so he can see

items.q: A client with borderline personality disorder praises some staff and criticizes others. Which strategy is best?
items.x: Consistent limits from all staff reduce splitting and manipulation.
items.a: Have all staff follow the same care plan and limits
w: Assign the staff the client likes to most shifts
Let each nurse set rules for the client as needed
Discuss the client's complaints about staff with the client

items.q: A client on a mental health unit is pacing, clenching the fists and speaking loudly. What should the nurse do first?
items.x: Verbal de-escalation and choices are first-line. Restraint and seclusion are a last resort.
items.a: Speak calmly and offer a choice of a quiet room or a walk
w: Call for help to place the client in restraints
Tell the client that yelling will lead to seclusion
Ignore the behavior so it is not reinforced

items.q: Which statement by the nurse is most likely to block communication with a client?
items.x: Why-questions sound judgmental and make clients defensive. The other statements are therapeutic.
items.a: "Why did you stop taking your medicine?"
w: "You seem upset about going home."
"Tell me what happened before you came in."
"Go on. I'm listening."

items.q: A client who had a mastectomy yesterday has not looked at the incision. What should the nurse do?
items.x: Offering a choice respects the client's pace in adjusting to a change in body image.
items.a: Ask whether the client would like to look at the incision now or later
w: Insist that the client look at the incision before discharge
Keep the incision covered until the provider visits
Tell the client the incision looks much better than expected

items.q: Parents have just delivered a stillborn infant. What should the nurse do?
items.x: Holding, naming and keepsakes help parents grieve. Removing the infant quickly or minimizing the loss can complicate grief.
items.a: Offer the parents time to hold the infant
w: Take the infant away quickly to spare the parents
Tell the parents they can try again soon
Avoid using the baby's name with the parents

items.q: A client 4 weeks after giving birth tells the nurse she has no interest in the baby and cannot sleep even when the baby sleeps. What should the nurse do?
items.x: Baby blues resolve within about 2 weeks. Lasting loss of interest and insomnia suggest postpartum depression.
items.a: Notify the provider and screen for postpartum depression
w: Explain that these feelings are normal baby blues
Suggest she take a nap when family can help
Encourage her to spend more time with the baby

items.q: A client is having electroconvulsive therapy for depression. Which statement shows the client understands the treatment?
items.x: Short-term confusion and memory loss after ECT are common. Clients receive anesthesia and should not drive afterward.
items.a: "I may be confused and forgetful for a while after each treatment."
w: "I will be awake and alert for the whole treatment."
"My memory loss will be permanent after treatment."
"I can drive myself home after each treatment."

items.q: A client with a terminal illness says, "I'm scared to die." Which response is best?
items.x: An open question helps the client name and talk through the fear. A chaplain referral may help later but should not cut off the discussion.
items.a: "What frightens you the most?"
w: "Everyone is scared of dying at some point."
"You have plenty of time left. Try not to worry."
"Would you like me to call the chaplain?"

items.q: The nurse is assessing a client's suicide risk. Which factors increase risk? Select all that apply.
items.x: Prior attempts, access to lethal means and recent loss increase risk. Social support and faith involvement are protective.
opts: A previous suicide attempt
A firearm in the home
The recent death of a spouse
A strong network of supportive friends
Regular involvement in a faith community
ok: A previous suicide attempt
A firearm in the home
The recent death of a spouse

items.q: A client is admitted with opioid withdrawal. Which findings should the nurse expect? Select all that apply.
items.x: Opioid withdrawal causes yawning, rhinorrhea, mydriasis and aches. Pinpoint pupils and respiratory depression point to opioid toxicity.
opts: Frequent yawning
Runny nose and watery eyes
Dilated pupils
Muscle aches
Pinpoint pupils
Slow, shallow breathing
ok: Frequent yawning
Runny nose and watery eyes
Dilated pupils
Muscle aches

items.q: Which communication techniques are therapeutic? Select all that apply.
items.x: Restating, reflecting and silence encourage the client to talk. Advice, false reassurance and why-questions block communication.
opts: Restating what the client said
Reflecting the client's feelings
Using silence
Giving advice
Offering false reassurance
Asking why questions
ok: Restating what the client said
Reflecting the client's feelings
Using silence

items.q: The nurse is assessing a child for possible abuse. Which findings should raise concern? Select all that apply.
items.x: Immersion burns, patterned bruising and inconsistent histories suggest abuse. Shin bruises and birthmarks are normal findings.
opts: Burns in a stocking or glove pattern
Bruises in different stages of healing on the back
An injury that does not match the history given
Bruises on the shins of an active 5-year-old
Blue-gray birthmarks on the lower back
ok: Burns in a stocking or glove pattern
Bruises in different stages of healing on the back
An injury that does not match the history given

items.q: A client is admitted for alcohol withdrawal. Which findings should the nurse expect? Select all that apply.
items.x: Alcohol withdrawal causes autonomic hyperactivity, including tremor, diaphoresis, tachycardia and anxiety.
opts: Tremors
Sweating
Rapid pulse
Anxiety
Slow pulse
Pinpoint pupils
ok: Tremors
Sweating
Rapid pulse
Anxiety

items.q: A client is in an acute manic episode. Which interventions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Low stimulation, portable nutrition and consistent limits help. Competition and long discussions increase stimulation.
opts: Provide a calm, low-stimulus environment
Offer high-calorie finger foods
Set firm, consistent limits
Encourage competitive group games
Encourage long, detailed group discussions
ok: Provide a calm, low-stimulus environment

Hold the arms and legs still
Give oral fluids

items.q: A client with an acute asthma attack was wheezing loudly. Now the chest is quiet and the client is too breathless to talk. What does this mean?
items.x: A silent chest means almost no airflow and signals impending respiratory failure.
items.a: Little air is moving through narrowed airways
w: The attack is resolving
The client is resting comfortably
The bronchodilator has fully worked

items.q: A client with COPD and chronic CO2 retention has an SpO2 of 86% on room air. Which action is best?
items.x: Clients with COPD need oxygen for hypoxemia; it is titrated to a prescribed target, often 88 to 92%.
items.a: Give oxygen titrated to the prescribed target
w: Withhold oxygen to avoid suppressing breathing
Give 100% oxygen by non-rebreather mask
Have the client breathe into a paper bag

items.q: A client with a chest injury has severe dyspnea, absent breath sounds on the right, and tracheal shift to the left. What should the nurse anticipate?
items.x: Tracheal deviation away from the affected side with absent sounds suggests tension pneumothorax, which needs immediate decompression.
items.a: Emergency needle decompression
w: An upper GI series
A sputum culture
Chest physiotherapy and postural drainage

items.q: A client with sickle cell disease is admitted in vaso-occlusive crisis. Which intervention is the priority?
items.x: Hydration and pain relief are first; cold causes vasoconstriction and worsens sickling.
items.a: IV fluids and pain management
w: Cold packs on painful joints
Limit oral fluids
Encourage strenuous exercise

items.q: A client with appendicitis suddenly reports that the pain is gone, then develops a rigid abdomen and fever. What does this suggest?
items.x: Sudden relief followed by peritoneal signs suggests rupture and peritonitis.
items.a: Perforation of the appendix
w: Resolution of inflammation
Response to pain medicine
Constipation from narcotics

items.q: A client with cirrhosis is confused and has a flapping tremor of the hands. Which lab value should the nurse review?
items.x: Asterixis and confusion are signs of hepatic encephalopathy, associated with elevated ammonia.
items.a: Serum ammonia
w: Serum amylase
Serum troponin
Serum lipase

items.q: A client after chest trauma has a falling BP, distended neck veins and muffled heart sounds. Which condition should the nurse suspect?

w: Left-sided heart failure
Hypovolemic shock
Pulmonary edema

items.q: A client with left-sided heart failure would most likely have which finding?

w: Distended neck veins and ascites
Weight gain from leg edema only
Enlarged liver

items.q: A client with peripheral arterial disease reports leg pain while walking. Which finding is expected?

Pain that is relieved by elevating the legs
Deep, irregular ulcers above the inner ankle

items.q: A client with myasthenia gravis has trouble swallowing and a weak cough. What is the nurse's priority?

Provide eye drops for dry, irritated eyes
Teach energy conservation

items.q: A client with Guillain-Barre syndrome has weakness spreading up from the legs. Which assessment is the priority?

Bowel sounds
Skin integrity on the heels and sacrum

items.q: A child arrives drooling, with a high fever and sitting forward with the mouth open. What should the nurse avoid?

w: Keeping the child calm on a parent's lap
Preparing intubation equipment
Giving humidified oxygen

items.q: A client in labor has a prolapsed umbilical cord. What should the nurse do first?

Have the client ambulate
Apply warm compresses to the cord

Normal labor
Braxton Hicks contractions

Apply warm blankets
Give an antipyretic

IV fluids
Pain management
High-fat meals
Encourage alcohol for relaxation
Monitor blood glucose
ok: NPO status initially

Pain management
Monitor blood glucose

Give anticoagulation as prescribed
Monitor for bleeding

High-pitched bowel sounds early

Cramping abdominal pain

Hyperkalemia
Fluid overload

Hyperkalemia
Fluid overload

items.q: The nurse finds an adult unresponsive in the hallway with no normal breathing. Put in order.

Obtain a noncontrast head CT

ok: Assess airway, breathing and circulation
Check the blood glucose
Obtain a noncontrast head CT

Reassess breathing and peak flow

Give a short-acting bronchodilator as prescribed

Begin CPR if unresponsive
ok: Ask if the child is choking
Give abdominal thrusts

items.q: The practical nurse is assigned four clients on a medical unit. Which client should the nurse see first after receiving report?
items.x: A falling oxygen saturation is an airway and breathing problem and takes priority. The other findings are stable or expected and can wait briefly.

A client with heart failure who gained 0.5 lb since yesterday's weight
A client two days after knee surgery who reports pain of 4 out of 10

items.q: The practical nurse is working with an unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP). Which task is appropriate for the nurse to delegate to the UAP?
items.x: Routine vital signs on a stable client are within UAP scope. Teaching, data collection on an unstable client and medication administration require a licensed nurse.
items.a: Obtaining vital signs on a client who has stable chronic heart failure
w: Reinforcing discharge teaching for a client going home on warfarin
Collecting data on a client who just returned from a cardiac catheterization
Giving a scheduled oral medication to a client who is sleeping

items.q: A client scheduled for surgery asks the practical nurse what the surgeon will be removing and says the surgeon never explained it. What should the nurse do?
items.x: Informed consent is the provider's responsibility. The nurse reports that the client does not understand so the provider can explain before consent is signed.
items.a: Notify the registered nurse or surgeon that the client needs more information before signing consent
w: Explain the surgical procedure in detail so the client can sign the consent form
Have the client sign the form because the surgeon will answer questions in the preoperative area
Tell the client that most people feel nervous and the procedure is routine

items.q: The practical nurse finds that a scheduled medication was given to the wrong client by another nurse. After checking on the client, what is the nurse's next action?
items.x: Client safety comes first, then the error is reported to the charge nurse and provider and an incident report is filed. The incident report is not mentioned in the medical record.
items.a: Notify the charge nurse and provider and file an incident report
w: Document in the client's chart that an incident report was completed
Talk with the other nurse privately and agree to watch the client closely
Wait to see whether the client develops any adverse effects before reporting

items.q: A client with a terminal illness tells the practical nurse that they do not want cardiopulmonary resuscitation. No advance directive is on the chart. What should the nurse do?
items.x: A code status change requires a provider order. The nurse advocates by reporting the client's wishes so the provider can discuss and document them.
items.a: Report the client's wishes to the registered nurse and provider
w: Write a do-not-resuscitate order in the chart because the client stated this clearly
Tell the client that the family must agree before any decision is made
Remind the client that resuscitation is required for all hospitalized clients

items.q: The practical nurse overhears two staff members discussing a client's HIV status in the cafeteria line. What is the best action?

Report the staff members directly to the state board of nursing

Refuse the entire assignment until a different one is created

items.a: A resident who is suddenly confused and has a new fever of 101.8 F (38.8 C)

A resident who ate 50% of breakfast and 75% of lunch

items.q: A client who is alert and oriented refuses a prescribed dressing change. What is the practical nurse's best action?

Ask a family member to convince the client to accept the dressing change

w: A newly admitted client with chest pain who needs an initial admission assessment

A client with a new tracheostomy whose oxygen saturation is falling

items.x: Health information is released only with the client's authorization. Being a relative does not grant access.

w: Give the family member the results because they are the next of kin
Read the results aloud so the family member does not have a written copy
Tell the family member to ask the unit secretary for a printout

items.q: The practical nurse receives a telephone prescription from a provider. What should the nurse do while on the phone?
items.x: Read-back of the complete order reduces transcription errors. Facility policy determines whether a practical nurse may take telephone orders.
items.a: Write it down and read it back to the provider
w: Repeat the drug name only and ask the provider to sign it later
Ask the provider to call back when a registered nurse is available
Remember the prescription and enter it after the call ends

w: Apply wrist restraints to keep the client in bed
Ask the provider for a sedative to help the client rest
Raise all four side rails on the bed

Measuring and recording intake and output

Checking a postoperative incision for signs of infection

ok: Ambulating a stable client who has done so twice today
Measuring and recording intake and output
Giving a bed bath to a client with a stable stroke

Turning the computer screen away from the hallway

Performing the initial discharge assessment and care plan

The nurse sustains a needlestick injury

Goggles
Mask

items.x: The stable post-MI client no longer needs ICU-level monitoring. The others need titrated drips, hourly checks or ventilator support.

w: A client with diabetic ketoacidosis on an insulin infusion with hourly glucose checks
A client on a norepinephrine infusion whose blood pressure is still being titrated
A client intubated yesterday for pneumonia who now needs less oxygen on the ventilator

items.q: The nurse receives report on four clients. Which client should the nurse see first?
items.x: A sudden severe headache in a client on an anticoagulant may mean intracranial bleeding, which is life-threatening. The other clients need care but are not unstable.
items.a: A client on a heparin infusion who reports a sudden, severe headache
w: A client with pneumonia who has a temperature of 38.3 C (100.9 F)
A client 1 day after knee surgery who rates pain at 6 on a 0 to 10 scale
A client with diabetes whose breakfast tray has just been delivered

items.q: The nurse is caring for a client who had a stroke yesterday and passed a bedside swallow screen. Which task can the nurse delegate to the unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP)?
items.x: Measuring intake is a routine task within UAP scope. Assessment, teaching and evaluation remain with the nurse.
items.a: Measuring and recording the client's oral intake at each meal
w: Assessing the client's ability to swallow before giving liquids
Teaching the client how to use a straw safely with thin liquids
Evaluating whether the client's speech has changed since morning

items.q: The UAP reports that a client with type 1 diabetes has a fingerstick glucose of 48 mg/dL and is sweating. What should the nurse do?
items.x: Symptomatic hypoglycemia needs prompt nursing assessment and treatment. The nurse does not delegate the response to an unstable finding.
items.a: Go to the client right away to assess and treat the low glucose
w: Ask the UAP to recheck the glucose in an hour and report back then
Tell the UAP to note the result in the chart for the next shift
Ask the UAP to give the client the next scheduled insulin dose

items.q: The charge nurse learns that two staff nurses are in an ongoing disagreement about who does more work on the shift. What is the best first action?
items.x: Bringing the parties together for open discussion is the first step in conflict resolution. Escalation is used only if this fails.
items.a: Meet with both nurses together to discuss the issue and find a solution
w: Report both nurses to human resources so the conflict is on their record
Assign the two nurses to different units until the conflict goes away
Ignore the problem, because adults should solve these issues on their own

items.q: A client's blood pressure has fallen to 82/48 mm Hg and urine output is low. The nurse has paged the provider twice in 30 minutes with no response. What should the nurse do next?
items.x: When a provider does not respond about a deteriorating client, the nurse escalates through the chain of command (or calls a rapid response) rather than waiting.
items.a: Notify the charge nurse or supervisor using the facility's chain of command
w: Keep paging the same provider every 15 minutes until a call comes back
Wait for the provider's morning rounds, since two pages have been sent
Write a note in the chart that the provider did not return the two pages

items.q: A client with heart failure has been readmitted three times in 2 months for fluid overload. Which referral is most likely to help prevent another readmission?
items.x: Frequent readmission suggests problems with self-care at home. Home health nursing can monitor weight, symptoms and adherence and report early changes.
items.a: Home health nursing to check daily weights and medicine use at home
w: Physical therapy to begin a strength program in an outpatient gym
A dietitian visit once a year to review the low-sodium meal plan
A support group that meets monthly for people with heart disease

items.q: The charge nurse assigns staff based on how sick the clients are, not on their insurance or ability to pay. Which ethical principle does this show?
items.x: Justice means fair distribution of care and resources. Fidelity is keeping promises, veracity is truthfulness and autonomy is self-determination.
items.a: Justice
w: Fidelity
Veracity
Autonomy

items.q: The nurse realizes that a note was written in the wrong client's paper chart. What should the nurse do?
items.x: Errors are corrected so the original entry stays readable, with a note of the error and the nurse's initials and date. Erasing, obscuring or removing entries is improper. Electronic records follow the facility's correction process.
items.a: Draw one line through the entry, write error, and add initials and date
w: Use correction fluid to cover the entry and write the correct note on top
Tear out the page and copy the correct entries onto a new chart page
Scribble over the entry heavily so that nobody can read it any longer

items.q: A client received IV morphine 20 minutes ago and is drowsy. The surgeon now asks the nurse to have the client sign a surgical consent form. What should the nurse do?
items.x: Valid consent requires a client who is able to understand. Sedation from an opioid can make consent invalid, so the nurse informs the surgeon rather than witnessing it.
items.a: Tell the surgeon that the client may not be able to give valid consent now
w: Have the client sign quickly before the morphine makes the client sleepier
Ask the client's adult son, who is visiting, to sign the form for the client
Sign the form as a witness and write that the client seemed a bit sleepy

items.q: A client asks to read the medical record during the hospital stay. What should the nurse do?
items.x: Clients have a legal right to access their own health information. The nurse follows facility procedure and stays available to answer questions.
items.a: Follow facility policy for client access and offer to explain any terms
w: Tell the client that medical records belong to the hospital, not clients
Tell the client that only an attorney can request to see the medical record
Give the client the record and leave the room so the client can read it alone

items.q: At the end of the shift, the controlled-substance count shows one tablet of oxycodone missing. What should the nurse do?
items.x: Controlled-substance discrepancies must be reported and resolved before the counting nurses leave. Falsifying or delaying the count is a legal violation.
items.a: Report the discrepancy before either nurse leaves, as policy requires
w: Recount the drawer tomorrow and report only if it is still not correct
Sign the count as correct, since one tablet is likely a simple miscount
Take a tablet from another drawer to make the count match for the shift

items.q: An 82-year-old client with intact decision-making capacity wants to return home alone after a fall, against the family's wishes. What should the nurse do?
items.x: A competent adult has the right to make choices others see as risky. The nurse supports autonomy while helping reduce risk.
items.a: Respect the decision and help plan for safety measures at home
w: Ask the provider to declare the client unable to make decisions
Tell the family they can override the decision since they disagree
Delay the discharge until the client agrees to go to a nursing home

items.q: Which situations does a nurse need to report to the proper authority according to state law? Select all that apply.
items.x: Suspected child or elder abuse and reportable communicable diseases must be reported. A past abortion and refusing a vaccine are private matters with no reporting duty.
opts: A child with burns that do not match the parent's story
A client with a newly confirmed case of measles
An older adult with signs of financial exploitation by a caregiver
A client who tells the nurse about a past abortion
A client who declines a recommended flu vaccine
ok: A child with burns that do not match the parent's story
A client with a newly confirmed case of measles
An older adult with signs of financial exploitation by a caregiver

items.q: The nurse is reviewing the five rights of delegation. Which are among them? Select all that apply.
items.x: The five rights of delegation are right task, circumstance, person, directions and communication, and supervision and evaluation. Route and time are rights of medication administration.
opts: Right task
Right person
Right supervision and evaluation
Right directions and communication
Right route
Right time of day
ok: Right task
Right person
Right supervision and evaluation
Right directions and communication

items.q: Which nurse actions cross professional boundaries with a client? Select all that apply.
items.x: Social contact outside care and sharing personal problems blur the therapeutic relationship. Sitting at eye level and using the preferred name are respectful care.
opts: Accepting a friend request from a client on social media
Telling a client about the nurse's own marriage problems
Meeting a current client for coffee after the shift
Sitting at eye level while talking with the client
Using the client's preferred name during care
ok: Accepting a friend request from a client on social media
Telling a client about the nurse's own marriage problems
Meeting a current client for coffee after the shift

items.q: During a disaster, the hospital must free beds quickly. Which inpatients are appropriate for early discharge? Select all that apply.
items.x: Stable clients who could finish care at home are discharged first. Clients on titrated drips or active treatment for an unstable condition stay.
opts: A client finishing oral antibiotics for cellulitis who is afebrile
A client 2 days after an uncomplicated appendectomy who is eating
A client admitted for observation after a fall with normal studies
A client on a continuous heparin infusion for a new pulmonary embolism
A client receiving a third bag of IV fluid for diabetic ketoacidosis
ok: A client finishing oral antibiotics for cellulitis who is afebrile
A client 2 days after an uncomplicated appendectomy who is eating
A client admitted for observation after a fall with normal studies

items.q: Which actions show the nurse acting as a client advocate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Advocacy protects the client's rights and understanding. Pressuring the client or signing for the client undermines autonomy.
opts: Asking the provider to explain a procedure again when the client is confused
Arranging a medical interpreter for a client who speaks limited English
Supporting a competent client's informed decision to decline a treatment
Persuading a client to agree with the family's choice of treatment
Signing a consent form for a client who is busy on the phone
ok: Asking the provider to explain a procedure again when the client is confused
Arranging a medical interpreter for a client who speaks limited English
Supporting a competent client's informed decision to decline a treatment

items.q: The emergency department nurse uses the Emergency Severity Index to triage. Which clients need immediate or emergent care? Select all that apply.
items.x: Chest pain with diaphoresis, acute stroke signs and airway compromise are high acuity. A minor sprain and a refill need few resources and can wait.
opts: A client with crushing chest pain and diaphoresis
A client with sudden slurred speech that began 30 minutes ago
A child with stridor at rest and drooling
A client with a sprained ankle who can bear some weight
A client who needs a prescription refill for blood pressure pills
ok: A client with crushing chest pain and diaphoresis
A client with sudden slurred speech that began 30 minutes ago
A child with stridor at rest and drooling

items.q: A client's condition is getting worse and the provider does not respond. Put the nurse's escalation in order. Put in order.
items.x: The chain of command moves from the direct provider through nursing leadership to medical leadership. A rapid response can be called at any point if the client is unstable.
opts: Call the client's attending provider with an SBAR report
Call the provider again after no response in the expected time
Notify the charge nurse
Notify the nursing supervisor
Contact the medical director or chief of the department
ok: Call the client's attending provider with an SBAR report
Call the provider again after no response in the expected time
Notify the charge nurse
Notify the nursing supervisor
Contact the medical director or chief of the department

items.q: A client on the medical unit becomes suddenly confused with a respiratory rate of 30/min. Put the nurse's actions in order. Put in order.
items.x: The nurse recognizes deterioration, calls for help and gives care until the team arrives. A structured hand-off and documentation follow.
opts: Recognize the change and stay with the client
Call the rapid response team
Give oxygen and support the client until the team arrives
Give the team an SBAR hand-off
Document the event and the client's response
ok: Recognize the change and stay with the client
Call the rapid response team
Give oxygen and support the client until the team arrives
Give the team an SBAR hand-off
Document the event and the client's response

items.q: The nurse is delegating a task to an unlicensed assistive personnel. Put the steps in order. Put in order.
items.x: Delegation starts with nursing assessment, then matching the task to the right person, communicating clearly, supervising and evaluating.
opts: Assess the client's stability and needs
Choose a task within the UAP's scope and skills
Give clear directions and expected results
Supervise while the task is done
Evaluate the outcome and give feedback
ok: Assess the client's stability and needs
Choose a task within the UAP's scope and skills
Give clear directions and expected results
Supervise while the task is done
Evaluate the outcome and give feedback

items.q: A client is admitted with confirmed seasonal influenza. Which precaution should the nurse use when entering the room?
items.x: Influenza spreads by large droplets, so droplet precautions with a surgical mask are used. An N95 and airborne room are for airborne diseases such as tuberculosis and measles.
items.a: Wear a surgical mask in addition to standard precautions
w: Wear a fit-tested N95 respirator and keep the door closed
Wear a gown and gloves only, since influenza spreads by touch
Use standard precautions only, because influenza is common

items.q: The nurse notices that the sharps container in a client's room is about three-quarters full. What should the nurse do?
items.x: Sharps containers are sealed and replaced at the fill line, usually about three-quarters full, to prevent needlestick injuries. Contents are never pushed down or emptied.
items.a: Seal the container and replace it with a new one per policy
w: Push the contents down to make room for a few more needles
Keep using it until the needles reach the very top opening
Empty it into a red bag and put the empty container back up

items.q: The nurse must recap a needle in an emergency because no sharps container is nearby. Which method is safest?
items.x: Recapping is avoided, but when unavoidable the one-handed scoop keeps the free hand away from the needle. Two-handed recapping and bending cause needlesticks.
items.a: Use the one-handed scoop method with the cap lying on a flat surface
w: Hold the cap in one hand and guide the needle into it with the other
Bend the needle against the bed rail before replacing the plastic cap
Ask a coworker to hold the cap steady while the needle is slid inside

items.q: A specimen tube of blood breaks and spills on the floor of a client's room. What should the nurse do after putting on gloves?
items.x: Blood spills are absorbed, then the area is cleaned with an approved disinfectant such as diluted bleach, with gloves and proper disposal of waste.
items.a: Soak up the blood with towels, then clean with an approved disinfectant
w: Wipe the floor with a dry paper towel and leave it to air dry naturally
Cover the spill with a towel and wait for housekeeping to clean it later
Rinse the area with plain water and mop it into the floor drain quickly

items.q: The nurse sees an unlicensed assistive personnel raise all four side rails on the bed of a client with dementia who is not on a restraint order. What should the nurse do?
items.x: Raising all side rails to keep a client in bed is a restraint and can increase injury when the client climbs over. Alternatives such as a low bed and frequent checks are used.
items.a: Explain that four raised rails count as a restraint and lower some of them
w: Praise the UAP, because full side rails always prevent falls from the bed
Ask the UAP to tie the call light to one rail so the client can find it
Tell the UAP to also put mitts on the client's hands to prevent climbing

items.q: A nurse finds several vials of concentrated potassium chloride stored in a medication room on a general unit. What should the nurse do?
items.x: Concentrated potassium is a high-alert drug and should not be stocked on general units. Premixed bags prevent fatal errors.
items.a: Remove the vials and report them to the pharmacy per safety policy
w: Label the vials with a bright sticker and leave them on the shelf
Move the vials to the top shelf where they are harder to reach
Use the vials first before the unit orders any premixed products

items.q: Why do some medicine labels use mixed upper- and lowercase letters, such as hydrOXYzine and hydrALAZINE?
items.x: Tall man lettering highlights the differences between look-alike drug names to prevent selection errors.
items.a: To help staff tell apart drugs with names that look alike
w: To show which drugs need a second nurse to double check
To mark drugs that must be given through a central line
To identify drugs that come only in a generic formulation

items.q: The nurse is reviewing a handwritten order. Which item should the nurse clarify because it is on the do-not-use list?
items.x: U can be misread as 0 or 4 and is on the Joint Commission do-not-use list. Writing out units and daily, and using a leading zero, are safe practices.
items.a: The letter U written to mean units
w: The word daily written out in full
A leading zero placed before a decimal
The word units written out in full

items.q: A person in scrubs without a visible badge comes to a postpartum room and says the newborn must go to the nursery for a test. What should the nurse do?
items.x: Infant abduction prevention requires that only staff with proper ID take a newborn. Scrubs alone do not prove identity.
items.a: Check for a valid hospital ID badge before releasing the newborn
w: Let the person take the baby, since the person is wearing scrubs
Ask the mother if she is comfortable and then let the person go
Walk the person to the nursery and leave the baby in the room

items.q: A visitor in a client's room begins shouting and threatening the nurse. What should the nurse do first?
items.x: The nurse protects personal and client safety by staying near an exit and calling for help. Touching or closing in an angry person can escalate the situation.
items.a: Keep a clear path to the door and call security for help
w: Close the door to keep the visitor's shouting from others
Stand close and touch the visitor's arm to calm the person
Tell the visitor firmly to leave and turn to finish the care

items.q: A nurse answers a phone call from a person who says there is a bomb in the hospital. What should the nurse do?
items.x: The nurse keeps the caller on the line and notes details such as voice, background noise and location, then follows the facility's emergency code process.
items.a: Keep the caller talking and write down every detail that is heard
w: Hang up right away and start moving all clients out of the building
Tell the caller the threat is not believed and end the call quickly
Put the caller on hold while asking the charge nurse what to do next

items.q: A bag of chemotherapy leaks onto the floor while the nurse is hanging it. What should the nurse do after securing the area?
items.x: Hazardous drug spills are cleaned with a chemotherapy spill kit, including a gown, double gloves and eye protection, and the waste goes in a hazardous drug container.
items.a: Put on protective gear from the spill kit and clean up the spill
w: Wipe the spill up with a paper towel and wash the hands after
Have housekeeping mop the area with water at the end of the shift
Cover the spill with a sheet and leave it until pharmacy arrives

items.q: A client received IV chemotherapy this morning. What should the nurse wear when emptying the client's urinal over the next 48 hours?
items.x: Many chemotherapy drugs are excreted in body fluids for about 48 hours. The nurse wears chemotherapy-tested gloves and a gown to avoid exposure.
items.a: Chemotherapy-tested gloves and a disposable impermeable gown
w: No protective gear, because urine does not carry the drug
A surgical mask only, to prevent breathing in the drug fumes
Clean exam gloves only if the urine looks dark or very bloody

items.q: The nurse is changing an infant's diaper on a raised crib mattress and needs to reach for a clean diaper on a shelf. What should the nurse do?
items.x: Infants can roll unexpectedly. The nurse keeps a hand on the infant or raises the rail before turning away.
items.a: Keep one hand on the infant while reaching for the diaper
w: Turn away quickly, since a young infant cannot roll over
Lower the side rail fully so the shelf is easier to reach
Ask the infant's sibling to watch the baby for a moment

items.q: Which action by a nurse needs correction?
items.x: Gloves used on a contaminated site must be removed and hands cleaned before touching clean areas or equipment. The other actions are correct.
items.a: Changing a soiled brief, then adjusting the IV pump in the same gloves
w: Using alcohol hand rub before entering a room to check a blood pressure
Removing gloves and cleaning the hands after emptying a urinary drain bag
Putting on clean gloves before touching the client's broken skin area

items.q: A client receiving chemotherapy develops herpes zoster with lesions spread over many parts of the body. Which precautions should the nurse use?
items.x: Disseminated zoster, or any zoster in an immunocompromised client, needs airborne and contact precautions until all lesions are dry and crusted.
items.a: Airborne and contact precautions until the lesions are crusted
w: Standard precautions only, since shingles is not contagious
Droplet precautions with a surgical mask for the first day
Contact precautions only, with a gown and gloves for care

items.q: A client is on contact precautions for vancomycin-resistant enterococcus (VRE). Which action is correct?
items.x: Dedicated equipment prevents spread of resistant organisms. A gown is removed before leaving the room, and a mask is not needed for contact precautions.
items.a: Keep a dedicated stethoscope in the room for this client's use
w: Use the unit's shared stethoscope and wipe it off after leaving
Wear a surgical mask whenever the nurse is standing near the bed
Leave the gown on when going to the next client's room for care

items.q: A tornado warning is announced for the area of the hospital. What should the nurse do for clients on the unit?
items.x: During a tornado, clients are moved away from windows to interior areas, and those who cannot be moved are covered with blankets, and blinds and curtains are closed.
items.a: Move clients away from windows and into inner hallways when possible
w: Open the windows slightly to keep air pressure equal inside the room
Take all ambulatory clients to the parking garage on the top floor
Keep clients in their rooms with the blinds open to watch the storm

items.q: Who is responsible for marking the surgical site before a procedure?
items.x: The Universal Protocol states the site is marked by the licensed practitioner performing the procedure, with the client involved when possible.
items.a: The surgeon or practitioner who will do the procedure
w: The circulating nurse during the operating room check
The admitting nurse during the preoperative checklist
The client, using a marker given at the admission desk

items.q: The nurse collects blood samples from a client for lab testing. When should the tubes be labeled?
items.x: Labeling at the bedside in the client's presence, using two identifiers, prevents wrong-client specimens.
items.a: At the bedside, in front of the client, right after collection
w: At the nurses' station once all of the samples are collected
Before going into the room, so the tubes are ready to use
In the lab, where the staff can match them to the request

items.q: The nurse is about to start a unit of packed red blood cells. Which verification process is correct?
items.x: Two qualified people verify client identity, blood product and compatibility at the bedside before transfusion to prevent a fatal ABO mismatch.
items.a: Two qualified staff check the client and blood unit at the bedside
w: One nurse checks the unit at the station and then hangs it alone
The blood bank's check is enough, so no bedside check is needed
The client's family confirms the name and blood type at bedside

items.q: Which clients need droplet precautions? Select all that apply.
items.x: Pertussis, influenza and mumps spread by droplets. Measles is airborne, and C. difficile and RSV need contact precautions.

An adult with influenza
A teenager with mumps
A child with measles (rubeola)
An adult with C. difficile diarrhea
An infant with respiratory syncytial virus

An adult with influenza
A teenager with mumps

items.q: The nurse is giving IV chemotherapy. Which actions protect the nurse from exposure? Select all that apply.
items.x: Double gloves, a fluid-resistant gown and hazardous waste disposal reduce exposure. Tubing is primed with a non-drug solution, and PPE is not reused.

Wearing a disposable gown that resists fluid
Placing used tubing in a hazardous drug waste container
Priming the IV tubing with the chemotherapy drug
Wearing the same gown to the next client's room
ok: Wearing two pairs of chemotherapy-tested gloves
Wearing a disposable gown that resists fluid
Placing used tubing in a hazardous drug waste container

items.q: Which actions help prevent needlestick injuries? Select all that apply.
items.x: Safety devices, immediate disposal and not overfilling containers prevent injuries. Two-handed recapping and bending needles cause them.
opts: Activating the needle's safety device right after use
Placing the used needle in a sharps container right away
Replacing sharps containers when they reach the fill line
Recapping needles with two hands before throwing them out
Bending used needles so they will fit in the container
ok: Activating the needle's safety device right after use
Placing the used needle in a sharps container right away
Replacing sharps containers when they reach the fill line

items.q: Which measures help prevent infant abduction on a maternity unit? Select all that apply.
items.x: Matching bands, badge checks and electronic tags help prevent abduction. Posting names and leaving the baby alone increase risk.
opts: Using matching ID bands for the mother and newborn
Teaching parents to give the baby only to staff with the right badge
Using an electronic security tag on the newborn
Posting the baby's name and room number on the door
Leaving the baby alone in the room while the mother showers
ok: Using matching ID bands for the mother and newborn
Teaching parents to give the baby only to staff with the right badge
Using an electronic security tag on the newborn

items.q: Which actions follow the Universal Protocol to prevent wrong-site surgery? Select all that apply.
items.x: The Universal Protocol includes pre-procedure verification, site marking by the operator and a time-out. The time-out is never skipped.
opts: Verifying the procedure and site with the client before surgery
Having the person doing the procedure mark the site
Doing a time-out with the whole team just before the incision
Having the circulating nurse mark the site in the operating room
Skipping the time-out when the surgeon is in a hurry
ok: Verifying the procedure and site with the client before surgery
Having the person doing the procedure mark the site
Doing a time-out with the whole team just before the incision

items.q: Which actions reduce the risk of workplace violence for the nurse? Select all that apply.
items.x: Keeping an exit path, getting help early and using a calm approach reduce risk. Turning away or meeting alone in a closed room increases danger.
opts: Staying between an agitated client and the door
Calling security early when a person makes threats
Speaking in a calm, low voice with a client who is angry
Turning one's back on an agitated client to give space
Meeting alone with a known violent client in a closed room
ok: Staying between an agitated client and the door
Calling security early when a person makes threats
Speaking in a calm, low voice with a client who is angry

items.q: The unit must be evacuated during a fire. Put the groups of clients in the order they are usually moved. Put in order.
items.x: Ambulatory clients are moved first because they can leave quickly with guidance, then clients who need help, then those who are bedbound and finally those who need the most staff and equipment.
opts: Clients who can walk on their own
Clients who need a wheelchair or help to walk
Clients who are bedbound
Clients on life support who need special help to move
ok: Clients who can walk on their own
Clients who need a wheelchair or help to walk
Clients who are bedbound
Clients on life support who need special help to move

items.q: The nurse is cleaning up a small blood spill. Put the steps in order. Put in order.
items.x: Protective gear comes first, then the blood is absorbed, and the area is disinfected for the full contact time before final cleanup and disposal.
opts: Put on gloves and other needed protective gear
Soak up the blood with disposable towels
Apply an approved disinfectant to the area
Leave the disinfectant on for the required contact time
Wipe the area and discard waste in a biohazard bag
ok: Put on gloves and other needed protective gear
Soak up the blood with disposable towels
Apply an approved disinfectant to the area

items.x: Hand hygiene comes first. The bare hand touches only the inside of the first glove, and the gloved hand touches only the outside of the second.
opts: Perform hand hygiene
Open the glove package on a clean, dry surface
Pick up the first glove by the folded inside cuff and put it on
Slide the gloved fingers under the cuff of the second glove and put it on
Adjust the fingers of both gloves, touching only sterile surfaces
ok: Perform hand hygiene
Open the glove package on a clean, dry surface
Pick up the first glove by the folded inside cuff and put it on
Slide the gloved fingers under the cuff of the second glove and put it on
