items.q: A pregnant client's last menstrual period began on June 10. Using Naegele's rule, what is the estimated date of birth?
items.x: Naegele's rule: add 7 days to the first day of the last period, subtract 3 months and add 1 year. June 10 becomes March 17.
items.a: March 17 of the following year
w: March 3 of the following year
September 17 of this same year
April 10 of the following year

items.q: A client at 14 weeks of gestation asks how the provider knows for sure she is pregnant. Which finding is a positive sign of pregnancy?
items.x: Positive signs come only from the fetus, such as fetal heart sounds or visualization on ultrasound. A pregnancy test and uterine changes are probable signs, and skin changes are presumptive.
items.a: Fetal heart sounds heard with a Doppler device
w: A positive urine pregnancy test at the clinic
Darkening of the skin on the face and abdomen
Softening of the lower uterine segment on exam

items.q: A client at 30 weeks of gestation reports painful leg cramps at night. What should the nurse teach?
items.x: Dorsiflexing the foot with the knee straight stretches the calf muscle and relieves the cramp.
items.a: Straighten the leg and pull the toes up toward the knee
w: Point the toes down firmly until the cramp goes away
Massage the calf hard with the knee bent all the way
Walk briskly on the toes until the cramping stops

items.q: A client at 34 weeks of gestation lying flat for an exam becomes dizzy and pale, and her blood pressure drops. What should the nurse do?
items.x: Supine hypotension is caused by the uterus pressing on the inferior vena cava. A left lateral position relieves the pressure and restores blood return.
items.a: Turn the client onto her left side
w: Raise the head of the exam table
Have the client sit up and lean forward
Elevate the legs with the client supine

items.q: At 1 minute after birth, a newborn has a heart rate of 110/min, slow irregular breathing, some flexion of the arms and legs, a grimace with suction, and a pink body with blue hands and feet. What is the Apgar score?
items.x: Heart rate over 100 scores 2; slow irregular breathing 1; some flexion 1; grimace 1; pink body with blue extremities 1. The total is 6.

items.q: Parents ask how to care for their newborn's umbilical cord stump at home. What should the nurse teach?
items.x: Dry cord care is recommended. Folding the diaper down keeps urine off the stump. Sponge baths are used until it falls off.
items.a: Keep the stump clean and dry and fold the diaper below it
w: Clean the stump with alcohol after every single diaper change
Cover the stump with a tight bandage until it falls off fully
Give the baby a full tub bath each day to help it fall off

items.q: The nurse is assessing a newborn at 18 hours of age. Which finding should the nurse report to the provider?
items.x: Jaundice in the first 24 hours is pathologic and needs evaluation. Acrocyanosis, milia and a stork bite are normal.
items.a: Yellow skin and sclera seen at 18 hours after birth
w: Bluish hands and feet while the baby's body is pink
Small white bumps across the bridge of the nose
A flat red patch at the nape of the baby's neck

items.q: A parent asks about a newborn's circumcision 1 day after the procedure. Which finding is expected?
items.x: A yellowish exudate is part of normal healing and should not be wiped off. Active bleeding, no urine and purulent drainage are reported.
items.a: A yellowish film over the glans that forms during healing
w: Bright red bleeding that soaks through more than one diaper
No wet diaper in the 12 hours since the circumcision was done
A foul-smelling green drainage coming from the tip of the penis

items.q: The nurse is examining a healthy 9-month-old. Which finding should be reported?
items.x: The Moro reflex normally disappears by about 6 months, so persistence at 9 months needs evaluation. A positive Babinski is normal until about age 2, and sitting and stranger anxiety are expected.
items.a: The Moro (startle) reflex is still present
w: The Babinski reflex shows fanning of toes
The infant sits alone without any support
The infant shows clear fear of strangers

items.q: A parent says a 2-year-old has temper tantrums when told no. Which approach should the nurse suggest?
items.x: Tantrums are normal for toddlers seeking autonomy. Staying calm, keeping the child safe and not rewarding the behavior works best.
items.a: Make sure the child is safe and ignore the tantrum calmly
w: Give the child the item so the tantrum ends more quickly
Spank the child so the tantrum does not happen again
Explain the reasons in detail until the child calms down

items.q: A 4-year-old is upset after blood is drawn from the arm. Which action by the nurse is most helpful?
items.x: Preschoolers fear body injury and mutilation. A bandage reassures them that the body is intact.
items.a: Put a colorful bandage on the puncture site
w: Leave the site uncovered so it heals in air
Explain in detail how blood cells are made
Tell the child that big kids do not cry

items.q: Which activity is best for a hospitalized 9-year-old who is on bed rest?
items.x: School-age children are in Erikson's industry stage and enjoy completing projects and games with rules. The other activities suit infants or toddlers, or are not possible on bed rest.
items.a: Building a model kit or playing a board game
w: Stacking soft blocks and a shape sorter toy
Playing peek-a-boo with a parent at the bed
Pushing a toy lawn mower around the room

items.q: The nurse is doing a health history for a 15-year-old client who came with a parent. What should the nurse do?
items.x: Teens are more likely to disclose risk behaviors in private. Confidential time is a standard part of adolescent care.
items.a: Spend part of the visit talking with the teen alone
w: Ask all questions with the parent in the room
Have the parent answer the questions for the teen
Skip questions about sex, drugs and mood at this age

items.q: A 4-month-old is due for routine vaccines and has a runny nose and a temperature of 37.8 C (100 F). What should the nurse do?
items.x: A mild illness with or without low-grade fever is not a contraindication to vaccination. Delaying leaves the infant unprotected.
items.a: Give the vaccines as scheduled, since a mild illness is not a reason to wait
w: Reschedule the vaccines until the infant has had no fever for a full week
Give only the oral rotavirus vaccine today and the rest in two weeks
Give the vaccines only after the provider orders a chest X-ray first

items.q: A parent asks when the HPV vaccine is routinely recommended. What should the nurse say?
items.x: The HPV vaccine is routinely given at 11 to 12 years for all genders and works best before any exposure to the virus.
items.a: At age 11 to 12, though it can be started as early as age 9
w: Only after a teen becomes sexually active for the first time
At age 18, when the child is old enough to make the choice
Only for girls, at the time of the first cervical cancer screen

items.q: A client with an egg allergy that causes hives asks whether she can have a flu shot. What should the nurse say?
items.x: Current CDC guidance says people with egg allergy can receive any age-appropriate influenza vaccine without extra precautions beyond those for any vaccine.
items.a: Yes, any flu vaccine suited to her age and health can be given
w: No, people with an egg allergy can never receive a flu vaccine
Only after a skin test with the vaccine shows no reaction to it
Only in a hospital intensive care unit with a provider present

items.q: A pregnant client at 28 weeks of gestation asks why she needs a Tdap vaccine when she had one 3 years ago. What should the nurse say?
items.x: Tdap is recommended in every pregnancy, ideally between 27 and 36 weeks, so maternal antibodies protect the newborn from pertussis.
items.a: It is given in each pregnancy so antibodies pass to protect the baby
w: It is given only because the earlier vaccine has stopped working
It protects the mother from tetanus during the birth process alone
It is not needed, since the prior dose still protects her newborn

items.q: Which client should the nurse identify as eligible for yearly low-dose CT lung cancer screening?
items.x: Screening is recommended for adults 50 to 80 with at least a 20 pack-year history who smoke now or quit within the past 15 years.
items.a: A 58-year-old who smoked a pack a day for 25 years and quit 5 years ago
w: A 45-year-old who has smoked a few cigarettes on weekends for 10 years
A 70-year-old who smoked a pack a day for 20 years and quit 30 years ago
A 62-year-old who has never smoked but lived with a smoker as a child

items.q: A 68-year-old man who smoked for 30 years asks which screening test is recommended for his age and history. What should the nurse tell him?
items.x: Men 65 to 75 who have ever smoked are advised to have one ultrasound to screen for abdominal aortic aneurysm.
items.a: A one-time abdominal ultrasound to check for an aortic aneurysm
w: A yearly chest X-ray to check for any new aortic enlargement
A yearly cardiac stress test to look for heart artery disease
A one-time carotid ultrasound to check the neck for narrowing

items.q: Which client should the nurse identify as having a contraindication to a combined estrogen-progestin birth control pill?
items.x: Smoking at age 35 or older with combined hormonal contraceptives greatly raises the risk of stroke, heart attack and blood clots.
items.a: A 38-year-old who smokes a pack of cigarettes each day
w: A 22-year-old with heavy, painful menstrual periods
A 30-year-old with mild acne on the face and back
A 26-year-old who has never been pregnant before

items.q: A healthy 78-year-old says he rarely feels thirsty and drinks little during the day. What should the nurse teach?
items.x: The thirst sense declines with age, raising the risk of dehydration. Scheduled fluids during the day help, while limiting late evening fluids reduces nighttime trips.
items.a: Drink fluids on a schedule rather than waiting to feel thirsty
w: Drink only when thirsty, since the body knows what it needs
Drink most fluids right before bed to keep hydrated at night
Replace water with coffee, which counts toward fluid needs

items.q: A client at 39 weeks of gestation calls the clinic. Which findings suggest true labor? Select all that apply.

Contractions that continue when she walks around
Pain that starts in the lower back and moves to the front
Contractions that go away after she rests and drinks water
Discomfort felt only in the lower abdomen and groin
ok: Contractions that get closer together and stronger over time
Contractions that continue when she walks around
Pain that starts in the lower back and moves to the front

items.q: The nurse is teaching a postpartum client about warning signs after discharge. Which signs should be reported right away? Select all that apply.

A severe headache with blurred vision

Lochia that changes from red to pink by day 5
Breast fullness on the third day after birth

A severe headache with blurred vision
Pain, warmth and swelling in one calf

items.q: Which clients have a contraindication to the live measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine? Select all that apply.

A client with an allergy to eggs
A breastfeeding mother of a 2-month-old
ok: A client who is 10 weeks pregnant
A client receiving chemotherapy for leukemia
A client with prior anaphylaxis to neomycin

items.q: Which milestones should the nurse expect in a healthy 6-month-old? Select all that apply.
items.x: Rolling, tripod sitting and babbling appear by about 6 months. Cruising, pincer grasp and first words come around 9 to 12 months.

Babbles with consonant sounds

Picks up a raisin with thumb and finger
Says two or three words with meaning
ok: Rolls from front to back and back to front
Sits with support or leaning on the hands
Babbles with consonant sounds

items.q: The nurse is teaching a client who plans to become pregnant. Which instructions should the nurse include? Select all that apply.

Avoid all alcohol once trying to conceive

Eat raw fish and soft cheeses to boost protein

Avoid all alcohol once trying to conceive

items.q: The nurse is teaching parents about protecting children from sun damage. Which instructions are correct? Select all that apply.

Plan outdoor play at midday when the sun is strongest

Use a broad-spectrum sunscreen with SPF 30 or higher

items.q: Put the stages and phases of labor in order. Put in order.

Formal operational

Preoperational

items.q: The nurse is performing Leopold maneuvers. Put them in order. Put in order.
items.x: The maneuvers move from the fundus, to the sides, to the presenting part, then assess descent into the pelvis.

items.q: A client with Alzheimer disease becomes restless, agitated and confused every evening. Which action is best?
items.x: Sundowning is reduced by low stimulation, adequate light and a predictable routine. Noise, complex tasks and new surroundings worsen confusion.
items.a: Keep a calm, quiet setting and a regular evening routine
w: Turn on the TV loudly to keep the client awake and alert
Give the client a long list of tasks to stay busy at night
Move the client to a new room each night for a fresh view

items.q: A client with antisocial personality disorder asks the nurse for extra phone time, saying, "You're the only nurse here who really gets me." What should the nurse do?
items.x: Clients with antisocial personality disorder may use flattery to manipulate. Firm, consistent limits applied by all staff are the best approach.
items.a: Restate the unit rules calmly and apply them the same as for others
w: Give the extra phone time to build trust with this particular client
Tell the client the other nurses do not like him and to be careful
Avoid talking with the client at all so the flattery has no effect

items.q: A client with somatic symptom disorder talks about stomach pain at every contact although tests are normal. Which approach is best?
items.x: The nurse accepts the symptoms as real to the client but limits focus on them and explores feelings and coping. Dismissing or reinforcing the symptoms is not helpful.
items.a: Acknowledge the discomfort, then shift the talk toward feelings
w: Tell the client that the pain is all in the mind and not real
Spend most of each visit discussing the pain in great detail
Promise to ask the provider for more tests to find the cause

items.q: A client with major depression has stayed in bed for 3 days. Which activity should the nurse plan first?
items.x: Simple, brief, noncompetitive activities with support suit the low energy and concentration of depression. Success builds from small tasks.
items.a: A short walk on the unit with the nurse
w: A competitive card game with peers
Leading the morning group meeting
A two-hour art class in the day room

items.q: A client with schizophrenia says, "I went to the store, the sky is blue and my dog has fleas, so the TV is broken." How should the nurse document this speech?
items.x: Loose associations are shifts between unrelated ideas. Echolalia is repeating words, clang associations link words by sound and neologisms are made-up words.
items.a: Loose associations
w: Echolalia
Clang associations
Neologisms

items.q: A client in a manic episode tells the nurse, "I am the owner of this hospital and I will fire you." Which response is best?
items.x: With grandiose delusions, the nurse presents reality briefly and does not argue or play along.
items.a: "I am your nurse, and you are a client here today."
w: "Which other hospitals do you own besides this one?"
"You are lying, and you know very well it is not true."
"I will tell my manager to give you a raise."

items.q: A family arrives at the emergency department after their house burned down. No one was injured. Which action by the nurse is most helpful first?
items.x: Crisis intervention focuses on the immediate problem and basic needs. Long-term issues and teaching come later.
items.a: Help the family find a safe place to stay tonight
w: Explore what childhood losses the family has had
Teach the family how to install smoke detectors
Ask the family to fill out a mental health survey

items.q: A client who is in an abusive relationship decides to return home. Which teaching about a safety plan is most important?
items.x: A safety plan prepares for a quick exit with documents, money, keys and phone numbers. Confronting the partner or isolating raises risk.
items.a: Keep a packed bag with key papers, money and keys in a safe place
w: Confront the partner calmly about the abuse once back at home again
Tell no one about the abuse so the partner does not get angry again
Wait until the next incident before making any plan to leave

items.q: A client is brought to the emergency department after snorting cocaine. Which finding is the nurse most likely to see?
items.x: Cocaine is a stimulant that causes tachycardia, hypertension, chest pain and dilated pupils. Pinpoint pupils suggest opioids, and red eyes with appetite suggest cannabis.
items.a: Chest pain, fast heart rate and dilated pupils
w: Slow breathing, pinpoint pupils and drowsiness
Low blood pressure, slow pulse and cool skin
Calm mood, red eyes and an increased appetite

items.q: A client with long-term alcohol use is confused, has unsteady gait and abnormal eye movements. Which prescribed treatment should the nurse expect to give first?

items.a: Thiamine before any glucose-containing fluid
w: Glucose-containing fluid before any thiamine
Haloperidol to control the client's confusion
A high-protein snack to boost the client's energy

items.q: The spouse of a client with alcohol use disorder asks where to find support. Which referral is best?
items.x: Al-Anon supports adult family members and friends of people with alcohol problems. Alateen is for teens.
items.a: Al-Anon
w: Alateen
Narcotics Anonymous
Gamblers Anonymous

items.q: A client's husband died 6 weeks ago. Which finding is consistent with normal grief?
items.x: Sadness, crying and some sleep problems are normal in early grief. Inability to function, command hallucinations or ongoing denial suggest complicated grief or a psychiatric problem.
items.a: Crying when talking about him and trouble sleeping some nights
w: Not getting out of bed or eating for most of the past six weeks
Saying he hears his husband telling him to join him in death
Refusing to admit that her husband has died and set his place

items.q: A client has just died. The family asks to keep the body in the room for a few hours for religious prayers. What should the nurse do?
items.x: The nurse respects cultural and religious practices around death and accommodates them whenever possible.

w: Explain that the body must go to the morgue within the hour
Tell the family the prayers can be done at the funeral home
Ask the family to pray quietly in the chapel down the hall

items.q: A parent of a 7-year-old with ADHD says homework time always ends in a fight. What should the nurse suggest?
items.x: Children with ADHD do best with short tasks, frequent breaks, structure and a quiet space.
items.a: Break the homework into short parts with brief breaks between
w: Have the child finish all homework in one long session after dinner
Let the child do homework in front of the TV to help keep calm
Give the child homework only on weekends to avoid daily struggles

items.q: A 6-year-old with autism spectrum disorder is admitted for surgery. Which action is most helpful?
items.x: Children with autism are calmed by routine and consistency. Changes and overstimulation increase distress.
items.a: Keep the child's home routines and use the same caregivers
w: Put the child in a room near the busy nurses' station
Introduce many new staff so the child can get used to them
Change the child's schedule daily to build flexibility

items.q: A client with a phobia of elevators is starting systematic desensitization. Which description of this therapy is correct?
items.x: Systematic desensitization exposes the client to the feared situation in small steps while using relaxation. Flooding is intense, prolonged exposure.
items.a: Gradual exposure to the feared object paired with relaxation
w: Forced exposure to riding an elevator for a full hour at once
Talking about childhood events that may have caused the fear
Taking a sedative each time before using any of the elevators

items.q: A client who is on the unit voluntarily tells the nurse, "I want to leave the hospital today." What should the nurse do?
items.x: Voluntary clients may ask to leave, usually in writing, and the provider is notified to evaluate safety. State law and policy guide the process.

w: Tell the client that leaving is not allowed until the treatment is done
Lock the unit door and explain that the client must stay for 3 days
Pack the client's things and walk the client out of the unit at once

items.q: A client who cuts her forearms when upset shows the nurse new superficial cuts. What should the nurse do first?
items.x: The nurse treats the injury and responds matter-of-factly. Then the nurse explores feelings, suicide risk and safer coping.
items.a: Calmly assess and care for the wounds without showing judgment
w: Tell the client that cutting is for attention and should not happen
Put the client in seclusion for the rest of the day as a consequence
Ignore the cuts so the behavior does not get any extra attention

items.q: The nurse is assessing a client with depression for suicide risk. Which question is best?

"Do you think things will get better soon for you?"

items.q: A client with dementia tells the nurse, "Someone stole my purse!" The purse is in the closet. What is the best response?
items.x: Validating the feeling and helping search reduces distress. Arguing or confirming theft increases agitation.

w: "Nobody here steals; you just forgot where it went."

items.q: On the third day after birth, a client is tearful and says, "I cry for no reason, but I love my baby." What should the nurse do?

Ask the family to take the baby home so she can rest alone for a few days
Tell her that crying will upset the baby and she should try to stay happy

items.q: A client may have taken too much of an opioid. Which findings should the nurse expect? Select all that apply.

items.q: A client who drinks heavily stops drinking. Put the alcohol withdrawal findings in the order they usually appear. Put in order.

Delirium tremens

items.q: The nurse is applying a cold pack to a client's sprained ankle. Which action is correct?
items.x: A cloth barrier and limited time of about 15 to 20 minutes prevent cold injury to the skin. Cold, not heat, is used in the first 24 to 48 hours.

items.q: A client who had hemorrhoid surgery is prescribed sitz baths. What should the nurse teach?

items.q: The nurse is giving a bed bath. How should the nurse clean the client's eyes?

Clean the rectal area first, then use the same cloth for the urethra

items.q: A client receiving warfarin asks the nurse for help shaving. Which razor should the nurse use?

A safety razor with soap

items.q: The nurse is caring for a client's dentures. Which action is correct?

Clean them over the bare sink and store them in an unlabeled cup by the bedside

Give the client a sleeping pill so the CPAP will not be needed

items.q: A client is on a clear liquid diet. Which item should the nurse offer?

Cream soup
Orange juice with pulp

items.q: A client with celiac disease is choosing lunch. Which choice shows understanding of the diet?
items.x: Celiac disease requires avoiding gluten from wheat, barley and rye. Rice, plain meats and vegetables are gluten-free.
items.a: Grilled chicken with rice and steamed carrots
w: Turkey sandwich on whole wheat bread and an apple
Beef barley soup with a side of saltine crackers
Spaghetti with meatballs and a small green salad

items.q: A client had a partial gastrectomy and has cramping, sweating and a fast heart rate soon after meals. What should the nurse teach?
items.x: Dumping syndrome is reduced by small, low-sugar meals with protein and fat, fluids between meals, and lying down after eating to slow gastric emptying.
items.a: Eat small meals, drink fluids between meals and lie down after eating
w: Eat three large meals a day and drink plenty of fluids with each meal
Add more sugary desserts to meals to keep up energy and body weight
Walk around briskly right after each meal to help digestion go faster

items.q: A client has not voided for 8 hours after surgery and feels the urge but cannot go. What should the nurse do first?
items.x: A bladder scan is a quick, noninvasive way to confirm retention before catheterizing, and simple measures like positioning and privacy can be tried.
items.a: Use a bladder scanner to check how much urine is in the bladder
w: Insert an indwelling catheter right away to drain the full bladder
Restrict the client's fluids until the client is able to void again
Tell the client the urge will pass once the anesthesia wears off

items.q: The nurse is applying a condom catheter. Which action is correct?
items.x: Leaving space at the tip prevents irritation and backflow. Tape around the shaft can cut off blood flow, and the skin should be clean and dry.
items.a: Leave a small space between the tip of the penis and the end of the sheath
w: Wrap adhesive tape all the way around the shaft to hold the sheath firmly
Apply the sheath to a penis that is still wet from cleaning to help it seal
Roll the sheath on tightly so there is no space left at the tip at all

items.q: An older client who has not had a bowel movement in 6 days now has small amounts of liquid stool leaking. What does the nurse suspect?
items.x: Oozing liquid stool after days without a bowel movement is a classic sign of fecal impaction. The nurse assesses and reports.
items.a: A fecal impaction with liquid stool passing around it
w: A new infection with C. difficile causing diarrhea
A normal bowel pattern that needs no further care
An allergy to a new food served at recent meals

items.q: A client returned from lumbar spinal fusion surgery. How should the nurse turn the client?
items.x: Log rolling moves the body as one unit so the spine does not twist after surgery.
items.a: Log roll the client with help, keeping the spine straight
w: Have the client pull on the side rail to twist onto the side
Raise the head of the bed fully before turning the client
Turn the shoulders first and then the hips a minute later

items.q: The nurse is doing passive range-of-motion exercises for a client. Which action is correct?
items.x: Joints are moved slowly and smoothly to the point of resistance. Forcing past pain can injure tissue.
items.a: Move each joint only to the point of resistance, not pain
w: Push each joint past the point of pain to stretch it more
Move the joints quickly to finish the exercises sooner
Exercise only the client's strong side to prevent strain

items.q: A client who is on bed rest for several weeks is at risk for footdrop. Which action helps prevent it?
items.x: Supporting the feet in dorsiflexion prevents plantar flexion contracture. Tight sheets push the feet into footdrop.
items.a: Use foot boots or high-top sneakers to keep the feet at a right angle
w: Keep the feet pointed down by tucking the top sheet tight over the toes
Place a pillow under the knees all day to keep the legs bent up more
Leave the feet free with no support so the client can move them alone

items.q: A client with advanced dementia cannot report pain. How should the nurse assess pain?
items.x: Clients who cannot self-report are assessed with a validated behavioral tool such as the PAINAD scale, which scores breathing, sounds, facial expression, body language and consolability.
items.a: Use a behavioral pain scale that looks at face, sounds and body movement
w: Use a 0 to 10 number scale and ask the client to pick a number for pain
Assume no pain is present unless the client says so in clear words
Ask only the family how much pain the client has had in the past week

items.q: A 5-year-old needs a dressing change. Which nonpharmacologic measure should the nurse use?
items.x: Distraction such as blowing bubbles helps preschoolers cope and also encourages slow breathing. Parents' presence and honesty help too.
items.a: Have the child blow bubbles during the dressing change
w: Explain the steps of wound healing in medical terms
Leave the parent out of the room so the child is calm
Tell the child that it will not hurt at all this time

items.q: A client is using a transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS) unit for back pain. What should the nurse teach?
items.x: TENS pads go on clean, intact skin near the pain. Pads are not placed over the front of the neck, broken skin or used in water.
items.a: Place the pads on clean, intact skin around the painful area
w: Place the pads over the front of the neck to block more pain
Use the unit while in the bath to help the current work better
Place the pads on broken skin to get the current closer to nerves

items.q: A client near the end of life breathes through the mouth and has dry lips. Which comfort measure should the nurse use?
items.x: Moist oral swabs and lip balm keep the mouth comfortable. Large sips may cause aspiration, and lemon-glycerin dries the mouth.
items.a: Give mouth care with moist swabs and apply a lip moisturizer
w: Give large sips of water through a straw every few minutes
Leave the mouth alone so the client is not disturbed at all
Use lemon-glycerin swabs several times each hour on the lips

items.q: A client who is dying has noisy, gurgling breathing that upsets the family. Which nursing action is most appropriate?
items.x: Side-lying positioning helps secretions drain. Deep suctioning is distressing and often not effective, and extra fluid can increase secretions.
items.a: Turn the client onto the side and explain the sound to the family
w: Suction deeply through the nose every hour to clear the secretions
Give the client large amounts of IV fluid to thin the secretions
Lay the client flat on the back with the head of the bed down low

items.q: The nurse is caring for a client who cannot speak after a stroke. Which findings may show pain? Select all that apply.

White rice
Green beans
Bananas
Oranges
Baked potatoes

White rice
Green beans

items.q: The nurse is caring for a client in the last days of life. Which comfort measures are appropriate? Select all that apply.

Keeping the mouth and lips moist
Allowing family to stay at the bedside

items.q: A client has nausea after chemotherapy. Which nonpharmacologic measures can the nurse suggest? Select all that apply.

Lie flat right after eating each meal

items.q: A client with moisture-associated skin damage from incontinence is being cared for. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.

Apply a moisture barrier cream to the area

ok: Clean the skin gently soon after each episode
Apply a moisture barrier cream to the area
Use a pH-balanced, no-rinse skin cleanser

items.q: The nurse is giving a complete bed bath. Put the body areas in the order they are washed. Put in order.

Perineal area
ok: Eyes and face

items.q: A client has taken amiodarone for 8 months. Which new finding should the nurse report promptly?
items.x: Amiodarone can cause pulmonary toxicity, which shows as new cough and dyspnea. It needs prompt evaluation.
items.a: A dry cough with shortness of breath on exertion
w: A mild headache that goes away with acetaminophen

Mild nausea when the dose is taken without food

items.q: A client is starting dabigatran for atrial fibrillation. Which instruction should the nurse give?
items.x: Dabigatran capsules break down with moisture, so they stay in the original container. Opening them greatly increases absorption and bleeding risk.
items.a: Keep the capsules in the original bottle and swallow them whole
w: Move the capsules to a weekly pill box to help remember each dose
Open the capsules and sprinkle them on food if they are hard to swallow
Store the capsules in the refrigerator to keep them working longer

items.q: A client is prescribed insulin lispro with meals. When should the nurse give it?
items.x: Lispro is rapid-acting, with onset in about 15 minutes, so it is given just before or right with a meal to prevent hypoglycemia.
items.a: Within about 15 minutes before the client starts eating
w: One hour before the meal tray arrives on the unit
Only at bedtime, regardless of when meals are eaten
Two hours after the meal when the glucose has peaked

items.q: A client who takes glipizide says, "I've been skipping lunch to lose weight." Which adverse effect should the nurse discuss?
items.x: Sulfonylureas stimulate insulin release regardless of food intake, so skipped meals can cause hypoglycemia.
items.a: Low blood glucose, because the drug keeps releasing insulin
w: High blood glucose, because the body has less food to use
Weight gain, because skipping meals slows the metabolism
Kidney stones, because less food means more concentrated urine

items.q: A client is starting empagliflozin for type 2 diabetes. Which instruction should the nurse include?
items.x: SGLT2 inhibitors cause glucose in the urine, raising the risk of genital yeast infections and urinary tract infections. Hydration is encouraged.
items.a: Keep the genital area clean and report burning with urination
w: Take the drug only on days when the blood glucose is above normal
Limit water intake to avoid making too much urine during the day
Expect to gain weight during the first few months of the therapy

items.q: A client taking weekly semaglutide reports severe upper abdominal pain that spreads to the back, with vomiting. What should the nurse do?
items.x: Severe abdominal pain radiating to the back can signal pancreatitis, a serious adverse effect of GLP-1 receptor agonists. The provider must be told right away.
items.a: Notify the provider promptly, since this may be pancreatitis
w: Tell the client this is a normal effect that will fade in time
Suggest an antacid and recheck the client's pain in one day
Advise the client to take the next injection with a big meal

items.q: A client who started lisinopril 6 weeks ago has a dry, tickling cough that keeps the client awake. What should the nurse do?
items.x: A persistent dry cough is a common adverse effect of ACE inhibitors from bradykinin buildup. The provider may switch to another drug class.
items.a: Report the cough to the provider, who may change the medicine
w: Tell the client to take an extra dose when the cough is worse
Teach the client that the cough means the drug is working well
Advise the client to switch to a family member's cough syrup

items.q: A client taking clonidine for hypertension says, "I sometimes skip a few days when I feel fine." What should the nurse teach?
items.x: Abruptly missing clonidine can cause dangerous rebound hypertension. It is taken daily and tapered only as the provider directs.
items.a: Taking it every day matters, since missed doses can cause rebound high BP
w: Skipping a few days is fine as long as the client feels well at the time
Taking two doses together later makes up for any days that were missed
Missing doses is safe, since the drug stays in the body for many weeks

items.q: The nurse is preparing to give IV phenytoin. Which action is correct?
items.x: Phenytoin precipitates in dextrose, so it is given with normal saline only. It is given slowly to prevent hypotension and dysrhythmias.
items.a: Flush the line with normal saline before and after the drug
w: Mix the drug with dextrose 5% in water to dilute it first
Push the drug through the same line as a glucose infusion
Give the drug rapidly so that it reaches the brain faster

items.q: A client taking ciprofloxacin reports new pain and swelling at the back of the heel. What should the nurse do?
items.x: Fluoroquinolones can cause tendinitis and tendon rupture, most often of the Achilles tendon. The provider must be told and the tendon rested.
items.a: Report it promptly and advise the client to rest the leg
w: Encourage jogging to stretch out the tight heel tendon
Apply a heating pad and tell the client it is normal
Suggest the client take the next dose with milk instead

items.q: A client is prescribed metronidazole for a C. difficile infection. Which instruction is most important?
items.x: Metronidazole with alcohol can cause a disulfiram-like reaction with flushing, vomiting and a fast heart rate. Alcohol is avoided during and for a few days after therapy.
items.a: Avoid all alcohol during therapy and for a few days after
w: Take the drug with a glass of wine to reduce stomach upset
Expect the urine to turn bright green while taking the drug
Double the next dose if one dose is missed during the day

items.q: A client received IV naloxone for opioid overdose and is now awake with a respiratory rate of 16/min. What should the nurse do next?
items.x: Naloxone often wears off before the opioid does, so respiratory depression can return. Close monitoring is needed.
items.a: Keep monitoring breathing, since sedation can return when naloxone wears off
w: Discharge the client home now that the breathing rate is back to normal
Give the client the next scheduled opioid dose for pain relief right away
Leave the client unmonitored to rest, because the overdose is now reversed

items.q: A client with chronic pain takes a prescription opioid that contains acetaminophen. Which teaching is most important?
items.x: Acetaminophen is found in many combination products. Taking more than one can exceed the safe daily limit and cause liver injury.
items.a: Read labels on cold and flu products, since many also contain acetaminophen
w: Take extra acetaminophen tablets whenever the pain is worse than usual
Acetaminophen is safe in any amount, since it is sold without a prescription
Drink alcohol with the medicine to help the client sleep through the pain

items.q: A client starting zolpidem for insomnia asks about side effects. Which effect should the nurse teach the client to report?
items.x: Zolpidem can cause complex sleep behaviors such as sleepwalking and sleep driving, which can be dangerous and must be reported.
items.a: Doing activities while asleep, such as walking or driving
w: Falling asleep within about 30 minutes after taking it
Feeling rested the next morning after a full night's sleep
Having a dry mouth in the morning after waking up early

items.q: A client has taken haloperidol for several years. Which finding should the nurse report?
items.x: Involuntary movements of the mouth and tongue suggest tardive dyskinesia, which can become permanent. The AIMS is used to monitor.
items.a: Repeated lip smacking and tongue thrusting movements
w: A steady weight with a normal appetite at each meal
A calm mood with fewer voices heard during the day
Mild dry mouth that improves with sips of cool water

items.q: A 20-year-old client is starting sertraline for depression. Which instruction is most important?
items.x: Antidepressants carry a boxed warning for increased suicidal thinking in young adults, especially early in treatment. Full effect takes weeks.
items.a: Report any new or worse thoughts of suicide right away
w: Expect the depression to lift fully within the first day
Take the drug only on days when the mood feels very low
Take it with an over-the-counter St. John's wort product

items.q: A client is being considered for bupropion to help quit smoking. Which history should the nurse report to the provider?
items.x: Bupropion lowers the seizure threshold and is contraindicated in clients with seizure disorders or eating disorders.
items.a: A seizure disorder
w: Seasonal allergies
Mild osteoarthritis
A past appendectomy

items.q: A client taking desmopressin for diabetes insipidus has a headache, confusion and a weight gain of 2 kg in 2 days. What should the nurse do?
items.x: Desmopressin causes water retention, which can lead to dilutional hyponatremia with headache, confusion and weight gain.
items.a: Check the serum sodium and report the findings to the provider
w: Encourage the client to drink more water to relieve the headache
Give the next dose early to help the kidneys make more urine
Teach the client that these are expected signs the drug works

items.q: A postpartum client has a prescription for methylergonovine for uterine atony. Her blood pressure is 162/104 mm Hg. What should the nurse do?
items.x: Methylergonovine causes vasoconstriction and is contraindicated in hypertension and preeclampsia. The provider must be told before it is given.
items.a: Notify the provider before giving the dose because of the high BP
w: Give the dose as ordered, since bleeding is the bigger problem
Give the dose by IV push to make it work faster on the uterus
Give the dose and recheck the client's blood pressure tomorrow

items.q: A client with angina who uses sublingual nitroglycerin asks about taking sildenafil. What should the nurse say?
items.x: PDE-5 inhibitors with nitrates can cause life-threatening hypotension. The client needs to discuss this with the provider.
items.a: Taking them together can cause a severe drop in blood pressure

Sildenafil will help the nitroglycerin relieve chest pain faster
Sildenafil can be used freely, since it does not affect the heart

items.q: A client has an insulin glargine pen that has been opened and is being used. How should it be stored?

In a hot car glove box so it is always available when the client needs it
In the refrigerator door forever, with no limit on how long it can be used

items.q: A client with ascites is scheduled for a paracentesis. What should the nurse do right before the procedure?

items.q: Several liters of fluid were removed during a client's paracentesis an hour ago. Which finding should the nurse report?

items.q: A client had a cardiac catheterization through the right radial artery. Which finding should the nurse report right away?

items.q: A client is scheduled for a pharmacologic stress test with regadenoson. What should the nurse teach?

items.q: A client with new shortness of breath and leg swelling has a B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) level far above normal. Which condition does this support?

Asthma attack
Kidney stone

Encourage the client to eat more leafy greens to lower the INR now

items.q: A client's white blood cell differential shows a rise in band neutrophils. How should the nurse interpret this?

w: The client most likely has an allergic reaction now

w: Dilute urine from drinking too much water

w: Uncompensated respiratory acidosis

items.q: A client having an anxiety attack has these arterial blood gas results: pH 7.50, PaCO2 28 mm Hg and HCO3 24 mEq/L. How should the nurse interpret them?

items.a: Uncompensated respiratory alkalosis
w: Uncompensated metabolic alkalosis
Partly compensated respiratory acidosis
Fully compensated metabolic acidosis

items.q: A client's pulse oximeter on a cold finger reads 84%. The client is talking in full sentences with pink lips and no distress. What should the nurse do first?
items.x: Cold extremities reduce blood flow and can cause a falsely low reading. The nurse checks the client and gets an accurate reading before acting.
items.a: Assess the client and recheck with a probe on the earlobe or forehead
w: Start high-flow oxygen through a nonrebreather mask right away now
Call a rapid response for severe low oxygen in the client at once
Document the reading of 84% and recheck it again at the next round

items.q: A client has a Jackson-Pratt drain after surgery. The bulb is fully round and not compressed. What should the nurse do?
items.x: A JP drain works by gentle suction only when the bulb is compressed. A full, round bulb has lost suction.
items.a: Empty the bulb, squeeze it flat and close the port to restore suction
w: Leave the round bulb alone, since this means the drain is working well
Pull the drain out a short way to see whether it will start to drain
Attach the bulb to wall suction set to high to empty it more quickly

items.q: A client has a double-lumen sump nasogastric tube to low suction. Where should the blue air vent (pigtail) be kept?
items.x: Keeping the vent above the stomach prevents gastric contents from backing up into it. The vent is never clamped.
items.a: Above the level of the client's stomach
w: Clamped shut to keep the suction strong
Tucked under the pillow next to the head
Connected to the suction tube with a cap

items.q: A client had a permanent pacemaker placed today through the left upper chest. Which instruction should the nurse give?
items.x: Limiting arm movement on the device side for several weeks lets the leads attach without moving out of place.
items.a: Avoid raising the left arm above the shoulder until cleared
w: Move the left arm in big circles each hour to stop stiffness
Sleep on the left side to keep pressure on the new device
Lift heavy grocery bags with the left arm starting tomorrow

items.q: The provider is about to insert a subclavian central venous catheter. How should the nurse position the client?
items.x: Trendelenburg fills and distends the veins and raises the pressure in them, which lowers the risk of air embolism during insertion.
items.a: In Trendelenburg position with the head turned away from the site
w: In high Fowler position with the head turned toward the site used
In left side-lying position with the knees drawn up to the chest
In prone position with both arms raised up above the head level

items.q: A client with a PICC line in the right arm reports aching. Which finding should the nurse report?
items.x: An increase in arm circumference with aching suggests deep vein thrombosis in the arm, a known PICC complication.
items.a: The right upper arm is 3 cm larger around than at insertion
w: The PICC dressing was changed 5 days ago and is dry and intact
The PICC flushes easily and has a good blood return when drawn
The external length of the catheter is unchanged since placement

items.q: A client after a head injury opens the eyes only to pain, uses inappropriate words and pulls away from painful stimuli. What is the Glasgow Coma Scale score?
items.x: Eye opening to pain scores 2, inappropriate words 3 and withdrawal from pain 4, for a total of 9.

items.q: During the preoperative interview, a client says, "I take ginkgo every day for my memory." What should the nurse do?
items.x: Ginkgo has antiplatelet effects and can raise bleeding risk during surgery. The surgical team must know about all supplements.
items.a: Report it to the surgeon, since ginkgo can increase bleeding risk
w: Tell the client herbal products are safe and need not be reported
Document it only, since herbal products do not affect surgery
Tell the client to take a double dose the morning of surgery

items.q: A client had a right carotid endarterectomy this morning. Which finding should the nurse report right away?
items.x: New one-sided weakness on the side opposite the surgery suggests a stroke and is an emergency.
items.a: New weakness of the left arm and a drooping left face
w: Mild soreness at the right side of the neck incision
A blood pressure of 128/74 mm Hg after returning
Mild hoarseness that the client says is unchanged

items.q: A client on peritoneal dialysis at home calls the clinic. Which report needs prompt evaluation?
items.x: Cloudy effluent with abdominal pain is the classic sign of peritonitis, the most serious complication of peritoneal dialysis.
items.a: The drained fluid looks cloudy and the abdomen is tender
w: The drained fluid is clear and pale yellow in the bag
The fill takes about 10 minutes to run into the belly
The client feels slightly full while the fluid dwells

items.q: A client had a cystoscopy this morning. Which finding should the nurse report to the provider?
items.x: Pink urine, mild burning and frequency are expected after cystoscopy. Bright red blood with clots and retention are not.
items.a: Bright red urine with clots and trouble passing the urine
w: Pink-tinged urine during the first few times of voiding
Mild burning when voiding for the rest of the first day
Needing to void more often than usual during the first day

items.q: A client is 4 hours after abdominal surgery. Which findings suggest internal bleeding? Select all that apply.

A falling blood pressure
New restlessness and anxiety
Warm, dry, pink skin
Urine output that stays steady
ok: A heart rate rising from 84 to 120/min
A falling blood pressure
New restlessness and anxiety

items.q: A client is scheduled for a cardiac catheterization. Which data should the nurse check before the procedure? Select all that apply.

Serum creatinine and kidney function

Use of anticoagulants or metformin
Total cholesterol level from last year
The date of the client's last eye exam

Serum creatinine and kidney function
Time of the client's last food and drink
Use of anticoagulants or metformin

items.q: A client has a serum potassium of 2.8 mEq/L. Which findings should the nurse expect? Select all that apply.
items.x: Hypokalemia causes weakness, cramps, U waves and slowed bowel function. Peaked T waves are seen in hyperkalemia.
opts: Muscle weakness and leg cramps
U waves on the ECG
Decreased bowel sounds
Tall, peaked T waves
Hyperactive deep tendon reflexes
ok: Muscle weakness and leg cramps
U waves on the ECG
Decreased bowel sounds

items.q: A client with diabetes is having a CT scan with IV contrast. Which actions help protect the kidneys? Select all that apply.
items.x: Checking kidney function, hydrating and managing metformin reduce risk. Fluid restriction and NSAIDs can worsen kidney injury.

Giving IV fluids as prescribed
Asking whether the client takes metformin
Limiting fluids for a day after the scan
Giving an NSAID for pain after the scan

Asking whether the client takes metformin

items.q: A client has a serum magnesium level well below normal. Which findings should the nurse expect? Select all that apply.
items.x: Low magnesium increases nerve and muscle excitability and can cause dysrhythmias. Lost reflexes and flushing are signs of high magnesium.

Hyperactive deep tendon reflexes
Heart rhythm changes
Loss of deep tendon reflexes
Flushing and a feeling of warmth
ok: Tremors and muscle twitching
Hyperactive deep tendon reflexes
Heart rhythm changes

items.q: Which arterial blood gas values are within the normal range for an adult? Select all that apply.
items.x: Normal values are pH 7.35 to 7.45, PaCO2 35 to 45 mm Hg, HCO3 22 to 26 and PaO2 80 to 100 mm Hg.
opts: PaCO2 40 mm Hg
Bicarbonate of 24
PaO2 60 mm Hg
ok: PaCO2 40 mm Hg
Bicarbonate of 24

items.q: The nurse is removing a nasogastric tube. Put the steps in order. Put in order.
items.x: Flushing clears the tube, and breath-holding closes the airway to prevent aspiration while the tube is removed.
opts: Check the order and explain the procedure
Flush the tube with air or water and remove the tape
Ask the client to take a deep breath and hold it
Pull the tube out steadily and smoothly
Offer mouth care
ok: Check the order and explain the procedure
Flush the tube with air or water and remove the tape
Ask the client to take a deep breath and hold it
Pull the tube out steadily and smoothly
Offer mouth care

items.q: A client arrives in the post-anesthesia care unit. Put the nurse's first assessments in order. Put in order.
items.x: Post-anesthesia assessment follows ABCs, then neurologic status, then the surgical site and comfort.
opts: Airway patency
Breathing and oxygen saturation
Circulation and vital signs
Level of consciousness
Surgical site and pain
ok: Airway patency
Breathing and oxygen saturation
Circulation and vital signs
Level of consciousness
Surgical site and pain

items.q: The nurse is removing an indwelling urinary catheter. Put the steps in order. Put in order.
items.x: The balloon must be fully deflated before removal. Then the nurse records output and watches for urinary retention.
opts: Check the order and identify the client
Empty the balloon fully with a syringe
Gently pull out the catheter
Measure the urine in the drainage bag
Monitor for the first void within about 6 to 8 hours
ok: Check the order and identify the client
Empty the balloon fully with a syringe

items.q: An adult has partial- and full-thickness burns over the entire front of the trunk and the entire right arm. Using the rule of nines, what percent of the body is burned?
items.x: The anterior trunk is 18% and one entire arm is 9%, for a total of 27%.

items.q: A client with a new T2 spinal cord injury is admitted. Which set of findings suggests neurogenic shock?
items.x: Loss of sympathetic tone below the injury causes vasodilation and unopposed vagal activity: hypotension, bradycardia and warm, dry skin.
items.a: Low blood pressure with a slow heart rate and warm, dry skin
w: Low blood pressure with a fast heart rate and cool, clammy skin
High blood pressure with a slow heart rate and a pounding headache
High blood pressure with a fast heart rate and flushed, sweaty skin

items.q: A client with sepsis is on 100% oxygen by nonrebreather mask, but the oxygen saturation stays at 82% and the chest X-ray shows white-out in both lungs. Which condition should the nurse suspect?
items.x: Low oxygen that does not improve with high oxygen, plus bilateral infiltrates after an insult like sepsis, is typical of ARDS.
items.a: Acute respiratory distress syndrome
w: Spontaneous tension pneumothorax
An acute asthma exacerbation
Simple left-sided heart failure

items.q: A client with several broken ribs has a section of chest wall that moves in when the client breathes in and out when the client breathes out. How should the nurse document this?
items.x: In flail chest, a free-floating segment moves opposite to the rest of the chest wall, impairing ventilation.
items.a: Paradoxical chest movement from a flail chest
w: Normal chest expansion after a rib injury
Symmetric chest rise with deep breathing
Barrel chest from long-standing lung disease

items.q: A client with an inferior myocardial infarction and right ventricular involvement has a BP of 84/50 mm Hg and clear lungs. Which prescribed treatment should the nurse expect?
items.x: The right ventricle depends on preload. Fluids support output, while nitrates, diuretics and morphine can drop the blood pressure sharply.
items.a: An IV normal saline bolus to support preload
w: Sublingual nitroglycerin to lower the preload
IV furosemide to pull extra fluid off the lungs
IV morphine to reduce the preload and the pain

items.q: A client has new-onset atrial fibrillation that has lasted several days. Which complication is the nurse most concerned about?
items.x: In atrial fibrillation, the atria do not contract well, so blood pools and clots can form and travel to the brain.
items.a: A stroke from a clot formed in the atria
w: A sudden rise in serum potassium level
Kidney stones from slowed blood flow
A heart rate that drops to below 40/min

items.q: A client is in ventricular tachycardia with a pulse, a BP of 70/40 mm Hg and confusion. Which treatment should the nurse prepare for?
items.x: Unstable VT with a pulse is treated with synchronized cardioversion. Defibrillation is for pulseless rhythms.
items.a: Synchronized cardioversion
w: Unsynchronized defibrillation
Carotid sinus massage
Transcutaneous pacing

items.q: During a code, the monitor shows asystole, confirmed in two leads. What should the nurse expect the team to do?
items.x: Asystole is not a shockable rhythm. Treatment is CPR, epinephrine and finding reversible causes.
items.a: Continue high-quality CPR and give epinephrine as prescribed
w: Defibrillate right away and then resume chest compressions
Give synchronized cardioversion at the lowest energy setting
Pause compressions for one minute to see if a rhythm returns

items.q: A client with hypertension reports sudden, severe tearing pain in the chest that moves to the back. Which finding supports the suspected diagnosis?
items.x: Aortic dissection causes tearing pain radiating to the back and can cause unequal pulses or blood pressures between the arms.
items.a: A large difference in blood pressure between the two arms
w: Pain that gets better when the client leans forward a bit
Pain that came on slowly and was relieved by an antacid
A rash in a band on one side of the chest and the back

items.q: A client had a stroke affecting the left side of the brain. Which finding should the nurse expect?
items.x: The left hemisphere controls language in most people and the right side of the body, so aphasia and right-sided weakness are expected. Left neglect and impulsivity suggest a right hemisphere stroke.
items.a: Trouble speaking or understanding words
w: Weakness of the left arm and left leg
Ignoring things on the left side of space
Impulsive behavior with poor judgment

items.q: A client is admitted with suspected bacterial meningitis. Which finding should the nurse expect?
items.x: Fever, headache and nuchal rigidity, along with positive Kernig and Brudzinski signs, are classic meningitis findings.
items.a: Neck stiffness with pain when the head is bent forward
w: A slow, gradual headache that eases when lying flat
Weakness that starts in the feet and moves upward
Tremor of the hands at rest that eases with movement

items.q: A client with multiple sclerosis asks how to prevent symptom flares. What should the nurse teach?
items.x: Heat slows nerve conduction in damaged nerves and can worsen MS symptoms. Cooling measures help.
items.a: Avoid hot baths, saunas and becoming overheated
w: Take long hot showers to keep the muscles loose
Exercise hard in hot weather to build up strength
Keep the house warm to prevent the muscles from cramping

items.q: A client with cirrhosis and known esophageal varices begins vomiting large amounts of bright red blood. What is the nurse's priority?
items.x: Massive bleeding from varices puts the client at high risk for aspiration, so airway protection comes first, along with IV access and calling for help.
items.a: Protect the airway by raising the head of the bed and having suction ready
w: Give the client ice chips to sip slowly so the bleeding vessels will shrink
Insert a nasogastric tube right away so the blood can be measured each hour
Place the client flat on the back so blood flow to the brain stays normal

items.q: A client reports pain in the right upper abdomen that started after a fatty meal and spreads to the right shoulder. Which condition should the nurse suspect?
items.x: Right upper quadrant pain after fatty meals, radiating to the right shoulder or scapula, is typical of gallbladder inflammation.
items.a: Acute cholecystitis
w: Acute appendicitis
Diverticulitis flare
Peptic ulcer perforation

items.q: A client is admitted with renal colic from a kidney stone. Which instruction should the nurse give?
items.x: Straining urine allows the stone to be analyzed so future stones can be prevented. Fluids and walking help the stone pass.
items.a: Strain all urine and save any stones that are found
w: Limit fluid intake so the stone does not move along
Stay in bed until the stone passes out on its own time
Flush any stones that pass down the toilet right away

items.q: A client with untreated hypothyroidism is admitted with myxedema coma. Which findings should the nurse expect?
items.x: Myxedema coma slows metabolism, causing hypothermia, bradycardia, hypoventilation and decreased consciousness.
items.a: Low body temperature, slow heart rate and slow breathing
w: High fever, fast heart rate and severe restlessness
Low blood pressure with fruity breath and deep breathing
Hand spasms, tingling lips and a positive Chvostek sign

items.q: A client with Cushing syndrome is admitted. Which lab finding should the nurse expect?
items.x: Excess cortisol raises blood glucose and sodium and lowers potassium. It also tends to raise the white cell count.
items.a: High blood glucose
w: Low blood sodium
High potassium level
Low white cell count

items.q: An 84-year-old client from a nursing home has pneumonia. Which finding may be the first sign of the infection in this client?
items.x: Older adults often have blunted fever and cough, and new confusion or falls may be the earliest sign of infection.
items.a: New confusion or a sudden change in behavior
w: A high fever over 40 C (104 F) with chills
A productive cough with thick green sputum
Sharp chest pain with each deep breath in

items.q: A 9-month-old has periods of severe crying with the knees drawn up and a stool that looks like red currant jelly. Which condition should the nurse suspect?
items.x: Intussusception causes episodic abdominal pain and stools mixed with blood and mucus, described as currant jelly.
items.a: Intussusception
w: Pyloric stenosis
Hirschsprung disease
Gastroesophageal reflux

items.q: A 7-month-old has had vomiting and diarrhea for 2 days. Which finding suggests significant dehydration?
items.x: A sunken fontanel and little or no urine output are signs of moderate to severe dehydration in an infant.
items.a: A sunken anterior fontanel and no wet diaper in 8 hours
w: A flat anterior fontanel and six wet diapers a day
Moist mouth with tears present when the infant cries
Capillary refill under 2 seconds and alert behavior

items.q: An hour after birth, the nurse finds the client's uterus soft and boggy with heavy bleeding. What should the nurse do first?
items.x: Uterine atony is the most common cause of postpartum hemorrhage. Fundal massage helps the uterus contract and is the first action.
items.a: Massage the fundus until it is firm
w: Place the client in high Fowler position
Insert an indwelling urinary catheter
Give the client fluids by mouth to drink

items.q: A client has right-sided heart failure. Which findings should the nurse expect? Select all that apply.
items.x: Right-sided failure backs blood up into the venous system, causing JVD, dependent edema and hepatomegaly. Pulmonary findings are typical of left-sided failure.
opts: Jugular vein distention
Swelling of the feet and ankles
An enlarged, tender liver
Pink, frothy sputum
Crackles from pulmonary edema as the main sign
ok: Jugular vein distention
Swelling of the feet and ankles
An enlarged, tender liver

items.q: A client with sepsis may have disseminated intravascular coagulation. Which findings support this? Select all that apply.
items.x: DIC uses up clotting factors and platelets, causing bleeding, low platelets, low fibrinogen and prolonged PT and aPTT.
opts: Oozing blood from IV sites
Petechiae and bruising
A falling platelet count
A rising fibrinogen level
A shorter than normal PT
ok: Oozing blood from IV sites
Petechiae and bruising
A falling platelet count

items.q: A client with a head injury has rising intracranial pressure. Which findings are late signs (Cushing's triad)? Select all that apply.
items.x: Cushing's triad of rising systolic pressure with widened pulse pressure, bradycardia and irregular respirations is a late sign of brain herniation.
opts: Widening pulse pressure
Slow heart rate
Irregular breathing pattern
Fast heart rate
Narrowing pulse pressure
ok: Widening pulse pressure
Slow heart rate
Irregular breathing pattern

items.q: A 4-week-old infant is admitted with suspected pyloric stenosis. Which findings should the nurse expect? Select all that apply.
items.x: Pyloric stenosis causes nonbilious projectile vomiting, a palpable olive-shaped mass and a hungry infant. Bilious vomit and currant jelly stools point to other conditions.

An olive-shaped mass in the upper abdomen
Hunger right after vomiting
Green, bile-stained vomit
Stools that look like red currant jelly
ok: Projectile vomiting after feeding
An olive-shaped mass in the upper abdomen
Hunger right after vomiting

items.q: A client has hyperthyroidism. Which findings should the nurse expect? Select all that apply.
items.x: Hyperthyroidism speeds metabolism, causing heat intolerance, weight loss and tachycardia. Constipation and cold intolerance suggest hypothyroidism.
opts: Heat intolerance
Weight loss with a good appetite
Fast heart rate
Constipation
Cold intolerance
ok: Heat intolerance
Weight loss with a good appetite
Fast heart rate

items.q: A client at 33 weeks of gestation has placenta previa. Which findings should the nurse expect? Select all that apply.
items.x: Placenta previa causes painless bright red bleeding with a soft, nontender uterus. Pain and a rigid abdomen suggest placental abruption.
opts: Painless, bright red vaginal bleeding
A soft uterus that is not tender
A rigid, board-like abdomen
Dark red bleeding with severe pain
Sudden, constant abdominal pain
ok: Painless, bright red vaginal bleeding
A soft uterus that is not tender

items.q: A client arrives with burns from a house fire. Put the nurse's priorities in order. Put in order.
items.x: The burning is stopped first, then ABCs are addressed. Wounds are covered and the client is kept warm to prevent hypothermia.

Assess and secure the airway
Assess breathing and give oxygen
Start IV access and fluid resuscitation
Cover the burns with clean, dry dressings and keep the client warm

Assess and secure the airway
Assess breathing and give oxygen
Start IV access and fluid resuscitation
Cover the burns with clean, dry dressings and keep the client warm

items.q: The nurse is doing a primary survey on a trauma client. Put the steps in order. Put in order.
items.x: The primary survey follows ABCDE to find and treat life threats in order of urgency.

Breathing and ventilation
Circulation and bleeding control
Disability: brief neurologic check
Exposure while preventing heat loss
ok: Airway with cervical spine protection
Breathing and ventilation

Disability: brief neurologic check
Exposure while preventing heat loss

items.q: An AED arrives while CPR is in progress on an adult. Put the steps in order. Put in order.
items.x: The AED is turned on and pads placed with minimal pause in compressions. No one touches the client during analysis or shock, and CPR resumes right after.
opts: Turn on the AED
Attach the pads to the bare chest
Clear everyone while the AED analyzes the rhythm
Clear everyone and deliver the shock if advised
Resume CPR right away, starting with compressions
ok: Turn on the AED
Attach the pads to the bare chest
Clear everyone while the AED analyzes the rhythm
Clear everyone and deliver the shock if advised

items.q: A client tells the practical nurse, 'I am leaving this hospital right now, and nobody can make me stay.' The provider has not written a discharge order. What should the nurse do first?
items.x: An alert adult may leave against medical advice, but the RN and provider must be told at once so the risks can be explained and the form completed. Threatening or detaining the client is not legal.
items.a: Notify the RN and provider right away and stay with the client
w: Tell the client security will be called if he tries to leave
Remove the client's IV catheter so he can leave safely now
Help the client pack and walk him to the hospital exit door

items.q: The practical nurse cannot clearly read the dose on a handwritten prescription for a new medication. What should the nurse do?
items.x: An unclear order is clarified with the prescriber before any dose is given. Guessing or relying on a coworker's reading can cause a medication error.
items.a: Contact the prescriber to clarify the order before giving it
w: Give the dose most often used for that drug in adult clients
Ask another nurse to read it and give whatever dose they see
Leave the order for the next shift to sort out with pharmacy

items.q: A client with limited English is being discharged. The client's 12-year-old grandson offers to interpret while the practical nurse reinforces the discharge teaching. What should the nurse do?
items.x: A trained medical interpreter protects accuracy and privacy. Children and family members should not interpret health teaching.
items.a: Arrange for a qualified medical interpreter for the teaching
w: Let the grandson interpret, since the client trusts him most
Give the client written English instructions to read at home
Speak slowly and loudly in English and show the pill bottles

items.q: A nursing assistant reports that a client's blood pressure is 82/50 mm Hg. The client's usual reading is about 130/80. What should the practical nurse do first?
items.x: The nurse who assigns a task follows up on abnormal results. A sudden low reading needs the nurse to see the client, confirm it and report to the RN.
items.a: Go to the client, recheck the blood pressure and collect data
w: Write the reading in the chart and recheck it in four hours
Ask the assistant to recheck it with a different cuff later
Tell the assistant that home readings are often a bit lower

items.q: The practical nurse sees a nursing assistant walk out of a contact-precautions room still wearing the gown and gloves. What should the nurse do?
items.x: Immediate, direct feedback corrects the unsafe practice and limits spread of germs. Bigger steps are used only if the problem continues.
items.a: Speak to the assistant right away and review correct removal
w: Report the assistant to the director of nursing in writing
Say nothing now and bring it up at the next staff meeting
Take over all care for that client for the rest of the shift

items.q: A coworker posts a picture from the unit on social media. A client's name is visible on the whiteboard behind the coworker. What should the practical nurse do?
items.x: Any client identifier posted online is a privacy breach. It is reported through the chain of command so it can be removed and handled.
items.a: Report it to the charge nurse or supervisor as policy requires
w: Comment on the post to warn the coworker that it is not safe
Ignore it, because the client's face is not shown in the photo
Share the post with the client so the client is kept informed

items.q: At the start of a shift, the practical nurse smells alcohol on a coworker's breath and notices the coworker is unsteady. What should the nurse do?
items.x: A possibly impaired nurse is a danger to clients. The nurse reports it right away to the supervisor so the coworker is removed from care.
items.a: Report the concern to the charge nurse or supervisor at once
w: Offer to give the coworker's medications for the whole shift
Suggest that the coworker drink coffee before seeing clients
Wait to see if the coworker makes an error before reporting

items.q: A client in long-term care coughs during most meals and has lost weight this month. Which team member should the practical nurse suggest the RN involve?
items.x: Coughing with meals suggests a swallowing problem. A speech-language pathologist evaluates swallowing and recommends safe diet textures.
items.a: A speech-language pathologist to check the client's swallowing
w: A physical therapist to work on the client's walking strength
A respiratory therapist to start breathing treatments at meals
A pharmacist to look for medications that cause the weight loss

items.q: A client refuses the scheduled evening medication and says it makes him dizzy. What should the practical nurse do?
items.x: A client has the right to refuse. The nurse documents the refusal and the reason and reports it, since the dizziness may need to be addressed.
items.a: Document the refusal and reason, and report it to the RN
w: Mix the medication in applesauce so the client will take it
Tell the client he must take it because the provider said so
Leave the medication cup at the bedside in case he changes his mind

items.q: The practical nurse has these tasks at the start of the shift. Which should the nurse do first?
items.x: A client recovering from low blood sugar is the least stable and needs a recheck to confirm the glucose is rising. The other tasks can wait.
items.a: Recheck a client whose low blood sugar was treated with juice
w: Give a client the scheduled morning vitamin and stool softener
Change the linen on a client's bed after the client showers
Finish documenting care given to a client before the shift

items.q: A provider writes an order for a client to have soft wrist restraints 'as needed for agitation.' What should the practical nurse do?
items.x: Restraint orders cannot be written as needed (PRN). They must be time-limited and specific, so the order must be clarified.
items.a: Report to the RN that the order needs clarifying with the provider
w: Apply the restraints whenever the client seems a little restless
Keep the restraints on overnight so the client sleeps safely
Ask the family to sign a form allowing restraints as needed

items.q: The practical nurse is giving a handoff report to the oncoming nurse. Which actions support a safe handoff? Select all that apply.
items.x: A structured report that includes changes, pending items and time for questions prevents missed care. Report is given in a private place.
opts: Include any changes in the client's condition this shift
Mention tests that are pending and when results are due
Use a standard format such as SBAR for the report
Leave time for the oncoming nurse to ask questions
Give report in the hallway where visitors can hear
Leave out minor details the client mentioned to save time
ok: Include any changes in the client's condition this shift
Mention tests that are pending and when results are due
Use a standard format such as SBAR for the report
Leave time for the oncoming nurse to ask questions

items.q: The practical nurse is asked to witness a client's signature on a surgical consent form. Which are the nurse's responsibilities? Select all that apply.
items.x: The witness confirms identity, voluntariness and that the signature is the client's. Explaining the procedure and its risks is the surgeon's job.
opts: Confirm the identity of the client signing the form
Make sure the client is signing of their own free will
Tell the RN if the client seems confused or has questions
Explain the risks and benefits of the planned surgery
Sign as witness after the client has gone to the operating room
ok: Confirm the identity of the client signing the form
Make sure the client is signing of their own free will
Tell the RN if the client seems confused or has questions

items.q: Which actions show client advocacy by the practical nurse? Select all that apply.
items.x: Advocacy means speaking up for the client's needs and wishes. Alert clients make their own decisions.
opts: Report to the RN that a client says pain is not controlled
Request an interpreter for a client who speaks little English
Speak up when planned care conflicts with the client's wishes
Persuade an alert client to accept the care the family wants
Make care choices for an alert client to save time on the unit
ok: Report to the RN that a client says pain is not controlled
Request an interpreter for a client who speaks little English
Speak up when planned care conflicts with the client's wishes

items.q: The practical nurse calls the RN about a client whose breathing has changed. Place the parts of the SBAR call in order. Put in order.

Give the client's admitting diagnosis and relevant history
Share the vital signs and other data you collected
Say what you need, such as for the RN to see the client now

Give the client's admitting diagnosis and relevant history

Say what you need, such as for the RN to see the client now

items.q: A client in a long-term care facility is diagnosed with scabies. How should the practical nurse handle the client's bed linens?

items.a: Bag them and wash in hot water, then dry them on high heat
w: Shake them out in the room before placing them in the hamper
Wash them in cold water with the other residents' laundry
Leave them on the bed until the client finishes treatment

items.q: A client's family brings in a bedside lamp from home. The practical nurse notices the cord is frayed. What should the nurse do?

items.a: Unplug it, remove it from use and follow the facility policy
w: Wrap the frayed part with tape so the client can keep using it
Let the client use it only during the day when staff can watch
Move the lamp to the far side of the room away from the bed

items.q: A client is placed on seizure precautions. Which item should the practical nurse make sure is ready at the bedside?
items.x: Suction and oxygen help keep the airway clear after a seizure. Nothing is placed in the mouth, and restraints can cause injury.
items.a: Working suction equipment and oxygen setup ready to use
w: A padded tongue blade to place between the client's teeth
Wrist restraints to keep the client's arms still in a seizure
A pillow to place under the client's head during a seizure

items.q: The sharps container in a client's room is filled to the fill line. What should the practical nurse do?

w: Push the needles down to make room for a few more sharps
Empty it into a red trash bag and reuse the same container
Use a small cup to hold used needles until a new box arrives

items.q: A client has disseminated herpes zoster (shingles) affecting many areas of the body. Which precautions should the practical nurse use?
items.x: Disseminated zoster can spread through the air and by contact with lesions, so airborne and contact precautions are used until lesions crust.
items.a: Airborne and contact precautions along with standard ones
w: Droplet precautions only, because shingles spreads by coughing
Standard precautions only, because the lesions are covered
Contact precautions only, since it spreads only by touching

items.q: The practical nurse is about to give hydroxyzine. At the bedside, the nurse sees the label on the packet reads hydralazine. What should the nurse do?

items.q: A client with a latex allergy needs a urinary catheter inserted. Which action is most important?

items.a: Use a latex-free catheter kit and latex-free gloves for the care
w: Use a latex catheter but give the client an antihistamine first
Wear latex gloves but avoid touching the client's bare skin
Use a latex catheter and watch the client closely for a rash

items.q: The practical nurse must move a client who is heavy and cannot help from the bed to a stretcher. What is the safest method?

w: Lift the client with one other nurse using good body mechanics
Ask the client's family to help pull the client across
Slide the client by pulling on the client's arms and legs

items.q: A cleaning product is spilled in a client's bathroom. Where should the practical nurse look for information on how to handle it safely?
items.x: The Safety Data Sheet lists hazards, protective equipment and cleanup steps for each chemical used in the facility.

w: The client's medical record and the nursing care plan notes
The nearest poison control phone number on the unit wall
The medication reference book kept at the nurses' station

items.q: A client received IV chemotherapy yesterday. Which action should the practical nurse take when emptying the client's urinal?

items.a: Wear a chemotherapy-rated gown and two pairs of gloves
w: Wear a surgical mask and one pair of regular exam gloves
Wash hands after emptying it; no other protection is needed
Add bleach to the urine before pouring it into the toilet

items.q: A client is being prepared for surgery tomorrow. Which instruction should the practical nurse reinforce to lower the risk of a surgical site infection?
items.x: Shaving causes tiny cuts that let bacteria in. If hair must be removed, staff use clippers just before surgery.

w: Shave the area at home the night before the surgery is done
Apply lotion to the surgical area the morning of the surgery
Skip bathing the night before so the skin keeps its natural oils

Keep the drainage system closed and connected

Disconnect the tubing to collect a urine specimen

Raise the bag above the bladder when moving the client
ok: Keep the drainage bag below the level of the bladder
Keep the drainage system closed and connected
Give perineal care daily and after any soiling
