items.q: After IM epinephrine, a patient with anaphylaxis has persistent hives and itching, and diphenhydramine is considered. Which statements are accurate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Diphenhydramine treats urticaria and itching as an adjunct after epinephrine. It commonly causes drowsiness and dry mouth, is contraindicated in neonates, and causes tachycardia rather than bradycardia.
opts: It is an adjunct given after epinephrine, not a replacement for it
Drowsiness and dry mouth are common effects
It reverses airway swelling and hypotension faster than epinephrine
It is contraindicated in neonates and premature infants
It should be avoided because it causes bradycardia
ok: It is an adjunct given after epinephrine, not a replacement for it
Drowsiness and dry mouth are common effects
It is contraindicated in neonates and premature infants

items.q: A paramedic gives methylprednisolone to a patient with a severe asthma exacerbation per protocol. Which statements are accurate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Methylprednisolone 125 mg IV is a common protocol dose for asthma and COPD, and it raises blood glucose. It reduces inflammation over hours, so bronchodilators remain first-line for immediate relief.
opts: A typical protocol adult dose is 125 mg IV
Hyperglycemia is a common effect
It provides immediate bronchodilation within minutes
It is given alongside bronchodilators rather than instead of them
It is the first-line drug for acute wheezing
ok: A typical protocol adult dose is 125 mg IV
Hyperglycemia is a common effect
It is given alongside bronchodilators rather than instead of them

items.q: An unresponsive adult with known diabetes has a blood glucose of 38 mg/dL and an IV in place. Place the steps for giving D10 in order.
items.x: Hypoglycemia and a patent line are confirmed first because extravasation can cause tissue injury. D10 is titrated in aliquots with reassessment between doses.
opts: Confirm hypoglycemia with a glucose reading and check the IV site for patency
Verify D10 is the correct solution and spike the bag
Infuse D10 in 5-10 g (50-100 mL) aliquots
Reassess mental status and recheck blood glucose
Give additional aliquots if glucose remains low
ok: Confirm hypoglycemia with a glucose reading and check the IV site for patency
Verify D10 is the correct solution and spike the bag
Infuse D10 in 5-10 g (50-100 mL) aliquots
Reassess mental status and recheck blood glucose
Give additional aliquots if glucose remains low

items.q: A malnourished adult with chronic alcohol use is confused and ataxic with a blood glucose of 54 mg/dL. Which statements about thiamine are accurate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Thiamine treats deficiency and Wernicke encephalopathy, with 100 mg IV as the initial labeled dose, and it is given with dextrose rather than avoided. It does not raise glucose, and hypersensitivity is its serious adverse effect.
opts: It is used to treat Wernicke encephalopathy
An initial dose of 100 mg IV is consistent with the label
It is contraindicated with IV dextrose
It corrects hypoglycemia on its own
An allergic reaction during IV administration should be reported
ok: It is used to treat Wernicke encephalopathy
An initial dose of 100 mg IV is consistent with the label
An allergic reaction during IV administration should be reported

items.q: A dialysis patient who missed treatment has peaked T waves and a widening QRS. Calcium chloride is considered. Which statements are accurate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Calcium chloride stabilizes the heart in hyperkalemia with ECG changes but does not lower potassium itself. It can cause tissue necrosis with extravasation, is traditionally avoided in digoxin toxicity, and rapid push can cause bradycardia.
opts: It is indicated for hyperkalemia with ECG changes
Extravasation can cause tissue necrosis, so a patent IV is required
It lowers the serum potassium level directly
Digoxin toxicity has traditionally been a contraindication
Tachycardia is the expected effect of a rapid push
ok: It is indicated for hyperkalemia with ECG changes
Extravasation can cause tissue necrosis, so a patent IV is required
Digoxin toxicity has traditionally been a contraindication

items.q: A paramedic is considering ondansetron for a vomiting patient. Which findings should cause the paramedic to withhold it and contact medical direction? Select all that apply.
items.x: Ondansetron is contraindicated with congenital long QT and with apomorphine, and it is held for a prolonged QTc. Headache is a common effect, and motion sickness is not a contraindication.
opts: History of congenital long QT syndrome
Current use of apomorphine
Recent motion sickness
Prolonged QTc on the 12-lead ECG
Mild headache
ok: History of congenital long QT syndrome
Current use of apomorphine
Prolonged QTc on the 12-lead ECG

items.q: A paramedic is considering promethazine for nausea. Which statements are accurate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Promethazine is contraindicated under age 2 and with intra-arterial or subcutaneous injection; deep IM is preferred and IV must be diluted and slow. Burning at the site requires stopping, and sedation is a common effect.
opts: It must not be given to children under 2 years
IV doses should be diluted and given slowly
Subcutaneous injection is the preferred route
Burning or pain at the IV site is a reason to stop
It has no sedating effects
ok: It must not be given to children under 2 years
IV doses should be diluted and given slowly
Burning or pain at the IV site is a reason to stop

items.q: A paramedic is considering haloperidol for a severely agitated patient. Which findings would contraindicate it or require holding it? Select all that apply.
items.x: Haloperidol is contraindicated in Parkinson's disease and severe CNS depression, and fever with rigidity is a hold finding suggesting a serious reaction. Hallucinations and agitation are the indications.
opts: History of Parkinson's disease
Unresponsive with severe CNS depression
Auditory hallucinations
Fever with muscle rigidity after a prior dose
Pacing and shouting
ok: History of Parkinson's disease
Unresponsive with severe CNS depression
Fever with muscle rigidity after a prior dose

items.q: During an interfacility transfer, a patient in septic shock is receiving a norepinephrine infusion titrated to a MAP goal of 65 mm Hg or greater. Which findings should the flight crew act on and report? Select all that apply.
items.x: Digital ischemia, new dysrhythmias and signs of extravasation are listed reasons to stop or report norepinephrine. A MAP at goal and a modest reflex slowing of the heart rate are expected effects of the drug.
opts: Cool, mottled fingertips that were warm at departure
MAP of 70 mm Hg on the current rate
New irregular wide-complex beats on the monitor
Blanching and coolness spreading around the peripheral IV site
Heart rate slowing from 112 to 100/min as MAP improves
ok: Cool, mottled fingertips that were warm at departure
New irregular wide-complex beats on the monitor
Blanching and coolness spreading around the peripheral IV site

items.q: A septic shock patient on norepinephrine has vasopressin added at 0.03 units/min before air transport. Which adverse effects should the crew monitor for? Select all that apply.
items.x: Vasopressin can cause digital and mesenteric ischemia and hyponatremia from water retention. It has no beta effect and tends to slow the heart rate, and hyperkalemia and hypoglycemia are not typical vasopressin effects.
opts: Cyanotic, painful fingers or toes
New abdominal pain or distension
Hyperkalemia with peaked T waves
Confusion or seizure from a falling sodium
Marked tachycardia from beta-receptor stimulation
Rebound hypoglycemia
ok: Cyanotic, painful fingers or toes
New abdominal pain or distension
Confusion or seizure from a falling sodium

items.q: Phenylephrine by push dose or infusion is being considered for several hypotensive patients. In which patients would phenylephrine be a poor choice? Select all that apply.
items.x: Phenylephrine is a pure vasoconstrictor that causes reflex bradycardia and can lower cardiac output, and ventricular tachycardia is a listed contraindication. Vasodilatory hypotension from anesthesia or sedation is its main indication.
opts: Hypotension with a heart rate of 44/min
Hypotension minutes after propofol induction with a heart rate of 110/min
Cardiogenic shock with a low cardiac output
Hypotension with sustained ventricular tachycardia
Hypotension after procedural sedation in a healthy adult
ok: Hypotension with a heart rate of 44/min
Cardiogenic shock with a low cardiac output
Hypotension with sustained ventricular tachycardia

items.q: A patient in low-output cardiogenic shock with an SBP of 92 mm Hg is started on dobutamine at 2-5 mcg/kg/min before transfer. Which statements about this drug are accurate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Dobutamine is an inotrope that improves output but can cause hypotension and dysrhythmias, and it is titrated within 2-20 mcg/kg/min. It is not a vasoconstrictor and is contraindicated in HOCM.
opts: It may lower blood pressure, so BP is closely watched during titration
It is mainly a vasoconstrictor used to raise systemic vascular resistance
It can increase ventricular ectopy and tachydysrhythmias
It is the preferred agent in hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy
Its usual dose range is 2-20 mcg/kg/min, titrated to effect
ok: It may lower blood pressure, so BP is closely watched during titration
It can increase ventricular ectopy and tachydysrhythmias
Its usual dose range is 2-20 mcg/kg/min, titrated to effect

items.q: A patient with acute decompensated heart failure on a milrinone infusion is transferred to a cardiac center. Which findings should the crew report to medical control? Select all that apply.
items.x: Hypotension, ventricular dysrhythmias and falling urine output or renal function are reasons to stop milrinone and notify. Improving symptoms, good perfusion and a normal potassium are desired findings.
opts: New runs of ventricular tachycardia
SBP falling below the ordered parameter
Mild improvement in dyspnea since the infusion began
Declining urine output during transport
Warm, well-perfused extremities
Potassium within normal limits
ok: New runs of ventricular tachycardia
SBP falling below the ordered parameter
Declining urine output during transport

items.q: A patient in refractory septic shock is on an epinephrine infusion titrated within 0.05-2 mcg/kg/min. Which laboratory changes would the crew expect the drug itself to cause? Select all that apply.
items.x: Beta stimulation from epinephrine causes hyperglycemia, shifts potassium into cells and raises lactate, so lactate trends must be read with caution. Hypoglycemia and hyperkalemia are opposite to its expected effects.
opts: Rise in blood glucose
Fall in blood glucose
Fall in serum potassium
Rise in serum potassium
Rise in serum lactate
ok: Rise in blood glucose
Fall in serum potassium
Rise in serum lactate

items.q: An intubated adult has been on a propofol infusion for 3 days in the ICU before transfer. Which findings raise concern for propofol-related complications and should be reported? Select all that apply.
items.x: Unexplained acidosis, rising triglycerides, CK or lactate, and green urine with acidosis are listed reasons to stop and notify. Injection pain is a minor common effect, and target sedation and a normal lipase are reassuring.
opts: Unexplained worsening metabolic acidosis
Mild pain at the IV site when the infusion was started
Rising triglyceride level
Sedation score at the ordered target
Green urine together with acidosis
Serum lipase within normal limits
ok: Unexplained worsening metabolic acidosis
Rising triglyceride level
Green urine together with acidosis

items.q: A non-intubated patient receives a dexmedetomidine load of 1 mcg/kg over 10 min followed by an infusion for transport. Which effects should the crew anticipate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Dexmedetomidine commonly causes bradycardia and hypotension and can cause hypertension with the load; sinus arrest and AV block are serious risks. Fasciculations and hypersalivation are effects of succinylcholine and ketamine.
opts: Bradycardia
Muscle fasciculations
Hypotension during the infusion
Profuse salivation
Transient hypertension during the loading dose
Hyperkalemia
ok: Bradycardia
Hypotension during the infusion
Transient hypertension during the loading dose

items.q: A hypotensive trauma patient requires RSI, and ketamine 1-2 mg/kg IV is chosen for induction. Which effects of ketamine should the crew be prepared for? Select all that apply.
items.x: Ketamine causes hypersalivation, may cause laryngospasm, and usually raises heart rate and blood pressure, which is why it is favored in hypotension. Adrenal suppression is an etomidate effect, and malignant hyperthermia is linked to succinylcholine.
opts: Increased oral secretions
Adrenal suppression
Laryngospasm
Profound bradycardia and hypotension as the usual response
Rise in heart rate and blood pressure
Triggering of malignant hyperthermia
ok: Increased oral secretions
Laryngospasm
Rise in heart rate and blood pressure

items.q: A flight crew is planning RSI for several patients. In which patients is succinylcholine contraindicated? Select all that apply.
items.x: Burns or crush injury beyond 48-72 hours, known hyperkalemia and a personal or family history of malignant hyperthermia are contraindications. Acute injuries within the first hours and asthma are not.
opts: Large-surface-area burns sustained 5 days ago
Femur fracture from a crash 1 hour ago
Dialysis patient with a known potassium of 7.0 mEq/L
Isolated head injury from 30 minutes ago
Sibling with malignant hyperthermia under anesthesia
History of asthma
ok: Large-surface-area burns sustained 5 days ago
Dialysis patient with a known potassium of 7.0 mEq/L
Sibling with malignant hyperthermia under anesthesia

items.q: A patient is intubated with etomidate and rocuronium 1.2 mg/kg before a 90-minute flight. Which actions are appropriate after tube confirmation? Select all that apply.
items.x: Rocuronium paralysis outlasts a single etomidate dose, so sedation and analgesia must start promptly to prevent awareness under paralysis. A paralyzed patient cannot move, so lack of movement does not show adequate sedation.
opts: Start sedation promptly because etomidate wears off long before rocuronium
Delay sedation until the patient begins to move
Provide analgesia along with sedation
Use absence of movement to confirm adequate sedation
Treat unexplained tachycardia and hypertension as possible awareness
ok: Start sedation promptly because etomidate wears off long before rocuronium
Provide analgesia along with sedation
Treat unexplained tachycardia and hypertension as possible awareness

items.q: A flight crew is evaluating injured patients with suspected hemorrhage for tranexamic acid. Which patients are appropriate candidates? Select all that apply.
items.x: In trauma, tranexamic acid (1 g over 10 min, then 1 g over 8 h) is used for significant hemorrhage within 3 hours of injury. More than 3 hours since injury and subarachnoid hemorrhage are contraindications, and minor bleeding is not an indication.
opts: Hemorrhagic shock from an injury 5 hours ago
Penetrating torso wound 45 minutes ago with SBP 80 mm Hg
Suspected subarachnoid hemorrhage without other injuries
Unstable pelvic fracture 2 hours ago with tachycardia and hypotension
Stable patient with a minor forearm laceration
ok: Penetrating torso wound 45 minutes ago with SBP 80 mm Hg
Unstable pelvic fracture 2 hours ago with tachycardia and hypotension

items.q: A NSTEMI patient on a heparin infusion is transferred for catheterization. Which findings require stopping the infusion and notifying medical control? Select all that apply.
items.x: Bleeding, neurologic change and a platelet drop of 50% or more (possible HIT) are reasons to stop heparin. Minor bruising is a common effect and an in-range aPTT is the goal.
opts: New confusion with unequal pupils
Small bruise at a prior injection site
Persistent bleeding from the arterial line site
aPTT within the protocol range
Platelet count down 60% from baseline
ok: New confusion with unequal pupils
Persistent bleeding from the arterial line site
Platelet count down 60% from baseline

items.q: A stroke patient is flown to a comprehensive stroke center while the alteplase infusion runs after the bolus. Which findings require stopping the infusion and notifying the receiving physician? Select all that apply.
items.x: Neurologic decline, new headache or vomiting, angioedema and BP above 180/105 are reasons to stop alteplase and notify. A stable exam and BP under the post-lytic limit are acceptable.
opts: New severe headache with vomiting
NIHSS unchanged from the pre-infusion exam
Swelling of the lips and tongue
BP 196/112 mm Hg despite treatment
BP 168/94 mm Hg
Drop in level of consciousness
ok: New severe headache with vomiting
Swelling of the lips and tongue
BP 196/112 mm Hg despite treatment
Drop in level of consciousness

items.q: A STEMI patient at a rural hospital without PCI is being considered for tenecteplase before transfer. Which findings contraindicate tenecteplase? Select all that apply.
items.x: Prior hemorrhagic stroke, suspected aortic dissection and active internal bleeding are contraindications to fibrinolysis. Older age, controlled hypertension and remote PCI do not contraindicate it.
opts: Prior hemorrhagic stroke
Age 76 years
Tearing chest pain to the back with unequal arm blood pressures
Hypertension controlled on daily medication
Active GI bleeding
PCI performed 2 years ago
ok: Prior hemorrhagic stroke
Tearing chest pain to the back with unequal arm blood pressures
Active GI bleeding

items.q: A patient with intracerebral hemorrhage is transported on a nicardipine infusion. Which statements about the infusion are accurate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Nicardipine starts at 5 mg/h and increases by 2.5 mg/h every 5-15 min to a maximum of 15 mg/h, and it can cause reflex tachycardia. Advanced aortic stenosis is a contraindication.
opts: The usual starting rate is 5 mg/h
The maximum rate is 30 mg/h
The rate may be increased by 2.5 mg/h every 5-15 minutes
It is preferred in patients with advanced aortic stenosis
Reflex tachycardia is a recognized effect
ok: The usual starting rate is 5 mg/h
The rate may be increased by 2.5 mg/h every 5-15 minutes
Reflex tachycardia is a recognized effect

items.q: A patient in hypertensive emergency is being considered for IV labetalol. Which findings make labetalol inappropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Reactive airway disease, heart block and severe bradycardia are contraindications to labetalol. It is commonly used for severe hypertension in preeclampsia and to lower BP before thrombolysis.
opts: Active wheezing in a patient with asthma
Severe hypertension in preeclampsia at 34 weeks
Second-degree type II AV block
Acute ischemic stroke with BP above the thrombolysis limit
Heart rate of 48/min
ok: Active wheezing in a patient with asthma
Second-degree type II AV block
Heart rate of 48/min

items.q: A patient on a prolonged, high-dose nitroprusside infusion is being transferred. Which findings suggest cyanide or thiocyanate toxicity? Select all that apply.
items.x: Nitroprusside releases cyanide, so acidosis, rising lactate and confusion are reasons to stop and notify. Hyperkalemia and increasing urine output are not signs of cyanide toxicity.
opts: New confusion
Hyperkalemia
Worsening metabolic acidosis
Increasing urine output
Rising lactate level
ok: New confusion
Worsening metabolic acidosis
Rising lactate level

items.q: A patient with severe preeclampsia receiving magnesium sulfate at 2 g/h is transported to a tertiary center. Which findings are reasons to stop the infusion and notify medical control? Select all that apply.
items.x: Loss of deep tendon reflexes and RR below 12 suggest magnesium toxicity, and falling urine output lets magnesium accumulate, so each is a reason to stop and notify. Flushing, warmth and nausea are common, expected effects.
opts: Absent patellar reflexes
Flushing and a feeling of warmth
Respiratory rate of 10/min
Mild nausea
Urine output dropping sharply over the past hour
ok: Absent patellar reflexes
Respiratory rate of 10/min
Urine output dropping sharply over the past hour

items.q: A patient is flown for postpartum hemorrhage after a home delivery. Which statements about oxytocin are accurate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Oxytocin is given after delivery once a second twin is excluded, is titrated to uterine tone, and can be given 10 units IM. Rapid IV bolus causes hypotension and tachycardia.
opts: For hemorrhage, it is given after the infant is delivered and a second twin is excluded
It is contraindicated once the placenta has delivered
A rapid IV bolus can cause hypotension and tachycardia
The infusion is titrated to blood pressure rather than uterine tone
10 units IM is an accepted dose and route
ok: For hemorrhage, it is given after the infant is delivered and a second twin is excluded
A rapid IV bolus can cause hypotension and tachycardia
10 units IM is an accepted dose and route

items.q: A postpartum patient with uterine atony and ongoing hemorrhage has severe preeclampsia and a history of asthma. Which medications are reasonable options? Select all that apply.
items.x: Oxytocin, misoprostol and tranexamic acid can be used in this patient. Methylergonovine is contraindicated in hypertension and preeclampsia, and carboprost is contraindicated in asthma because of bronchospasm.
opts: Oxytocin infusion
Methylergonovine
Misoprostol
Carboprost
Tranexamic acid
ok: Oxytocin infusion
Misoprostol
Tranexamic acid

items.q: An older patient with chronic digoxin toxicity is being transferred. Which findings support giving digoxin immune Fab? Select all that apply.
items.x: Life-threatening dysrhythmias, symptomatic bradycardia and significant hyperkalemia with signs of toxicity are indications. Mild symptoms with stable vital signs or a therapeutic level do not require Fab.
opts: Ventricular dysrhythmias
Mild nausea with normal vital signs
Symptomatic bradycardia with hypotension
Digoxin level in the therapeutic range without symptoms
Potassium of 6.0 mEq/L with signs of toxicity
ok: Ventricular dysrhythmias
Symptomatic bradycardia with hypotension
Potassium of 6.0 mEq/L with signs of toxicity

items.q: An agitated, delirious patient with suspected anticholinergic toxicity is being considered for physostigmine. Which findings contraindicate it? Select all that apply.
items.x: QRS widening or TCA overdose risks asystole and seizures, and asthma is a contraindication. Dry flushed skin, mydriasis and urinary retention are anticholinergic findings that support the diagnosis.
opts: QRS widening on the ECG
Dry, flushed skin
Suspected tricyclic antidepressant co-ingestion
Dilated pupils
History of asthma
Urinary retention
ok: QRS widening on the ECG
Suspected tricyclic antidepressant co-ingestion
History of asthma

items.q: A patient with symptomatic acquired methemoglobinemia is being considered for methylene blue. Which factors would make the drug unsafe or ineffective? Select all that apply.
items.x: G6PD deficiency causes hemolysis and poor response, and serotonergic drugs risk serotonin syndrome. Low SpO2, brown blood and dapsone exposure are typical features of methemoglobinemia, not contraindications.
opts: SpO2 near 85% despite high-flow oxygen
Known G6PD deficiency
Chocolate-brown arterial blood
Daily use of a serotonergic antidepressant
Recent dapsone use as the likely cause
ok: Known G6PD deficiency
Daily use of a serotonergic antidepressant

items.q: A house-fire victim with suspected cyanide poisoning is given hydroxocobalamin 5 g IV over 15 minutes during transport. Which statements are accurate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Lactate is drawn first because the drug interferes with lab tests, red skin and urine are expected, and hypertension is common. A second 5 g dose may be given, and acidosis is a sign of cyanide toxicity, not a contraindication.
opts: A lactate level is ideally drawn before the drug is given
The 5 g dose cannot be repeated
Red discoloration of skin and urine is expected
Lactic acidosis is a contraindication
Blood pressure may rise after the infusion
ok: A lactate level is ideally drawn before the drug is given
Red discoloration of skin and urine is expected
Blood pressure may rise after the infusion

items.q: A patient with pulmonary arterial hypertension on a continuous epoprostenol infusion through a central line is transported. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Epoprostenol must never be interrupted except by PAH specialist direction, and hypotension and line infection are reported at once. Pausing or flushing the line can cause rebound crisis or a drug bolus.
opts: Keep the infusion running without interruption
Pause the infusion while loading the patient into the aircraft
Report hypotension immediately
Flush the line rapidly to check patency
Monitor for fever and signs of line infection
ok: Keep the infusion running without interruption
Report hypotension immediately
Monitor for fever and signs of line infection

items.q: An intubated patient with a severe traumatic brain injury is being flown to a neurosurgical center. Which measures help limit secondary brain injury? Select all that apply.
items.x: Hypoxia and hypotension worsen brain injury, and midline head position with elevation helps venous drainage. Routine hyperventilation causes cerebral vasoconstriction and ischemia, and hypotonic fluids worsen cerebral edema.
opts: Preventing hypoxia
Routine hyperventilation without signs of herniation
Preventing hypotension
Using hypotonic fluids such as D5W for maintenance
Keeping the head midline with the head of the bed elevated
ok: Preventing hypoxia
Preventing hypotension
Keeping the head midline with the head of the bed elevated

items.q: A 3-year-old with fluid-refractory septic shock is intubated for transfer to a pediatric ICU. Which statements about drug therapy are accurate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Epinephrine and norepinephrine are used for pediatric fluid-refractory shock, propofol is not for prolonged pediatric ICU sedation, and dexmedetomidine can cause bradycardia. Ketamine is contraindicated only under 3 months, and vasopressin is not first-line in children.
opts: An epinephrine or norepinephrine infusion is appropriate for fluid-refractory shock
Ketamine is contraindicated in all children under 3 years
Propofol is not used for prolonged pediatric ICU sedation
Vasopressin is the first-line pediatric vasopressor
Dexmedetomidine sedation can cause bradycardia
ok: An epinephrine or norepinephrine infusion is appropriate for fluid-refractory shock
Propofol is not used for prolonged pediatric ICU sedation
Dexmedetomidine sedation can cause bradycardia

items.q: Place the steps of rapid sequence intubation in a critically ill adult in order.
items.x: Oxygenation and hemodynamics are optimized first, then induction is followed at once by paralysis. Placement is confirmed before ongoing sedation and analgesia are started to prevent awareness.
opts: Preoxygenate and optimize blood pressure before induction
Give the induction agent by rapid IV push
Give the neuromuscular blocker immediately after the induction agent
Pass the tube once muscle relaxation is achieved
Confirm placement with waveform capnography and start post-intubation sedation and analgesia
ok: Preoxygenate and optimize blood pressure before induction
Give the induction agent by rapid IV push
Give the neuromuscular blocker immediately after the induction agent
Pass the tube once muscle relaxation is achieved
Confirm placement with waveform capnography and start post-intubation sedation and analgesia

items.q: A peripheral norepinephrine infusion has extravasated during transport. Place the immediate steps in order.
items.x: The infusion is stopped first, drug is aspirated through the catheter while it is still in place, and the catheter is then removed before phentolamine is infiltrated to reverse vasoconstriction.
opts: Stop the infusion at the affected site
Aspirate residual drug through the catheter
Remove the catheter
Infiltrate the area with phentolamine per protocol
ok: Stop the infusion at the affected site
Aspirate residual drug through the catheter
Remove the catheter
Infiltrate the area with phentolamine per protocol

items.q: Place the steps for giving alteplase to an adult with acute ischemic stroke in order.
items.x: Eligibility and BP control come before any drug is given; the 0.9 mg/kg dose is then split into a 10% bolus over 1 minute followed by the remaining 90% over 60 minutes, with close neuro and BP monitoring to detect hemorrhage.
opts: Confirm last known well is within the treatment window and CT shows no hemorrhage
Lower BP below 185/110 mm Hg if needed
Give 10% of the 0.9 mg/kg dose (maximum 90 mg) as an IV bolus over 1 minute
Infuse the remaining 90% over 60 minutes
Perform frequent neurologic and BP checks during and after the infusion
ok: Confirm last known well is within the treatment window and CT shows no hemorrhage
Lower BP below 185/110 mm Hg if needed
Give 10% of the 0.9 mg/kg dose (maximum 90 mg) as an IV bolus over 1 minute
Infuse the remaining 90% over 60 minutes
Perform frequent neurologic and BP checks during and after the infusion

items.q: Place the steps for managing magnesium sulfate in a patient with severe preeclampsia during transport in order.
items.x: A baseline exam allows later comparison, the loading dose precedes maintenance, and ongoing checks detect toxicity, which is treated by stopping magnesium and giving calcium gluconate.

Give the 4-6 g IV loading dose over 15-20 minutes
Start the 1-2 g/h maintenance infusion
Reassess reflexes, respiratory rate and urine output during transport
If reflexes are lost and RR is below 12, stop the infusion and give calcium gluconate 1 g IV
ok: Assess baseline deep tendon reflexes, respiratory rate and urine output
Give the 4-6 g IV loading dose over 15-20 minutes
Start the 1-2 g/h maintenance infusion
Reassess reflexes, respiratory rate and urine output during transport
If reflexes are lost and RR is below 12, stop the infusion and give calcium gluconate 1 g IV

items.q: A patient develops fever, chills and hypotension 10 minutes into a blood transfusion during an interfacility transfer. Place the actions in order.
items.x: Stopping the transfusion limits further exposure, new tubing keeps access without infusing more blood, and the patient is stabilized before notification and preserving the product for testing.
opts: Stop the transfusion
Keep the IV open with normal saline through new tubing
Assess vital signs and support airway, breathing and circulation
Notify medical control and the receiving facility
Save the blood bag and tubing for return to the blood bank
ok: Stop the transfusion
Keep the IV open with normal saline through new tubing
Assess vital signs and support airway, breathing and circulation
Notify medical control and the receiving facility
Save the blood bag and tubing for return to the blood bank

items.q: Place the steps for starting treatment of an adult in DKA before transfer in order.
items.x: Fluids are started first, and potassium is confirmed before insulin because insulin drives potassium into cells and is held when potassium is low. Frequent rechecks follow to detect hypokalemia and hypoglycemia.
opts: Begin isotonic fluid resuscitation
Confirm the serum potassium is not below the protocol threshold
Start the insulin infusion at 0.1 unit/kg/h
Recheck potassium and glucose every 1-2 hours
ok: Begin isotonic fluid resuscitation
Confirm the serum potassium is not below the protocol threshold
Start the insulin infusion at 0.1 unit/kg/h
Recheck potassium and glucose every 1-2 hours

items.q: An intubated patient with tricyclic antidepressant overdose has hypotension. Place the steps of sodium bicarbonate therapy in order.
items.x: QRS widening identifies sodium channel toxicity, and bicarbonate boluses are repeated until the QRS narrows. A maintenance infusion then follows with monitoring of pH and electrolytes.
opts: Confirm QRS widening on the 12-lead ECG
Give 1-2 mEq/kg IV push
Reassess the QRS on the ECG
Repeat boluses until the QRS narrows
Begin a maintenance infusion with ABG or VBG, sodium and potassium monitoring
ok: Confirm QRS widening on the 12-lead ECG
Give 1-2 mEq/kg IV push
Reassess the QRS on the ECG
Repeat boluses until the QRS narrows
Begin a maintenance infusion with ABG or VBG, sodium and potassium monitoring

items.q: A dialysis patient has hyperkalemia with peaked T waves and a widening QRS. Place the treatment steps in order.
items.x: Calcium is given first because it protects the heart within minutes, then insulin with dextrose shifts potassium into cells. Glucose is monitored afterward because hypoglycemia is the main risk of insulin.
opts: Recognize the ECG changes of hyperkalemia
Give calcium chloride 1 g IV slowly to stabilize the myocardium
Give IV regular insulin with 25 g dextrose to shift potassium
Monitor glucose serially for hypoglycemia
ok: Recognize the ECG changes of hyperkalemia

Give glucagon 1 mg IM
Turn her on her side with suction ready
Give glucagon 3 mg intranasally
Rub oral glucose gel on her gums
Recheck the glucose after the dose
ok: Give glucagon 0.5 mg IM
Turn her on her side with suction ready
Recheck the glucose after the dose

items.q: Fifteen minutes after IM glucagon, an adult remains unresponsive with a glucose of 41 mg/dL. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: If glucose does not rise within 15 minutes, medical direction is notified and vascular access for dextrose is pursued. Oral agents are unsafe in an unresponsive patient, and treatment is not abandoned or delayed.
opts: Notify medical direction
Give oral glucose gel
Keep trying for IV or IO access for dextrose
Assume the meter is wrong and stop
Give activated charcoal
Wait 30 minutes before rechecking
ok: Notify medical direction
Keep trying for IV or IO access for dextrose

items.q: Right after a nebulized ipratropium and albuterol treatment, a COPD patient's wheezing and shortness of breath become much worse. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Paradoxical bronchospasm is a reason to stop ipratropium and notify medical direction while supporting breathing. It is not expected, and more ipratropium is not appropriate.
opts: Stop the nebulizer treatment
Continue because this is expected
Notify medical direction
Double the next ipratropium dose
Support oxygenation and ventilation as needed
Start a second ipratropium nebulizer
ok: Stop the nebulizer treatment
Notify medical direction
Support oxygenation and ventilation as needed

items.q: A 19-year-old with asthma used her levalbuterol inhaler several times before EMS arrived. She still wheezes, speaks in short phrases, is shaky and has a pulse of 118/min. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Levalbuterol is a beta-agonist closely related to albuterol, so tremor and tachycardia are expected and do not by themselves stop bronchodilator treatment. Oxygen is not delayed until cyanosis, her home puffs must be counted, and it is not a steroid.
opts: Give oxygen only if she becomes cyanotic
Treat levalbuterol as a steroid controller
Recognize tremor and tachycardia as expected effects
Assume levalbuterol cannot raise heart rate
Ignore the puffs she took before arrival
Withhold all bronchodilators due to tremor
ok: Recognize tremor and tachycardia as expected effects

items.q: A 20-kg child with vomiting and diarrhea has dry lips and is less playful than usual. Protocol allows ondansetron ODT. Which actions are correct? Select all that apply.
items.x: Children 15-30 kg receive 4 mg ODT; 2 mg is for 8-15 kg and 8 mg exceeds this weight band. The ODT dissolves on the tongue without water, and the child's dehydration and mental status are reassessed.
opts: Give a 4 mg ODT
Give an 8 mg ODT
Give a 2 mg ODT
Let the tablet dissolve on the tongue
Have the child swallow it whole with water
Reassess hydration and mental status
ok: Give a 4 mg ODT
Let the tablet dissolve on the tongue
Reassess hydration and mental status

items.q: Thirty minutes after ondansetron 4 mg IV, a 30-year-old with gastroenteritis has a headache and feels lightheaded when sitting up. Pulse is 112/min, BP is 98/60 mm Hg and her mouth is dry. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Headache is a common ondansetron effect, while tachycardia, low BP and a dry mouth point to dehydration that is treated with IV fluid and reassessment. Naloxone, glucose and more ondansetron do not treat this, and walking risks syncope.
opts: Recognize headache as a common ondansetron effect
Give naloxone for the headache
Give IV fluid per protocol
Have her walk to the ambulance
Repeat ondansetron to treat the headache
Give oral glucose for the lightheadedness
ok: Recognize headache as a common ondansetron effect
Give IV fluid per protocol

items.q: A patient who takes several antidepressants received ondansetron for vomiting. Which findings should the AEMT report to medical direction? Select all that apply.
items.x: Dysrhythmias from QT prolongation, signs of serotonin syndrome and allergic reactions must be reported. Mild headache and constipation are common, expected effects.
opts: A new irregular rhythm
Mild headache
Palpitations with fainting
Agitation, tremor and a high temperature
Mild constipation
Hives with throat swelling
ok: A new irregular rhythm
Palpitations with fainting
Agitation, tremor and a high temperature
Hives with throat swelling

items.q: After an unknown ingestion, a 55-year-old moans only to pain and has gurgling respirations. Which medications should the AEMT avoid until the airway is protected? Select all that apply.
items.x: Oral glucose, chewed aspirin and activated charcoal must be swallowed and risk aspiration in a patient who cannot protect the airway. IM, IN and IV routes do not depend on swallowing.
opts: Oral glucose
IM glucagon
Chewed aspirin
Intranasal naloxone
Activated charcoal
IV dextrose
ok: Oral glucose
Chewed aspirin
Activated charcoal

items.q: A 30-year-old with known Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome has an irregular, wide-complex tachycardia at 230/min, BP 112/70 mm Hg, and is alert. Which medications should the paramedic avoid? Select all that apply.
items.x: AV nodal blockers such as adenosine and diltiazem are contraindicated in pre-excited atrial fibrillation because they can speed conduction down the accessory pathway. Procainamide is indicated for this rhythm, and sedation and analgesia are appropriate if cardioversion becomes necessary.
opts: Adenosine 6 mg rapid IV push
Procainamide infusion per protocol
Diltiazem 0.25 mg/kg IV
Midazolam if cardioversion is needed
Fentanyl if cardioversion is needed
ok: Adenosine 6 mg rapid IV push
Diltiazem 0.25 mg/kg IV

items.q: A 52-year-old has a regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 188/min, BP 124/78 mm Hg, and vagal maneuvers have failed. Which findings would lead the paramedic to withhold adenosine? Select all that apply.
items.x: Sick sinus syndrome (or second- or third-degree block) without a pacemaker contraindicates adenosine because of the risk of prolonged bradycardia or asystole. Aspirin use, controlled hypertension, prior SVT, age and palpitations are not contraindications.
opts: Takes a daily low-dose aspirin
Controlled hypertension on medication
Sick sinus syndrome without a pacemaker
Prior episodes of SVT
Age over 50
Palpitations and anxiety
ok: Sick sinus syndrome without a pacemaker

items.q: A 29-year-old with stable SVT receives adenosine 6 mg rapid IV push. She reports flushing and chest pressure, and the monitor shows a pause of several seconds before sinus rhythm at 92/min. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.
items.x: Brief asystole, flushing and chest pressure are common, short-lived adenosine effects, and a 12-lead of the converted rhythm is appropriate. The rhythm converted, so a 12 mg dose, atropine and CPR are not indicated.
opts: The pause is an expected transient effect
Flushing and chest pressure are common and brief
Atropine is indicated for the pause
A 12 mg dose should follow now
Obtain a 12-lead ECG and reassess
CPR should begin during the pause
ok: The pause is an expected transient effect
Flushing and chest pressure are common and brief
Obtain a 12-lead ECG and reassess

items.q: A 64-year-old with stable monomorphic VT at 160/min is receiving amiodarone 150 mg IV over 10 minutes. Which findings require stopping the infusion and contacting medical direction? Select all that apply.
items.x: Hypotension and new AV block are stop criteria for amiodarone. Mild nausea is a common side effect, and normal SpO2 and respiratory rate do not require stopping.
opts: BP falls to 76/48 mm Hg
Mild nausea
New second-degree AV block
SpO2 of 97% on room air
Respiratory rate of 16/min
ok: BP falls to 76/48 mm Hg
New second-degree AV block

items.q: A patient with stable monomorphic VT has received repeated lidocaine boluses and is nearing the maximum dose. The patient now reports ringing in the ears and numbness around the mouth and is newly confused. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.
items.x: Tinnitus, perioral numbness and confusion near the 3 mg/kg maximum point to lidocaine toxicity, which can progress to seizures, so further doses are held. These are CNS toxicity signs, not allergy, and confusion is never ignored.
opts: These findings suggest lidocaine toxicity
Another 1-1.5 mg/kg bolus is indicated
Further lidocaine should be held
These are signs of an allergic reaction
Seizure precautions are appropriate
Confusion is expected and can be ignored
ok: These findings suggest lidocaine toxicity
Further lidocaine should be held
Seizure precautions are appropriate

items.q: An alert 58-year-old with severe dehydration has a new proximal tibial IO needle that is stable with no swelling, and he grimaces when the first flush starts. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: In an alert adult, IO infusion pain is treated with lidocaine 40 mg (2 mL of 2%) given slowly, then 20 mg as needed. Pain alone does not mean misplacement when the needle is stable without swelling, and the dehydrated patient still needs fluids. 1-1.5 mg/kg and 3 mg/kg are antiarrhythmic dosing and limits.
opts: Give 2% lidocaine 40 mg slowly, then flush
Remove the IO, since pain means misplacement
Give lidocaine 1-1.5 mg/kg rapid IO push
Skip analgesia, since IO pain is brief
Withhold the fluid bolus to avoid pain
Give lidocaine 3 mg/kg IO push
ok: Give 2% lidocaine 40 mg slowly, then flush

items.q: A 47-year-old has stable monomorphic VT at 170/min and BP 118/72 mm Hg. Procainamide is being considered. Which history findings would contraindicate it? Select all that apply.
items.x: Procainamide is contraindicated with long QT or torsades, myasthenia gravis, SLE and complete heart block. Diabetes, prior surgery, allergies and treated hypertension are not contraindications.
opts: Myasthenia gravis
Type 2 diabetes
Known long QT syndrome
Prior appendectomy
Seasonal allergies
Hypertension on medication
ok: Myasthenia gravis
Known long QT syndrome

items.q: A 61-year-old with an inferior STEMI has sinus bradycardia at 42/min and BP 82/56 mm Hg. After atropine 1 mg IV, the heart rate rises to 130/min and chest pain worsens with new ST changes. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.
items.x: Atropine can cause tachycardia that worsens ischemia, which is a stop criterion, so further doses are held and the change is reported. This is a sinus tachycardia from atropine, so adenosine and more atropine are wrong.
opts: Atropine-induced tachycardia can worsen ischemia
The response shows atropine should be repeated
Further atropine should be withheld
Adenosine should be given for the tachycardia
Report the change to medical direction
Give the remaining 2 mg at once
ok: Atropine-induced tachycardia can worsen ischemia
Further atropine should be withheld
Report the change to medical direction

items.q: A 74-year-old has symptomatic sinus bradycardia at 36/min with hypotension and confusion. Two 1 mg doses of atropine produced only a brief response. Which next steps are consistent with ACLS? Select all that apply.
items.x: Atropine 1 mg may be repeated to a 3 mg total, and pacing or a dopamine or epinephrine infusion are the next options when atropine is not effective. A 3 mg repeat would exceed the maximum, and adenosine slows AV conduction further.
opts: A third 1 mg atropine dose
Transcutaneous pacing
Atropine 3 mg as a single repeat dose
Dopamine infusion 5-20 mcg/kg/min
Epinephrine infusion 2-10 mcg/min
Adenosine 6 mg rapid IV push
ok: A third 1 mg atropine dose
Transcutaneous pacing
Dopamine infusion 5-20 mcg/kg/min
Epinephrine infusion 2-10 mcg/min

items.q: A 78-year-old has sinus bradycardia at 34/min, BP 70/40 mm Hg and confusion. Atropine did not help, transcutaneous pacing is not capturing, and an epinephrine infusion is ordered. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: The bradycardia infusion runs 2-10 mcg/min (up to 20), titrated to HR, BP and mental status with continuous monitoring for chest pain and dysrhythmias. 1 mg IV push is the arrest dose and 0.3 mg IM is the anaphylaxis dose.
opts: Run the infusion at 2-10 mcg/min, titrated
Give 1 mg IV push every 3-5 minutes
Recheck BP, HR and mentation while titrating
Give 0.3 mg IM in the lateral thigh
Stop cardiac monitoring once HR rises
ok: Run the infusion at 2-10 mcg/min, titrated
Recheck BP, HR and mentation while titrating

items.q: A 70-year-old in septic shock is on a norepinephrine infusion through a forearm IV with a MAP of 66 mm Hg. The skin around the site becomes pale, cool and swollen. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Extravasated norepinephrine causes tissue ischemia, so it is stopped at that site (aspirate, and consider phentolamine with medical direction) and the pressor continues through new access so the MAP is not lost. Increasing the rate, massaging or flushing pushes more drug into the tissue.
opts: Stop the infusion at that site
Increase the rate to protect the MAP
Massage the area to spread the drug
Continue the pressor through a new, patent line
Flush the site with a saline bolus
ok: Stop the infusion at that site
Continue the pressor through a new, patent line

items.q: A 66-year-old with chest pain had BP 140/86 mm Hg before a first 0.4 mg SL nitroglycerin. Five minutes later BP is 104/70 mm Hg and pain has decreased from 8 to 6. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: A drop of 30 mm Hg or more from baseline is a stop point for nitroglycerin even when SBP stays above 90. Doubling, stacking doses or standing the patient increases the risk of hypotension and syncope.
opts: Withhold the next nitroglycerin dose
Give the next dose since SBP is over 90
Reassess BP and report the drop
Double the next dose to 0.8 mg
Have the patient stand to recheck BP
Give two doses back to back
ok: Withhold the next nitroglycerin dose
Reassess BP and report the drop

items.q: A 72-year-old with sudden severe dyspnea has BP 214/122 mm Hg, RR 34/min, SpO2 84%, crackles in all lung fields and no PDE-5 inhibitor use. Which interventions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Hypertensive pulmonary edema is treated with high-dose nitroglycerin (SCAPE protocol), CPAP and upright positioning. Fluids worsen congestion, and labetalol and metoprolol are contraindicated in overt or decompensated heart failure.
opts: High-dose SL nitroglycerin per protocol
A 1 L normal saline bolus
CPAP
IV labetalol for the blood pressure
Sitting the patient upright
IV metoprolol for the blood pressure
ok: High-dose SL nitroglycerin per protocol
CPAP
Sitting the patient upright

items.q: A 68-year-old on hemodialysis who makes no urine has missed two sessions and has crackles, SpO2 86%, BP 188/100 mm Hg and no PDE-5 inhibitor use. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Anuria contraindicates furosemide, so fluid overload in a dialysis patient is managed with CPAP, nitroglycerin and upright positioning, with transport for dialysis. A saline bolus worsens congestion and lying flat worsens dyspnea.
opts: Apply CPAP
Give furosemide IV
Give SL nitroglycerin per protocol
Give a saline bolus
Lay the patient flat for transport
ok: Apply CPAP
Give SL nitroglycerin per protocol

items.q: A 70 kg 63-year-old has atrial fibrillation with RVR at 158/min, BP 132/84 mm Hg and no signs of heart failure. IV diltiazem is ordered. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.
items.x: Diltiazem is given at 0.25 mg/kg over 2 minutes, then 0.35 mg/kg after 15 minutes if needed, watching for hypotension and bradycardia. Rapid push is the adenosine technique, and a recent IV beta blocker contraindicates diltiazem.
opts: Initial dose is 0.25 mg/kg IV over 2 minutes
Give it as a rapid push over 1-2 seconds
A 0.35 mg/kg dose may follow in 15 minutes
Repeat the first dose every 2 minutes
Monitor closely for hypotension and bradycardia
Add IV metoprolol for faster control
ok: Initial dose is 0.25 mg/kg IV over 2 minutes
A 0.35 mg/kg dose may follow in 15 minutes
Monitor closely for hypotension and bradycardia

items.q: A 58-year-old has BP 238/132 mm Hg with a severe headache and confusion, and medical direction asks whether IV labetalol can be given. Which assessment findings would contraindicate it? Select all that apply.
items.x: Labetalol is contraindicated with reactive airway disease, severe bradycardia, second- or third-degree block and overt heart failure, so these findings are reported before it is given. Diabetes and prior stroke are not contraindications.
opts: Wheezing in a patient with asthma
Heart rate of 46/min on the monitor
Type 2 diabetes in the history
Second-degree AV block on the ECG
Crackles and JVD from overt heart failure
Prior ischemic stroke in the history
ok: Wheezing in a patient with asthma
Heart rate of 46/min on the monitor
Second-degree AV block on the ECG
Crackles and JVD from overt heart failure

items.q: A 56-year-old taking a QT-prolonging drug has recurrent runs of polymorphic VT with a long QT between runs and BP 102/64 mm Hg. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Torsades with a pulse is treated with magnesium 1-2 g over 5-15 minutes while watching for hypotension and bradycardia. Procainamide is contraindicated with long QT, adenosine with polymorphic tachycardia, and 4-6 g is the eclampsia dose.
opts: Magnesium 1-2 g IV over 5-15 min
Procainamide 20-50 mg/min
Adenosine 6 mg rapid IV push
Monitor for hypotension and bradycardia
Magnesium 4-6 g IV over 15-20 min
ok: Magnesium 1-2 g IV over 5-15 min
Monitor for hypotension and bradycardia

items.q: A 54-year-old is in PEA with high-quality CPR in progress, an IV established and a supraglottic airway in place. Which actions are indicated now? Select all that apply.
items.x: PEA is nonshockable, so care is CPR with epinephrine every 3-5 minutes while searching for reversible causes. Shocks and amiodarone are for VF or pulseless VT, pulse checks take no more than 10 seconds, atropine is no longer recommended in PEA, and adenosine is for perfusing SVT.
opts: Epinephrine 1 mg IV every 3-5 min
Defibrillate at the highest energy
Amiodarone 300 mg IV push
Pause CPR 30 seconds for a pulse check
Atropine 1 mg IV for the slow rate
Adenosine 6 mg rapid IV push
ok: Epinephrine 1 mg IV every 3-5 min

items.q: After ROSC from a VF arrest, an intubated 60-year-old has BP 72/40 mm Hg and sinus tachycardia at 112/min. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Post-ROSC hypotension is treated with a vasopressor infusion, along with a 12-lead to look for STEMI and titrated oxygen. Arrest-dose epinephrine stops at ROSC, hyperventilation is harmful, and 300 mg amiodarone push is the arrest dose.
opts: Start a vasopressor infusion per protocol
Continue epinephrine 1 mg every 3-5 min
Obtain a 12-lead ECG
Ventilate as fast as possible
Titrate oxygen to avoid hypoxia
Give amiodarone 300 mg IV push
ok: Start a vasopressor infusion per protocol
Obtain a 12-lead ECG
Titrate oxygen to avoid hypoxia

items.q: During RSI, a patient has brief jerking of the limbs seconds after etomidate 0.3 mg/kg, before the paralytic is given. SpO2 is 98% and BP 132/80 mm Hg. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Myoclonus is a common, harmless effect of etomidate, so the RSI continues. There are no signs of seizure, anaphylaxis or malignant hyperthermia, and an induced patient should not be left without a secured airway while waiting to wake.
opts: Give the paralytic and continue the RSI
Abort RSI and treat a seizure with midazolam
Give IM epinephrine for anaphylaxis
Start cooling for malignant hyperthermia
Stop and wait for the patient to wake up
ok: Give the paralytic and continue the RSI

items.q: Ketamine is given IV for sedation before splinting a painful open fracture. Minutes later the patient has high-pitched inspiratory stridor, poor chest rise and falling SpO2. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Laryngospasm is a serious ketamine effect, treated with airway positioning and positive-pressure ventilation, and succinylcholine if it persists. More ketamine can worsen it, naloxone does not reverse ketamine, and albuterol does not relieve laryngospasm.
opts: Recognize probable laryngospasm
Jaw thrust and BVM with positive pressure
Give additional ketamine
Give naloxone to reverse ketamine
Prepare succinylcholine per protocol if it persists
Give nebulized albuterol for the stridor
ok: Recognize probable laryngospasm
Jaw thrust and BVM with positive pressure
Prepare succinylcholine per protocol if it persists

items.q: A 40-year-old burned over 35% of the body 4 days ago now needs RSI for worsening respiratory failure during an interfacility transfer. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.
items.x: After burns, succinylcholine can cause dangerous hyperkalemia from about 24 hours after the injury, with risk peaking around 7-10 days, so rocuronium is preferred. Preoxygenation, suction and waveform capnography apply to every RSI, and a short duration does not offset the hyperkalemia risk.
opts: Succinylcholine now risks severe hyperkalemia
Rocuronium is the safer paralytic choice
Preoxygenate and have suction ready
Confirm the tube with waveform capnography
Burn-related risk begins only after 72 hours
Succinylcholine is safest since it is short acting
ok: Succinylcholine now risks severe hyperkalemia
Rocuronium is the safer paralytic choice
Preoxygenate and have suction ready
Confirm the tube with waveform capnography

items.q: Ten minutes after RSI with etomidate and rocuronium 1.2 mg/kg, the patient's HR rises from 92 to 128/min, BP from 124/78 to 172/100 mm Hg, and tears run from the eyes. No other sedation has been given. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Etomidate wears off long before rocuronium, so tachycardia, hypertension and tearing suggest awareness under paralysis and need sedation and analgesia. More paralytic, naloxone or doing nothing leaves the patient paralyzed and aware.
opts: Give sedation and analgesia per protocol
Give more rocuronium only
No action, since the patient cannot move
Give naloxone
Give a dose of succinylcholine
ok: Give sedation and analgesia per protocol

items.q: An 80 kg adult with a shoulder dislocation received fentanyl 80 mcg IV. Ten minutes later pain is 6/10, RR 16/min, BP 122/76 mm Hg, SpO2 97%, and the patient is alert. Which actions are consistent with protocol? Select all that apply.
items.x: Fentanyl may be repeated at 0.5-1 mcg/kg every 5-10 minutes with ongoing monitoring when vitals are stable. An RR of 16 is normal, naloxone is not given prophylactically, and stacking IM morphine adds risk.
opts: Repeat 0.5-1 mcg/kg if pain persists
Withhold all doses due to the RR
Keep monitoring RR, SpO2 and sedation
Give naloxone to prevent depression
Add morphine 10 mg IM now
ok: Repeat 0.5-1 mcg/kg if pain persists
Keep monitoring RR, SpO2 and sedation

items.q: A 70-year-old received IV fentanyl for hip fracture pain and is now difficult to arouse with RR 8/min and SpO2 87%. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: RR under 10-12, falling SpO2 and oversedation are stop points; ventilation is supported and naloxone is used per protocol. Further opioid by any route is wrong, and an antiemetic does nothing for respiratory depression.
opts: Stop further fentanyl
Apply a nasal cannula and give the next dose
Assist ventilations with a BVM
Give naloxone per protocol
Give ondansetron
Give the remaining dose IM instead
ok: Stop further fentanyl
Assist ventilations with a BVM
Give naloxone per protocol

items.q: Ten minutes after IV morphine for a femur fracture, a patient reports itching and flushing of the face and chest. BP is 128/80 mm Hg, RR 16/min, lungs are clear and there is no swelling. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.
items.x: Itching and flushing are common morphine effects from histamine release, and stable vitals with clear lungs do not suggest anaphylaxis. Naloxone would reverse the analgesia, and these effects do not bar future opioid use.
opts: Itching and flushing are common with morphine
This is anaphylaxis needing IM epinephrine
Keep reassessing airway, BP and skin
Naloxone is needed to reverse the itching
Opioids may never be given to this patient again
ok: Itching and flushing are common with morphine
Keep reassessing airway, BP and skin

items.q: A 50-year-old with a closed humerus fracture has severe pain, HR 104/min, BP 142/88 mm Hg, RR 18/min, SpO2 98% and an IV in place. Medical direction orders hydromorphone. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: EMS hydromorphone doses are usually 0.5-1 mg IV, followed by reassessment of pain, RR and sedation. It is far more potent than morphine, so morphine-range or oral doses given IV risk respiratory depression; splinting is part of pain control, and monitoring continues.
opts: Give 0.5 mg IV slowly, then reassess pain and RR
Give 10 mg IV push, as with morphine
Give the 2-4 mg oral dose IV
Splint only after the pain is fully gone
Remove SpO2 monitoring since vitals are normal
ok: Give 0.5 mg IV slowly, then reassess pain and RR

items.q: A 72-year-old with normal renal function and no bleeding risk has acute low back pain, and a single dose of ketorolac is ordered. Which orders are consistent with the label? Select all that apply.
items.x: For patients 65 or older the single dose is 15 mg IV or 30 mg IM. The 30 mg IV and 60 mg IM doses are for patients under 65, and 120 mg is the daily maximum for younger adults.
opts: 15 mg IV
30 mg IV
30 mg IM
60 mg IM
120 mg IV
ok: 15 mg IV
30 mg IM

items.q: A paramedic is considering oral ibuprofen for musculoskeletal pain. In which patients is it contraindicated? Select all that apply.
items.x: Ibuprofen is contraindicated with aspirin or NSAID-induced asthma, third-trimester pregnancy, severe renal impairment and active GI bleeding. A healthy patient with a sprain or headache has none of these.
opts: Asthma that worsens after aspirin
Ankle sprain and no medical history
Third-trimester pregnancy
Severe kidney disease
Black, tarry stools today
Tension headache and no history
ok: Asthma that worsens after aspirin
Third-trimester pregnancy
Severe kidney disease
Black, tarry stools today

items.q: A 30-year-old with an acute asthma exacerbation is speaking in short phrases, with wheezing, RR 28/min and SpO2 91%. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Albuterol 2.5 mg every 20 minutes x3, upright positioning and reassessment after each treatment are standard. Albuterol is not given IM (0.3 mg IM is an epinephrine dose), hypoxic asthmatics need oxygen, and sedatives can precipitate respiratory failure.
opts: Albuterol 2.5 mg neb every 20 min x3
Sit the patient upright
Albuterol 0.3 mg IM in the thigh
Reassess breath sounds and SpO2 after each neb
Withhold oxygen to protect respiratory drive
Give midazolam for the anxiety
ok: Albuterol 2.5 mg neb every 20 min x3
Sit the patient upright
Reassess breath sounds and SpO2 after each neb

items.q: Ipratropium is being added to albuterol for a 70-year-old with a COPD exacerbation. Which findings would lead the paramedic to withhold ipratropium? Select all that apply.
items.x: Hypersensitivity to ipratropium, atropine or their derivatives contraindicates it. Ipratropium is meant to be combined with albuterol in COPD, and mild tachycardia, cough and age are not contraindications.
opts: Prior allergic reaction to atropine
Current albuterol use
Heart rate of 108/min
History of COPD
Productive cough
Age over 65
ok: Prior allergic reaction to atropine

items.q: A 34-year-old with severe asthma is too dyspneic to use a nebulizer effectively and is tiring, with HR 118/min and SpO2 88% on oxygen. SQ terbutaline is ordered. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Terbutaline is 0.25 mg SQ in the lateral deltoid (one repeat in 15-30 minutes, max 0.5 mg in 4 hours) and causes tachycardia and palpitations, so HR, rhythm and breathing are reassessed. It is not pushed IV or repeated every 5 minutes, and a tiring patient is ventilated without delay.
opts: Give 0.25 mg SQ in the lateral deltoid
Give 0.25 mg IV push over 1 minute
Watch HR, rhythm and work of breathing
Repeat every 5 minutes until wheezing clears
Delay BVM assist until terbutaline works
ok: Give 0.25 mg SQ in the lateral deltoid
Watch HR, rhythm and work of breathing

items.q: A 66-year-old with a COPD exacerbation has improved only partly after albuterol and ipratropium, with mild wheezing and SpO2 87%. Dexamethasone is given per protocol. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Corticosteroids reduce airway inflammation over hours, so bronchodilators continue, and COPD patients are titrated to 88-92% rather than denied oxygen. Dexamethasone is given IV, IM, IO or PO, not nebulized; blood glucose may rise.
opts: Continue bronchodilators after the dose
Expect wheezing to resolve within minutes
Titrate oxygen to an SpO2 of 88-92%
Give it by nebulizer for faster effect
Remove oxygen because of CO2 retention
ok: Continue bronchodilators after the dose
Titrate oxygen to an SpO2 of 88-92%

items.q: An adult with inspiratory stridor from upper-airway swelling after a neck infection receives racemic epinephrine 0.5 mL of 2.25% in 3 mL NS by nebulizer. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Racemic epinephrine is nebulized only and can cause tachycardia and dysrhythmias. Its effect can wear off, so monitoring continues and an airway plan is kept ready; a patient with airway swelling is kept upright, not laid flat.
opts: Monitor for tachycardia and dysrhythmias
Lay the patient flat to reduce effort
Keep an airway plan ready if stridor returns
Stop monitoring once the stridor eases
Give the dose IM if the nebulizer is slow
ok: Monitor for tachycardia and dysrhythmias
Keep an airway plan ready if stridor returns

items.q: A septic 64-year-old needs RSI for respiratory failure, and BP is 78/46 mm Hg. Which actions are appropriate before induction? Select all that apply.
items.x: Hypotension should be corrected before induction, the patient fully preoxygenated, and push-dose epinephrine kept ready for post-induction hypotension. The induction agent is given before the paralytic, and midazolam is relatively contraindicated in shock.
opts: Resuscitate BP before induction when possible
Skip preoxygenation to save time
Preoxygenate as fully as possible
Give the paralytic before the induction agent
Have push-dose epinephrine 10-20 mcg ready
Use a large midazolam dose for induction
ok: Resuscitate BP before induction when possible
Preoxygenate as fully as possible
Have push-dose epinephrine 10-20 mcg ready

items.q: An intubated patient being ventilated with a BVM suddenly desaturates during transport. Which causes should the paramedic assess for? Select all that apply.
items.x: Sudden deterioration in an intubated patient is assessed with DOPE: displacement, obstruction, pneumothorax and equipment failure. Hypoglycemia and deep sedation do not cause acute desaturation in a ventilated patient.
opts: Tube displacement
Tube obstruction
Pneumothorax
Hypoglycemia
Equipment failure
Excess sedation
ok: Tube displacement
Tube obstruction
Pneumothorax
Equipment failure

items.q: Vecuronium is used to maintain paralysis in an intubated patient during a long interfacility transport. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.
items.x: Vecuronium paralyzes without sedating, so ongoing sedation and continuous capnography are required. Its onset is slower than succinylcholine, naloxone does not reverse it, and no paralytic is given without an airway plan.
opts: It provides no sedation or analgesia
Its onset is faster than succinylcholine
Ongoing sedation must be given
Naloxone reverses its effect
Monitor tube position with waveform capnography
It is preferred when no airway plan exists
ok: It provides no sedation or analgesia
Ongoing sedation must be given
Monitor tube position with waveform capnography

items.q: A 57-year-old has 30 minutes of crushing chest pain, BP 148/90 mm Hg, HR 88/min, SpO2 97%, and no allergies, bleeding or PDE-5 inhibitor use. Which medications are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Aspirin, nitroglycerin and an opioid for pain unrelieved by nitroglycerin fit suspected ACS with a normal BP. NSAIDs such as ketorolac and ibuprofen are avoided in ACS, and diltiazem is for rate control of atrial fibrillation.
opts: Aspirin 162-324 mg chewed
Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL
Ketorolac 15 mg IV for the pain
Fentanyl if pain persists after nitroglycerin
Ibuprofen 400 mg PO
Diltiazem 0.25 mg/kg IV
ok: Aspirin 162-324 mg chewed
Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL
Fentanyl if pain persists after nitroglycerin

items.q: A 63-year-old with an inferior STEMI has ST elevation in V4R, BP 96/62 mm Hg and clear lungs. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Right ventricular infarction is preload dependent, so nitroglycerin and furosemide are avoided and fluids are considered, while aspirin and PCI-capable transport still apply. Metoprolol is contraindicated in acute MI with SBP under 100.
opts: Give aspirin if no contraindication
Give nitroglycerin SL
Consider a fluid bolus per protocol
Give furosemide
Give IV metoprolol
Transport to a PCI-capable center
ok: Give aspirin if no contraindication
Consider a fluid bolus per protocol
Transport to a PCI-capable center

items.q: A 55-year-old has a regular, monomorphic wide-complex tachycardia at 165/min, BP 124/80 mm Hg, and is alert without chest pain. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Stable monomorphic VT calls for a 12-lead, an antiarrhythmic such as amiodarone 150 mg over 10 minutes, and pads in place in case synchronized cardioversion becomes necessary. Diltiazem is contraindicated in wide-complex tachycardia of unknown origin, atropine is for bradycardia, and 4-6 g magnesium is the eclampsia dose.
opts: Obtain a 12-lead ECG
Amiodarone 150 mg IV over 10 min
Diltiazem 0.25 mg/kg IV
Apply pads in case cardioversion is needed
Atropine 1 mg IV
Magnesium 4-6 g IV over 15-20 min
ok: Obtain a 12-lead ECG
Amiodarone 150 mg IV over 10 min
Apply pads in case cardioversion is needed

items.q: A 68-year-old with an anterior STEMI is cool and clammy with BP 74/48 mm Hg, sinus tachycardia at 108/min and crackles in both lungs. Which treatments are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Cardiogenic shock needs vasopressor support. Metoprolol and amiodarone are contraindicated in cardiogenic shock, and nitroglycerin and furosemide are withheld with this degree of hypotension.
opts: Vasopressor infusion per protocol
IV metoprolol
IV furosemide
Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL
Amiodarone 150 mg IV over 10 min
ok: Vasopressor infusion per protocol

items.q: CPAP is being considered for a patient in respiratory distress. Which findings contraindicate CPAP? Select all that apply.
items.x: CPAP needs a patient who can protect the airway and is contraindicated with vomiting, pneumothorax and hypotension. Wheezing with accessory muscle use and pulmonary edema with hypoxia are indications.
opts: Unresponsive and unable to protect the airway
Active vomiting
Wheezing and accessory muscle use
Suspected pneumothorax
Systolic BP of 78 mm Hg
Crackles with SpO2 of 86%
ok: Unresponsive and unable to protect the airway
Active vomiting
Suspected pneumothorax
Systolic BP of 78 mm Hg

items.q: An intubated patient with status asthmaticus is being ventilated rapidly with a BVM. BP falls and the bag becomes hard to squeeze. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Rapid ventilation in asthma causes air trapping (auto-PEEP) that lowers venous return; disconnecting briefly and slowing the rate let the lungs empty. A faster rate worsens trapping, and furosemide and rocuronium do not treat the cause.
opts: Briefly disconnect the bag to allow full exhalation
Increase the ventilation rate
Slow the rate to allow longer exhalation
Give furosemide for fluid overload
Give rocuronium to treat the hypotension
ok: Briefly disconnect the bag to allow full exhalation
Slow the rate to allow longer exhalation

items.q: After RSI with rocuronium, two intubation attempts fail and SpO2 falls to 84%. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: After failed attempts the priority is oxygenation: BVM with adjuncts, a supraglottic airway, help, and a surgical airway if oxygenation still fails. Rocuronium lasts too long to wait out, and repeated attempts without ventilation worsen hypoxia.
opts: BVM ventilation with an oral airway
Place a supraglottic airway
Wait for rocuronium to wear off without ventilating
Prepare for cricothyrotomy if unable to oxygenate
Keep attempting intubation without ventilating
Call for additional help
ok: BVM ventilation with an oral airway
Place a supraglottic airway
Prepare for cricothyrotomy if unable to oxygenate
Call for additional help

items.q: A 61-year-old with chest pressure and suspected ACS took one 81 mg enteric-coated aspirin at home 30 minutes ago and has no allergies or bleeding. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: A single enteric-coated 81 mg tablet is slowly absorbed and below the ACS dose, so 162-324 mg of chewed, non-enteric-coated aspirin is given along with an early 12-lead. Aspirin is not delayed for STEMI on the ECG or for nitroglycerin to fail.
opts: Give 162-324 mg of non-enteric-coated aspirin
Obtain a 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes
Have the patient chew the tablets
Withhold aspirin because one was taken
Wait until the 12-lead shows STEMI
Give aspirin only if nitroglycerin fails
ok: Give 162-324 mg of non-enteric-coated aspirin
Obtain a 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes
Have the patient chew the tablets

items.q: A 28-year-old is found next to a syringe with a respiratory rate of 4/min, SpO2 82%, pinpoint pupils and a weak radial pulse. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Ventilation comes first, and naloxone is titrated to respiratory effort (starting at 0.04-0.4 mg IV in opioid-dependent patients) to avoid precipitating severe withdrawal; full awakening is not the goal. Intubation is not required before naloxone, and charcoal has no role for an injected drug in a patient who cannot protect the airway.
opts: Ventilate with a BVM and oxygen
Push naloxone until the patient is fully awake
Titrate IV naloxone to adequate breathing
Delay naloxone until the patient is intubated
Start with a small IV dose if dependence is likely
Give activated charcoal for the injected drug
ok: Ventilate with a BVM and oxygen
Titrate IV naloxone to adequate breathing
Start with a small IV dose if dependence is likely

items.q: A 16 kg 4-year-old swallowed several of a relative's oxycodone tablets and now responds only to pain with a respiratory rate of 6/min. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.
items.x: The PALS full-reversal dose is 0.1 mg/kg (max 2 mg) by IV, IO, IM or IN, so 1.6 mg is appropriate, and ventilation is supported meanwhile. A long-acting opioid can outlast naloxone, so recurrence is watched for; charcoal is contraindicated with decreased mental status.
opts: Pediatric naloxone is capped far below the adult dose
Assist ventilations with a BVM while preparing naloxone
Intranasal naloxone cannot be used in children
A weight-based full-reversal dose is within the maximum
Give activated charcoal before naloxone
Respiratory depression may recur as naloxone wears off
ok: Assist ventilations with a BVM while preparing naloxone
A weight-based full-reversal dose is within the maximum
Respiratory depression may recur as naloxone wears off

items.q: An alert adult who took an overdose of an adsorbable drug 30 minutes ago is drinking activated charcoal. Which findings should cause the paramedic to stop giving it? Select all that apply.
items.x: A falling level of consciousness means the airway may not be protected, creating aspiration risk, so charcoal is stopped. An unpleasant taste, mild nausea without vomiting, a normal heart rate and a covered cup are not reasons to stop.
opts: Complaints about the gritty taste
Heart rate of 92/min
Decreasing level of consciousness
Mild nausea without vomiting
Asking for a covered cup and straw
ok: Decreasing level of consciousness

items.q: A 30-year-old who took a large amitriptyline overdose is intubated after a seizure. QRS is 150 ms, BP 86/50 mm Hg and ETCO2 has risen to 58 mm Hg with slow bagging. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Bicarbonate 1-2 mEq/kg, repeated until the QRS narrows, treats TCA sodium-channel toxicity, and because it generates CO2, inadequate ventilation must be corrected. Procainamide is a sodium-channel blocker that worsens TCA toxicity, and treatment is not delayed for a blood gas.
opts: Give sodium bicarbonate 1-2 mEq/kg IV
Increase ventilation to lower the ETCO2
Give procainamide for the wide QRS
Wait for a blood gas before any bicarbonate
Slow the bagging further to limit pressure
ok: Give sodium bicarbonate 1-2 mEq/kg IV
Increase ventilation to lower the ETCO2

items.q: During a nerve agent incident, a decontaminated patient has seizures, copious secretions, severe respiratory distress and SpO2 82%. DuoDote auto-injectors are available. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Severe exposure is treated with three DuoDote injections (600 mg pralidoxime plus 2.1 mg atropine each, IM) in rapid succession, with suction and ventilation. Atropine and pralidoxime do not stop seizures, so a benzodiazepine is also given; seizures are not a contraindication.
opts: Give three auto-injectors IM in rapid succession
Give one injector, then wait 1 hour
Suction and support ventilation with a BVM
Inject the auto-injectors IV
Give a benzodiazepine for the seizures
Withhold the auto-injectors during seizures
ok: Give three auto-injectors IM in rapid succession
Suction and support ventilation with a BVM
Give a benzodiazepine for the seizures

items.q: A patient with organophosphate poisoning has received large, repeated doses of atropine and the secretions are now dry. Which new findings suggest atropine toxicity? Select all that apply.
items.x: Delirium and hyperthermia are serious anticholinergic effects of atropine excess. Bronchorrhea, miosis, diarrhea and bradycardia are cholinergic signs of the poisoning itself, not of too much atropine.
opts: Bronchorrhea
Hyperthermia
Miosis
Delirium
Diarrhea
Bradycardia
ok: Hyperthermia
Delirium

items.q: A 30 kg child carried from a smoke-filled apartment bedroom is unresponsive with BP 64/40 mm Hg, and cyanide toxicity is suspected. SpO2 reads 99% on oxygen. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: The pediatric dose is 70 mg/kg IV (max 5 g) over 15 minutes, 2.1 g for 30 kg; it is not given IM or by rapid push. Pulse oximetry cannot exclude carbon monoxide poisoning, so high-flow oxygen continues alongside the antidote.
opts: Give the adult 5 g dose as a rapid IV push
Give hydroxocobalamin 2.1 g IM in the thigh
Give hydroxocobalamin 2.1 g IV over 15 minutes
Use the 99% SpO2 to rule out CO poisoning
Stop oxygen once the antidote is running
ok: Give hydroxocobalamin 2.1 g IV over 15 minutes

items.q: Which of these patients are candidates for hydroxocobalamin? Select all that apply.
items.x: Hydroxocobalamin treats known or suspected cyanide poisoning, likely after smoke in an enclosed space with coma and hypotension, or after direct cyanide exposure with seizures. An alert outdoor smoke exposure, organophosphate ingestion and opioid overdose have other treatments.
opts: Closed-room fire victim, unresponsive and hypotensive
Outdoor brush fire victim, alert with a mild cough
Farmworker who swallowed an organophosphate
Lab worker exposed to cyanide salts, now seizing
Opioid overdose with pinpoint pupils
ok: Closed-room fire victim, unresponsive and hypotensive
Lab worker exposed to cyanide salts, now seizing

items.q: A 52-year-old with insulin-treated diabetes is confused and combative with a blood glucose of 41 mg/dL, and two IV attempts have failed. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Glucagon 1 mg IM is the adult dose when IV access fails, and once the patient is awake, oral carbohydrate helps prevent recurrence. Oral glucose is unsafe without airway protection, treatment is not delayed for IV access, and 3 mg is the intranasal dose.
opts: Give glucagon 1 mg IM
Give oral glucose gel while she cannot follow commands
Offer food by mouth once awake and able to swallow
Keep trying for IV access before any glucose
Give glucagon 3 mg IM
ok: Give glucagon 1 mg IM
Offer food by mouth once awake and able to swallow

items.q: A 15 kg 4-year-old with type 1 diabetes is unresponsive with a blood glucose of 30 mg/dL, and IV/IO access is delayed. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Children under 20-25 kg receive 0.5 mg IM, and 3 mg IN is labeled from age 4; nausea and vomiting are common, and a glucose that does not rise within 15 minutes is reported. Oral glucose is contraindicated without airway protection, and 1 mg/kg is a large overdose.
opts: Give glucagon 0.5 mg IM
Give oral glucose gel while unresponsive
Use intranasal glucagon 3 mg as an option
Anticipate vomiting as the child wakes
Give glucagon 1 mg/kg IM
Recheck glucose if no response in 15 minutes
ok: Give glucagon 0.5 mg IM
Use intranasal glucagon 3 mg as an option
Anticipate vomiting as the child wakes
Recheck glucose if no response in 15 minutes

items.q: A 10 kg 1-year-old is limp, responds only to pain, and has a blood glucose of 32 mg/dL. An IV is in place. Which orders and actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.x: Infants and children receive D10 5-10 mL/kg (50-100 mL here), followed by a glucose recheck. D50 25 mL (12.5 g) exceeds 0.5-1 g/kg, 250 mL is the adult dose, and oral gel is unsafe in a child who cannot protect the airway.

D50 25 mL IV push
D10 100 mL IV
D10 250 mL IV
Oral glucose gel in the cheek
Recheck the glucose after the dose

D10 100 mL IV
